# Analysis

## Summary

`rebase-plan-guard` makes `tws sync` **state what it is about to replay, onto what, from which
cutoff — before it rewrites any local branch, worktree, or piece of tws state** — and gives the
operator a deterministic way to stop a run whose plan is broader or less determinate than expected.

### 0.1 Mutation vocabulary (binding for this whole document)

"Read-only" is **not** an accurate description of every plan invocation, and this analysis does not
use it as one. The precise contract is:

- A `--plan` invocation performs **no worktree mutation, no local-branch rewrite, no `stack.yaml`
  write, and no runtime-state write** — no `.sync-state.yaml`, no `.sync-state.v2.yaml`, no
  `.sync-run.lock`, no checkout transaction, no checkout lock, no sentinel, no push.
- **"Mutates nothing" is a scoped claim, and round-35 item 9 binds its scope here so no prose, help
  string, doc, skill or test may state it unqualified.** Wherever this document, its snippets or its
  suites say that an invocation "mutates nothing", the claim is exactly: **HEAD, the index, the
  working tree, `stack.yaml`, every runtime-state/lock/sentinel file, and every `refs/heads/**` ref
  outside the described fetch's own local-branch destinations are byte-identical afterwards**. It is
  **never** a claim about the whole repository. A **fetch-enabled** invocation — `--plan` under an
  effective `fetch` policy, and equally a guarded execution that refuses *after* its fetch — writes
  `refs/remotes/**`, writes that context's own `FETCH_HEAD`, may **delete** remote-tracking refs and
  local tags under an effective prune, may **clobber** tags under a forced covering refspec, and may
  even fast-forward or move `refs/heads/**` where a positive refspec covers them, all as the rest of
  this section specifies (§4.4 `fetch_effect`, `local_branch_destinations`). Only the explicit
  **new-mode `--no-fetch`** route carries the unqualified claim, and there the assertion is the
  strong one: no Git process writes anything at all.
- **`--plan --no-fetch` is fully local and read-only** (and, because `--no-fetch` is a mode trigger,
  it describes the **new-mode** run — §0.2): every Git process it runs is a read
  (`rev-parse`, `rev-list`, `merge-base`, `for-each-ref`, the dirty probes — `status --porcelain`
  for the shipped whole-repo fact and `status --porcelain --untracked-files=no
  --ignore-submodules=all` for the per-row tracked predicate of §5.4.7 — and the single enumeration
  behind the per-row untracked-**presence** fact of §5.4.7,
  `ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z`, which reads path names and never file content. All of
  them run
  with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` exactly as `probeDirty` already does,
  `internal/stack_status.go:326-337`, so not even the index is refreshed on disk).
- **`--plan` under an effective fetch policy of `fetch` runs `git fetch`**, which **mutates
  remote-tracking refs** — `refs/remotes/**` and any fetched tags, which live in the repository's
  **common** directory, plus **`FETCH_HEAD`, which does not**: it is a per-worktree pseudo-ref
  written into that context's own **`$GIT_DIR`** (round-22 item 4 — `FETCH_HEAD` is absent from
  Git's `common_list` in `path.c`, so a linked worktree writes
  `…/.git/worktrees/<wt>/FETCH_HEAD` while its `refs/`, `objects/` and `packed-refs` are shared)
  — **in the
  directories `fetch.repos[]` names, which are not always the repositories the plan is about**,
  *before* the projection is computed. **Those writes include deletions** (round-22 item 2): an
  effective `fetch.prune`/`remote.<name>.prune` removes remote-tracking refs, and
  `fetch.pruneTags`/`remote.<name>.pruneTags` **deletes** local tags under
  `refs/tags/**` that the remote no longer has (§4.4 `fetch.repos[]`). **Round 24 corrects the
  precondition of that tag deletion: `pruneTags` is sufficient, not necessary** (item 3). Pruning
  "doesn't actually care about branches, instead it'll prune local ↔ remote-references as a
  function of the refspec of the remote … Therefore if the refspec for the remote includes e.g.
  `refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*` … it won't be stale remote tracking branches that are deleted, but any
  local tag that doesn't exist on the remote" (`git fetch` manual, PRUNING, verified against Git
  2.55.0) — and `pruneTags` is exactly the shorthand that appends that refspec
  (`builtin/fetch.c` `fetch_one`: `refspec_append(&remote->fetch, TAG_REFSPEC)`, with
  `TAG_REFSPEC` = `"refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*"`, unforced). So **any positive configured fetch
  refspec whose destination pattern covers `refs/tags/**` puts local tags under the prune, with or
  without `pruneTags`**, and `--tags`/`tagOpt` does not ("We only prune based on refspecs specified
  explicitly (via command line or configuration); we don't care whether `--tags` was specified",
  `builtin/fetch.c` `do_fetch`). **What a fetch does not do
  is silently overwrite an existing tag, and round 22's "removes and clobbers" is withdrawn as to
  its second half** (round-23 item 2): "Until Git version 2.20 … any updates to `refs/tags/*` would
  be accepted without `+` in the refspec (or `--force`) … Since Git version 2.20, fetching to update
  `refs/tags/*` works the same way as when pushing. I.e. any updates will be rejected without `+` in
  the refspec (or `--force`)" (`git fetch` manual, `<refspec>`, verified against Git 2.55.0). So an
  **ordinary, unforced** tag update whose value differs is **rejected** — the run prints
  `! [rejected] … (would clobber existing tag)` and the local tag survives — and only a **forced**
  tag refspec (a leading `+`, or a `--force` this feature and the shipped call never pass) clobbers
  one. **"Forced tag refspec" is a coverage predicate, not a literal `refs/tags/` prefix**
  (round-24 item 3): a leading `+` on **any** destination pattern that covers `refs/tags/**`
  clobbers, so the mirror refspec `+refs/*:refs/*` clobbers tags exactly as
  `+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*` does — and, being positive and covering, it also puts tags **and local
  branches** under an effective prune (§4.3, §4.4). Deletion and clobbering are therefore two
  different facts with two different preconditions, and §4.4 publishes them as two members. That is a real
  repository write. It is
  the same write the unguarded run performs, and it is the reason the preview matches the run, but
  it must never be described as "read-only".
- **A bare `git fetch` can also write refs *outside* the directories `fetch.repos[]` names, in
  **submodule** stores, and the document says so rather than implying the listed contexts are the
  run's full reach** (round-23 item 3). `fetch.recurseSubmodules` "controls whether `git fetch` …
  will recursively fetch into populated submodules … **Defaults to on-demand**, or to the value of
  `submodule.recurse` if set" (`git config` manual, verified against Git 2.55.0), and the recursion
  is a real fetch in another repository: it contacts that submodule's own remotes and moves that
  submodule's `refs/remotes/**` and tags, in a store this document's `context_common_dir` does not
  name. **Round 24 corrects how that setting is resolved and what it applies to** (items 1 and 2).
  The manual's "or to the value of `submodule.recurse` if set" reads like a fallback chain, and the
  command does not implement one: `git_fetch_config` (`builtin/fetch.c`, verified against Git
  2.55.0) writes **both** `submodule.recurse` and `fetch.recursesubmodules` into the *same*
  `fetch_config->recurse_submodules` field as the ordered config stream is parsed, so the
  **last occurrence wins across both keys** — a `submodule.recurse` that is read later than a
  `fetch.recurseSubmodules` overrides it, in the same file and across scopes alike (§4.4, §8.6.9).
  And the recursion is **not** gated by submodule *activity*: for a gitlink that is present in the
  index and whose store can be opened, `git fetch` decides purely by the effective mode and the
  per-submodule `submodule.<name>.fetchRecurseSubmodules` (`submodule.c`
  `get_fetch_task_from_index` → `fetch_task_create` → `get_fetch_recurse_config`, which consult no
  `is_submodule_active`), so an **inactive but populated** submodule is fetched under `yes` like any
  other (§4.4, §15.15h4b3 vi-f). **Round 25 corrects the *direction* of that per-submodule
  override, which rounds 23 and 24 had backwards** (item 1): `get_fetch_recurse_config` returns the
  **context** mode immediately whenever one is set at all — `if (spf->command_line_option !=
  RECURSE_SUBMODULES_DEFAULT) return spf->command_line_option;`, and that field carries the value
  `builtin/fetch.c` resolved from `--recurse-submodules` *or* from the last occurrence of
  `fetch.recurseSubmodules`/`submodule.recurse` — so a set context mode **overrides every
  per-submodule value**, and `submodule.<name>.fetchRecurseSubmodules` is consulted **only** where
  no context mode is set at all (repository config first, `.gitmodules` second), before Git's
  `on-demand` default. **Round 26 adds one rung above those two and below the config chain**
  (item 6): the **context-level `[fetch] recurseSubmodules` in `.gitmodules`**, which seeds the same
  `recurse_submodules` variable through `fetch_config_from_gitmodules` (`submodule-config.c`) — so
  it is a context mode too, binds every submodule, and decides only where the config chain sets
  nothing. **Round 28 corrects the *mechanism* behind that precedence, which rounds 26 and 27 had
  inverted, and the correction changes what an *invalid* `.gitmodules` value does** (item 1).
  `cmd_fetch` does not seed from `.gitmodules` and then let the config chain overwrite it: it reads
  the **ordinary config chain first** — `repo_config(the_repository, git_fetch_config, &config)`,
  `builtin/fetch.c`, verified against Git 2.55.0 — then parses `--recurse-submodules`, and only
  afterwards, and only under two guards, consults `.gitmodules` at all:
  `if (config.recurse_submodules != RECURSE_SUBMODULES_OFF)` gates the call, and
  `int *rs = config.recurse_submodules == RECURSE_SUBMODULES_DEFAULT ? &config.recurse_submodules :
  NULL` gates the member. So the file is **not read for this purpose at all** when the chain
  resolved `no`, and its value is **read but never parsed** when the chain resolved `yes`/`on-demand`
  — `gitmodules_fetch_config` guards `parse_fetch_recurse_submodules_arg` behind
  `if (config->recurse_submodules)` (`submodule-config.c`). The net precedence is the one round 26
  stated, and the consequence round 26 could not have stated is this: **an invalid
  `.gitmodules` `[fetch] recurseSubmodules` value is silently ignored wherever any valid context mode
  already resolves from the config chain or the command line, and is a hard fetch-config failure —
  `die("bad fetch.recursesubmodules argument: <value>")`, before any transfer — exactly and only
  where the chain and the command line leave the mode DEFAULT** (§4.2's route-scoped invalid-value
  rule, §4.9 rank 5.07). **That fetch-only reading is right for `fetch.recurseSubmodules` and for
  this `.gitmodules` key, and wrong for `submodule.recurse`** (round-29 item 1): the two
  `fetch.recurseSubmodules` spellings are read by `git fetch` alone, while `submodule.recurse` is
  read — and fatally parsed as a boolean — by `git checkout` and `git push` too, so its invalidity
  blocks routes this bullet's fetch model never touches (§4.2 Part 2). Nothing about the *fetch*
  resolution above changes: within a fetch, the two keys remain one field resolved by last
  occurrence. The two `.gitmodules` rungs are also consumed at **two different moments
  through two different reads**: the context-level rung 2 in `cmd_fetch`, before the walk, through
  `config_from_gitmodules(gitmodules_fetch_config, …)`; every per-submodule
  `submodule.<name>.fetchRecurseSubmodules` of rung 4 later, during the walk, through
  `repo_read_gitmodules` → `gitmodules_cb` → the submodule-config cache. The exact five-rung ladder,
  its `mode_source`/`effective_mode_source` enums, its `.gitmodules` probe (**Git's own three-source
  ladder, corrected in round 27, item 2: the working-tree file if it exists — so an uncommitted edit
  counts — else the index blob `:.gitmodules`, else `HEAD:.gitmodules`, and nothing at all in a bare
  context, exactly as `config_from_gitmodules` does, `submodule-config.c`**) and its fixtures are in
  §4.4, §13 and §15.15h4b3. **Round 28 also corrects what an *unmerged* `.gitmodules` index entry
  does** (item 1): `is_gitmodules_unmerged` guards `repo_read_gitmodules` — the **per-submodule**
  read — and not `config_from_gitmodules`, so on the context-level path there is no unmerged gate at
  all, and where the working-tree file is absent `repo_get_oid(repo, ":.gitmodules")` simply **fails**
  on an unmerged path and the `||` falls through to `HEAD:.gitmodules`. The ladder is therefore
  **worktree file → index-read failure → `HEAD` blob → nothing**, and an unmerged index entry
  resolves rather than making the mode unknown; round 26's "unmerged is the fail-closed arm" is
  **withdrawn** (§4.4, §4.9 rank 5.05). **No sentence in this document, the flag help, the docs or the skills may say the fetch
  reaches "only the selected repositories" or "only the top-level contexts"** — the honest statement
  is "the contexts listed in `fetch.repos[]`, which may include the process cwd, plus any submodule
  store `fetch_effect.submodule_recursion` names or declares unbounded" (§4.4, §8.6.9, §11, §14).
- **A fetch can move *local branches*, not only remote-tracking refs** (round-23 item 5). A remote
  configured in the legacy `$GIT_DIR/branches/<name>` file — which Git still reads, `remote.c`
  `remotes_remote_get_1` → `read_branches_file`, verified against Git 2.55.0 — carries the
  synthesised fetch refspec `refs/heads/<branch>:refs/heads/<name>`, whose destination is a **local
  branch** in `refs/heads/**`, not `refs/remotes/**`. It is unforced, so it can only fast-forward
  (`git fetch` manual: updates to `refs/{tags,heads}/*` follow the push rules), but a fast-forward
  of a local branch under a rebase preview is exactly the class of movement this feature exists to
  disclose, so §4.4 publishes such a remote's refspecs like any other and §4.3's collateral bound is
  read against them. **Two non-contractual notes about those files, added by round 24 (item 6) and
  deliberately not schema members**: reading either one makes Git print
  `warning: reading remote from "<remotes|branches>/<name>", which is nominated for removal`
  (`remote.c` `warn_about_deprecated_remote_type`, called from `read_remotes_file` and
  `read_branches_file`), which the shipped `fetchQuiet`/`RunSilentDir` call discards along with the
  rest of the fetch's stderr — so an operator may never see it, which is one more reason the plan
  publishes `remotes[].source` itself; and the mechanism is listed for **removal in Git 3.0**
  (`Documentation/BreakingChanges.adoc`, and both code paths already compile out under
  `WITH_BREAKING_CHANGES`), at which point such a remote stops resolving and the same repository's
  effect becomes the contact-free cell of §4.4 instead. Neither note changes a published field, a
  blocker or a test expectation: they are context for whoever reads a `legacy-remotes`/
  `legacy-branches` row, and no contract in this document is conditioned on them.
- **The legacy file is not the only way a fetch reaches `refs/heads/**`, and round 25 states the
  general rule** (item 2). **Any** *positive* configured fetch refspec whose destination pattern
  **covers `refs/heads/**`** — by the same coverage test §4.4 already states for tags, so the
  mirror `+refs/*:refs/*`, the self-mapping `refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*` and `refs/h*` all cover,
  while `refs/remotes/*` and `refs/tags/*` do not — makes a bare `git fetch` **write local
  branches**: it updates them (fast-forward only when unforced, unconditionally under a leading
  `+`), and, when that remote's effective prune is on, it **deletes** every covered local branch the
  remote does not have, since pruning "doesn't actually care about branches, instead it'll prune
  local ↔ remote-references as a function of the refspec of the remote" (`git fetch` manual,
  PRUNING, verified against Git 2.55.0). §4.4 publishes the two facts as
  `fetch_effect.may_update_local_branches` and `fetch_effect.may_delete_local_branches`, and
  enumerates the covered branches in `fetch_effect.local_branch_destinations`.
- **Where such a refspec meets a *checked-out* branch, Git refuses the whole fetch — before it
  updates or prunes anything** (round-25 item 2). `check_not_current_branch` (`builtin/fetch.c`,
  verified against Git 2.55.0) walks the ref map before `prune_refs` and `fetch_and_consume_refs`
  and **dies** — `refusing to fetch into branch '<ref>' checked out at '<path>'` — for any mapped
  destination under `refs/heads/` that `branch_checked_out()` reports held. `branch_checked_out`
  (`branch.c` `prepare_checked_out_branches`, verified against Git 2.55.0) covers **every non-bare
  worktree** of the store and **four** kinds of hold, one more than this document's rank 5.4 rule:
  HEAD on the branch (`wt->head_ref`), an in-progress rebase's recorded branch
  (`wt_status_check_rebase`), a bisect's `bisecting_from` (`wt_status_check_bisect`) — and a branch
  registered in a running rebase's **`--update-refs` state**
  (`sequencer_get_update_refs_state`), which rank 5.4's `git checkout` predicate does not count and
  which the fetch predicate therefore must (round-25 item 2). `--update-head-ok` is the only escape and neither the shipped call nor
  this feature passes it. Two consequences the document publishes rather than smooths over: the die
  is a **process** failure, so under the shipped `fetchQuiet` the run simply continues against
  **stale** refs (§0.1's non-fatal rule); and the die is evaluated over the **ref map**, so it
  covers the branches the remote really advertises and *not* a prune-only deletion of a held branch
  the remote no longer has — that cell deletes the branch and leaves the worktree's HEAD dangling
  (`prune_refs` → `refs_warn_dangling_symrefs` → `warn_if_dangling_symref`, which prints
  `HEAD has become dangling after <ref> was deleted` on **stderr** — discarded with the rest of the
  fetch's stderr by the shipped `fetchQuiet`/`RunSilentDir` call, §0.1). The controlled route does not run either cell: it declines the fetch
  and refuses at rank 5.06 (§4.9, §8.6.1 cause 6), so **under the guard no covered deletion ever
  reaches a held branch and no HEAD is left dangling**; the unguarded run is unchanged and the
  document says so.
- **In particular, a bare external `--plan` can fetch — and therefore move refs — in the process
  working directory, which may be a repository outside the workspace entirely.** This is the shipped
  fallback context, not a plan-route invention: `fetchQuiet` chooses `-C <worktree>` when
  `UniqueRepos` recorded one, else `-C <entry.Repo>` when the token is non-empty, else
  **`internal.RunSilent` with no `-C` at all** (`internal/cli/sync.go:604-635`,
  `internal/stack.go:37-52`). So a default-repo token whose *first* entry has no worktree directory
  makes the run — and the preview — `git fetch` **wherever the operator is standing**: another
  clone, an unrelated repository, or a repository belonging to a different workspace. The document
  exposes it rather than smoothing it over: the row carries `context_source: process-cwd` with the
  resolved `context_root`, `fetch.mutated_remote_tracking_refs` is `true` **where that context's
  own effect really writes refs and `null` where it cannot be established** (round-23 item 1, §4.4),
  and
  `fetch-context-divergent` names the token when no entry row probes that directory (§4.4, §8.6.9).
  **No text in this document, the flag help, the docs or the skills may say a plan fetches "only the
  selected repositories"** — that claim is false on this route, and the honest statement is "the
  contexts listed in `fetch.repos[]`, which may include the process cwd" (§11, §14).
- The effective fetch policy is **mode-dependent, not flag-dependent**: external defaults to
  `fetch`, checkout defaults to `no-fetch` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:107-116`). So a bare
  `tws sync <feature> --plan` **fetches in external mode** and **does not fetch in checkout mode**.
  `--plan --no-fetch` is the fully-local form — but `--no-fetch` is a **mode trigger** (§0.2), so
  that form describes the **new-mode** run, not the legacy no-flag one. There is therefore no
  fully-local preview of the legacy external route, by construction (§5.3, §8.3.1).
- **No shipped continuation executor fetches.** `handleSyncContinue`
  (`internal/cli/sync.go:311-360`), `handleScopedSyncContinue` (`:363-431`) and
  `ContinueCheckoutSync` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:718-754`) all resume straight into the rebase
  loop with no fetch call at all. So a `--plan --continue` mirrors them with
  `fetch.attempted: false` **whatever the mode's default policy is** (§4.4, §8.6.4).
- **Fetch failure is non-fatal in both modes** (`internal/cli/sync.go:604-635`,
  `internal/checkout_sync.go:616-625`): Git's exit status is discarded, `failed` is printed, and the
  run continues against **stale remote-tracking refs**. A plan computed after a failed fetch is a
  plan over stale inputs.

Consequence for the schema: the plan document must carry the fetch **policy, attempt, per-repo
outcome, and freshness verdict** as first-class facts (§4.4). "The base SHA I am showing you may be
stale, because the fetch this run performed failed and was ignored" is a plan fact, not an
implementation detail.

### 0.2 Routing vocabulary (binding for this whole document)

The second binding vocabulary is *which run* a plan describes. It is fixed here because every later
section depends on it:

- **Mode triggers** are the six shipped flags and only those:
  `--fetch, --no-fetch, --full, --local-only, --only, --from` (`syncTriggerFlags`,
  `internal/cli/sync_modes.go:31`). They and nothing else set `newMode`
  (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:47-53`), which is what selects new-mode execution semantics in both
  workspace modes.
- **Control flags** are this feature's additions — `--plan`, its `--json` modifier,
  `--max-replay-per-entry`, `--max-replay-total`, `--approve-plan`. They are **not** mode triggers
  (§8.5). They *describe* or *guard* the exact underlying path the trigger flags already select.
- **Legacy route**: no trigger flag present. `tws sync <f> --plan` describes the legacy path
  (external `syncFeature` → `syncWithStackScoped` with `run == nil`, `internal/cli/sync.go:535-553`;
  checkout `RunCheckoutSync` with `NewMode == false`).
- **New-mode route**: at least one trigger flag present. `tws sync <f> --plan --only pr2` describes
  `runScopedSync` / the new-mode checkout preflight, with the selection, the header, the restricted
  fetch set and the v2 state that route entails.
- **Route identity is trigger-derived only for a *fresh* run.** On any `--continue` invocation the
  **effective** route and policy are **state-derived**: a v2 payload or a v2 `CheckoutTransaction`
  makes the continuation execute new-mode semantics — persisted scope, scoped argv, persisted
  header — **even with no trigger flag on the command line** (`handleScopedSyncContinue`,
  `internal/cli/sync.go:363-431`; `ContinueCheckoutSync` + `transactionPolicy`,
  `internal/checkout_sync.go:718-766`); a legacy `.sync-state.yaml` or a pre-v2 transaction makes it
  legacy. The document therefore publishes `route` as the **effective** route, `requested_route`
  when the command line asked for a different one, and binds the effective pair into the fingerprint
  (§4.4, §5.3, §8.6.4).
- **Plan-only inspection route** (`--plan`, §8.6): produces a document, takes no lock, writes no
  state, rewrites no local branch or worktree, and may report blockers it does not raise as errors.
  It observes state as a **pre-acquisition snapshot** (§4.4 `state`) — trivially so, since it
  acquires nothing — split into **`state.files`**, where every runtime-file artefact is an object
  carrying
  `{applicable, presence, unreadable_reason}`
  (`absent`/`readable`/`unreadable`/`symlink`/`not-applicable`), and the separate probe facts
  `state.external_cell`/`state.worktree`/`state.git_op`/`state.head`, which have no file behind them
  and therefore no `presence`; so an
  unreadable or symlinked guard is never published as an absent one and its liveness is `null`
  rather than `false`; and it publishes, beside `runnable`/`guard.would_refuse`/`refusal.kind`, the
  **`guard.execute_blocked_by[]`** axis for the refusals its guarded twin performs and the unguarded
  run ignores, so the plan→execute predicate is
  `runnable && !guard.would_refuse && guard.execute_blocked_by == [] && refusal.kind == null`
  — **and its scope is *admission*, not Git success** (binding for this whole document, round-18
  item 1): the predicate answers "will this exact command line be *admitted* — not refused by the
  guard, by a projected shipped gate, or by a declared blocker of this document" and it makes **no**
  claim about what Git does after the first process starts. Rebase conflicts, a checkout Git
  refuses, a hook, a validation command, a remote rejection, a full disk — every ordinary runtime
  failure that is **not knowable by the planner before the run** is outside the biconditional by
  construction. What the guard guarantees is **plan identity** (the §5.3.2 tuple the token binds)
  and **its own declared blockers**; it never guarantees that the replay lands
  (§4.4, §8.6.1 cause 3). **The oracle is only as strong as the state the route can actually
  detect**, so the two are kept in step deliberately: the guard file is inspected on **every** route
  through a dedicated safe inspector — one per runtime file, `Lstat` first, symlinks never followed,
  and each artefact decoded by **its own** shipped loader's rule rather than by one blanket
  version/emptiness rule (§8.6.1 step 2a) — owner signals are the two lock artefacts and
  never a persisted transaction PID, liveness is named for what `Signal(0)` answers, an **owner
  artefact that cannot be decoded** blocks controlled execution under its own
  `owner-artefact-undecodable` token **wherever the artefact is applicable on this route and the
  shipped acquisition ladder would not already
  have refused it** — a corrupt regular guard or lock file is rejected natively, in its own words,
  and is projected as an ordinary rank 3 blocker instead, while an artefact the mode cannot have is
  `not-applicable` and undecodable by nobody (§8.6.2, §4.4 `state`) — and
  `execute_blocked_by` is published on rows-less documents too — each of which closes a cell where
  the plan would otherwise have promised more than the guard can see.
- **Guarded execution route** (limits and/or `--approve-plan` **without** `--plan`, §8.7): the real
  run, with the same plan computed before the first rebase and a clean refusal if a limit or an
  approval fails. It publishes **no document**: `--json` is valid only with `--plan` in v1, a
  **guard-generated** refusal is exit 1 plus exactly one **anchored, guard-written** line
  matching `^plan-guard: <kind>: <sanitized-detail>$` at any position on
  stderr (§8.7.6), and a success prints the ordinary
  shipped prose of the underlying run. Refusals that fire **before** the guard seam are the shipped
  ones, byte-for-byte, and carry no marker (§8.7.6 states the one exception).

The two axes are orthogonal: {legacy, new-mode} × {plan-only, guarded execution, unguarded}. The
unguarded no-flag cell is frozen (§10.1) and no control flag can move a run into a different
underlying-path cell.

Everything below — the schema (§4), the dependency model (§5), the CLI (§8), timing (§9),
compatibility (§10), safety (§11) and the tests (§15) — uses both vocabularies and no other.

The capability **does not exist today**. Two shipped features are partial foundations and neither
is a plan guard:

- `amend-aware-rebase` gives the *execution* the right strategy (`--onto <base> <last_base_sha>`)
  but computes it inline, one entry at a time, with no pre-mutation projection
  (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:117-135`; `internal/checkout_sync.go:1116-1122`).
- `stack-status` / `stack-ancestry-doctor` give *observability* (`current | stale | divergent |
  missing | cross-repo-unsupported` plus recorded-base verdict) but deliberately refuse to claim a
  replay strategy — the evaluator's own comment says promising an identical strategy "would be a
  claim this evaluator cannot support" (`internal/stack_ancestry.go:675-697`).

Between "what state is this edge in" and "the rebase already happened" there is nothing.

Five findings shape the whole feature.

**Finding 1 — external mode has no plan object at all.** Checkout mode builds a real, persisted,
pre-mutation plan (`BuildCheckoutPlan`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:464-517`, persisted as
`CheckoutTransaction.Plan` **before** the first `git checkout`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:656-690`).
External mode makes the same decision inline inside the rebase loop, per entry, with nothing
recorded (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:117-135`). The feature's real structural work is giving
external mode the same pre-mutation plan object, and making one shared planner produce both.

**Finding 2 — "replay count" has exactly one honest definition, and it is not "commits applied".**
Verified on real Git 2.55.0: with the customer's exact-squash topology, the topological source range
for PR1 holds 1 commit and Git applies **0**, printing `dropping <sha> B -- patch contents already
upstream`. `git rev-list <upstream>..<branch>` is therefore **not** the set Git will apply; it is an
**upper bound** taken *before* Git's own two filters — clean-cherry-pick detection ("commits which
are clean cherry-picks (as determined by `git log --cherry-mark ...`) are detected and dropped as a
preliminary step", `git rebase` manual, `--empty` section) and `--empty=drop`, the default for
commits that become empty after replay. This document calls that bounded set the **candidate**
range and never calls it applied. §4.2 fixes the term; §6 contains the verified transcripts.

**Finding 3 — the whole-stack preview is inherently partial, and the source range is not always the
safe half.** After planning PR1, PR2's new base SHA is `post-rebase(pr1)`, which is unknown without
executing or simulating PR1 — so PR2's *destination* is deferred. The *source* range is knowable
**only when PR2 has a recorded cutoff that still resolves**: the recorded cutoff pins the replay
upstream to a commit that does not move (§5.1). With **no** recorded cutoff, both executors fall
back to a plain rebase whose upstream is the **base ref resolved at rebase time**, i.e. the unknown
post-rebase parent — so for a deferred entry the source range is unknown too, and any number printed
for it is a current-snapshot estimate, never an exact count. A guard that pretends otherwise is
lying; a guard that refuses to say anything about PR2 is useless. The recommendation (§5, §8) is a
**precomputed whole-run preview with explicitly deferred destinations, explicitly deferred source
ranges and strategies where they are deferred, plus a per-edge just-in-time revalidation immediately
before each rebase**.

**Finding 4 — a count is not an answer; identity is.** The request is explicit: "expose old cutoff
B, new base D, and **replay C** before mutation" (`request.md`). `candidates: 1` does not tell the
operator *which* commit is about to move, and two very different runs — replaying the commit you
just wrote versus replaying a commit the maintainer already rewrote — print the same `1`. The plan
must therefore publish **bounded candidate identity**: the range expression, the first candidate's
SHA/short/subject, and (in `--json`/verbose) a deterministic, truncation-annotated SHA list (§4.5).
The guard's fingerprint must bind that identity, not the count (§5.3).

**Finding 5 — a preview flag must not change the run it previews.** The obvious implementation makes
`--plan` a seventh member of `syncTriggerFlags`. That is wrong, and it is wrong in a way that
defeats the feature: a trigger flag *selects new-mode execution*, so `tws sync <f> --plan` would
describe a run with a different fetch set, a header, v2 state, and two selection refusals
(duplicate `GitBranch`, `internal/sync_selection.go:231-239`; checkout cross-repo,
`internal/sync_selection.go:223-229`) that the run the operator is actually about to type —
`tws sync <f>` — does not perform. The preview would be of a *different run*. The control flags are
therefore orthogonal to the trigger set (§0.2, §8.5): they wrap whichever path the trigger flags
select. That choice has one obligation attached, discharged in §8.5.5 and §8.6.3: because the legacy
external path answers an unreadable `stack.yaml` with a **mutating** `syncFallback`
(`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:390-399`), plan and guard must intercept *before* execution and
refuse with `plan-unavailable`, never fall through into an unguarded rebase.

The recommended surface is an explicit **non-mutating** `--plan` (human + `--json`) — non-mutating
in the §0.1 sense: no worktree, local-branch, `stack.yaml`, or runtime-state write, fully read-only
under `--no-fetch`, and remote-tracking-ref-mutating when the effective fetch policy is `fetch` — an
**opt-in** threshold guard (per-entry and aggregate, **flags only in v1**, §8.3), no TTY prompt, and
a **byte- and argv-identical no-flag path**. That last constraint is not a preference: the
`internal/cli/testdata/sync_noflag/**` goldens are declared pre-change evidence that "must never be
re-baselined after a production edit" (`internal/cli/sync_golden_test.go:19-31`), and they pin the
exact Git process sequence of a no-flag run in both modes. An automatic guard on the no-flag path
would require re-baselining them, i.e. would destroy the evidence that proves no-flag compatibility.

---

## 1. Is the capability present?

### 1.1 Verified absence

- `syncCmd` has no plan, preview, dry-run, threshold, or approval flag. Its complete flag set is
  `--verbose/-v`, `--push`, `--continue`, `--abort`, `--test`, `--fetch`, `--no-fetch`, `--full`,
  `--local-only`, `--only`, `--from` (`internal/cli/sync.go:132-142`).
- `CheckoutSyncOpts` has no plan/preview/threshold field (`internal/checkout_sync.go:545-561`).
- No command prints a base/cutoff/replay projection before mutating. `tws stack status` is the
  closest and is explicitly read-only, local-only and ancestry-shaped, not replay-shaped — it never
  fetches, so it is read-only in the strict sense §0.1 reserves for `--plan --no-fetch`
  (`internal/cli/stack_status.go:14-100`, `internal/stack_status.go:128-215`).
- `.tpatch/FEATURES.md:63` records `rebase-plan-guard` as `requested`; the roadmap names it as the
  current target (`docs/roadmap.md`, "Current target: **rebase plan guard**").

### 1.2 Partial foundations that must be consumed, not re-derived

| Foundation | What it already establishes | What it cannot do |
|---|---|---|
| `StackEntry.LastBaseSHA` + `UpdateBaseSHA` (`internal/stack.go:19,75-83`) | the recorded old cutoff | says nothing about whether it still resolves, or what will be replayed |
| `--onto` strategy selection (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:124-134`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:1117-1122`) | the executor's real strategy | invisible before mutation; not recorded in external mode |
| `BuildCheckoutPlan` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:464-517`) | a real pre-mutation plan **in checkout only** | no replay count, no cutoff verdict, no collateral analysis, not printed |
| `SyncSelection` (`internal/sync_selection.go:165-247`) | *which* entries participate, roles, cross-repo/duplicate refusals — **on the new-mode route only** (R6, R7) | carries no SHA and deliberately no `LastBaseSHA` (`internal/sync_selection.go:63-65`); does not exist at all on the legacy route |
| `StackEdge` (`internal/stack_ancestry.go:147-181`) | ancestry verdict, heads, merge base, recorded-base verdict | uses a *third* base-resolution rule (§7.2) and refuses to promise a strategy |
| `StackStatusReport` (`internal/stack_status.go:86-215`) | versioned, null-honest projection style to copy | is a status document, not a plan |

---

## 2. Grounded current behaviour: exact Git argv and timing

Everything below is read out of the source and cross-checked against the committed argv goldens
(`internal/cli/testdata/sync_noflag/external-clean/argv.log`,
`internal/cli/testdata/sync_noflag/checkout-clean/argv.log`).

### 2.1 External mode — ordered pipeline

No-flag run (`internal/cli/sync.go:35-125`, `internal/cli/sync.go:535-557`,
`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:78-254`):

1. `RequireTool("git")`, `RequireWorkspace()`, `GuardFeatureName`, `resolveExternalSyncLayout`.
2. `classifySyncState` → legacy-state refusal `previous sync incomplete (failed on: %s)`
   (`internal/cli/sync.go:107-110`).
3. `syncFeature` loads `stack.yaml`; on failure, `fetchQuiet("","",verbose)` + `syncFallback`
   (`git rebase --update-refs origin/main` per worktree directory, hard-coded,
   `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:390-399`). Note what that fallback *is*: an unconditional,
   unplanned, mutating rebase of every directory under the worktrees root, wrapped in
   `internal.Must`. Because the control flags are **not** mode triggers (§0.2), a bare
   `tws sync <f> --plan` and a guarded legacy run both route here: trigger routing does **not** make
   the fallback unreachable, and no section of this document may claim it does. Plan and guard
   therefore intercept the missing/unreadable-stack case **before** the fallback's fetch and before
   `syncFallback` itself, and return a structured `plan-unavailable` refusal that rebases nothing
   (§8.5.5, §8.6.3).
4. **Fetch, once per unique repo, before any planning** — `UniqueRepos` + `fetchQuiet`
   (`internal/cli/sync.go:541-544`, `internal/cli/sync.go:604-635`). This is a **repository write**:
   `git fetch` updates `refs/remotes/**` and fetched tags in the **common** directory and
   `FETCH_HEAD` in the context's **own per-worktree `$GIT_DIR`** (round-22 item 4), and — under an
   effective prune/pruneTags — **deletes** refs and tags there as well (round-22 item 2). Fetch
   failure is
   **non-fatal**: `fetchQuiet` discards Git's exit status, prints `failed`, and the run continues
   against stale remote-tracking refs. Its progress prose goes to **process stdout** through
   `fmt.Printf` (`Fetching <label>... ` then `done`/`failed`), and under `--verbose` it prints
   `Fetching <label>...` and then streams Git's own stdout **and** stderr to the process's
   (`internal.RunDir`, `internal/exec.go:126-134`). Both facts are load-bearing for `--plan --json`
   (§8.3, item 7).
5. `TopoSort` over the whole stack.
6. Pass 1, per materialized entry, **inline decision, no plan object**
   (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:93-163`):
   - `checkSyncWorktreeBranch` → wrong-branch stops the run;
   - `base := resolveEntryBase(stack, entry, syncRepoContext(layout, entry))`
     (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:117`, `:335-356`) — in-stack same-repo parent →
     `parent.GitBranch()`; otherwise `resolveBase`, which maps a base equal to
     `DefaultBranch()`/`DefaultBranchIn(repo)` to `origin/<default>` and leaves everything else
     literal;
   - `currentBaseSHA := internal.GetBranchSHA(gitContext, base)`
     (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:122`, `internal/stack.go:86-96`) —
     `git [-C ctx] rev-parse <base>`, evaluated **at the moment this entry is reached**, i.e.
     *after* every earlier entry of the same
     run has already rebased and possibly moved that ref. It is a live read, not a plan value;
   - argv selection (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:123-135`). The predicate is exactly
     `entry.LastBaseSHA != "" && currentBaseSHA != "" && entry.LastBaseSHA != currentBaseSHA`:

     | run | recorded cutoff state | argv |
     |---|---|---|
     | scope=all | absent, or `currentBaseSHA==""`, or equal | `git rebase --update-refs <base>` |
     | scope=all | present and different | `git rebase --update-refs --onto <base> <LastBaseSHA>` |
     | scoped (`--only`/`--from`) | absent/equal | `git rebase <base>` |
     | scoped | present and different | `git rebase --onto <base> <LastBaseSHA>` |

     Note `<base>` is a **ref name**, not a SHA, in all four shapes: external re-resolves it inside
     `git rebase`. `--no-fork-point` is never passed, and does not need to be: Git documents that
     "if `<upstream>` … is given on the command line, then the default is `--no-fork-point`"
     (`git rebase` manual, FORK-POINT section), and external always passes an explicit upstream.
     **The replay upstream is the second column made concrete**: in the `--onto` arm the upstream is
     the recorded cutoff SHA (pinned, immovable); in the plain arm the upstream is `<base>` *as Git
     resolves it at rebase time*. Because the plain arm is selected only when the cutoff is absent,
     unreadable, or **equal to** `currentBaseSHA`, a recorded, resolvable cutoff yields the same
     upstream *commit* in both arms — which is precisely why §5.1 can keep a source range exact
     while its destination is deferred.
   - execution is `internal.RunDirClean` (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:140`), whose read loop
     consumes git's **stderr**, filters `hint:`/advice lines, rewrites
     `skipped previously applied commit` to `    (skipped duplicate commit)`, and re-emits the rest
     to `os.Stderr` (`internal/exec.go:142-185`); stdout is inherited but carries none of the rebase
     progress or drop lines. This is why the customer saw
     external output literally report the dropped commit — **on stderr** (§6.1);
   - **any** rebase error is reported as `conflict` with "Resolve conflicts in: …"
     (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:140-146`) — including `fatal: invalid upstream <sha>`, which is
     not a conflict at all (§6.5);
   - validation, then `[+] <name> (active)`, `markUpdatedAncestors`, and
     **`UpdateBaseSHA` + `SaveStack` after every single entry**
     (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:148-162`) — guarded by `currentBaseSHA != ""`, so a base whose
     SHA could not be read both downgrades the strategy to a plain rebase *and* silently skips the
     cutoff update.
7. Pass 2, non-materialized entries (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:165-211`) — a **third executor
   arm** the planner must model in full (§5.4), not a footnote of pass 1:
   - `IsPrunableWorktree(entry.GitBranch())` → `[?] <name> (missing …)` and the run **stops**
     (`syncFailure`); prunability is blocking, never a note;
   - `updatedByRef[entry.Name]` → `[+] <name> (archived)` with **no rebase, no base resolution, no
     `GetBranchSHA` and no `UpdateBaseSHA` — but *after* the `IsPrunableWorktree` probe above,
     which is issued unconditionally and gates this skip** (round-37 item 1: the ordering is
     `stat` → prunability → `updatedByRef`, so this arm is not Git-free and a prunable entry never
     reaches it). That map
     is filled by `markUpdatedAncestors` during pass 1, and only on an unscoped run
     (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:151-154`, `:358-379`): it marks every ancestor of a rebased
     entry whose **worktree directory is absent**, from stack topology alone. It is an
     *assumption* that `--update-refs` moved that branch, never a verification (§4.3, §5.4);
   - otherwise `git rebase <base> <gitbranch>` — **an explicit-branch plain rebase**: no
     `--update-refs`, no `--onto`, `entry.LastBaseSHA` is never read, `UpdateBaseSHA` is never
     called, and `<base>` comes from `resolveEntryBase(stack, entry, entry.Repo)` — the entry's
     `Repo`, not its (absent) worktree, as the only repo context. Failure runs
     `git rebase --abort` in the same context and stops the run.
   External never reads `StackEntry.Archived`; "archived" here means "worktree directory absent".
8. Completion gate `staleStackEdgesFiltered` (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:220-233,295-317`);
   optional push (`internal/cli/sync.go:118-124`, `:216-229`).

New-mode run (`runScopedSync`, `internal/cli/sync.go:151-214`) inserts, in this order: selection
resolution → `verifySelectedBasesLocally` (**only under `--no-fetch`**, `internal/cli/sync.go:241-259`)
→ marker + owner token → **`setupSyncRunState` writes `.sync-state.v2.yaml` + `.sync-run.lock` +
the legacy sentinel** → header → fetch (restricted to selected repos) → the same rebase loop.
**State and guard files therefore exist on disk before the fetch and before any plan could be
computed** — a refusal after that point must tear them down (§9).

### 2.2 Checkout mode — ordered pipeline

`RunCheckoutSync` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:563-691`):

1. transaction-exists refusal; `gitOperationInProgress` (rebase/merge/cherry-pick/revert);
   dirty-tree refusal; detached-HEAD refusal; capture `OriginalBranch`/`OriginalHEAD`.
2. New-mode read-only preflight **before the lock**: `LoadStack`, `ResolveSyncSelection`,
   `verifyCheckoutBasesLocally` (again, only under `--no-fetch`,
   `internal/checkout_sync.go:693-716`).
3. `AcquireCheckoutLock` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:612`, `:185-220`).
4. Header, then fetch **only when the run is new-mode and the resolved policy is `fetch`**
   (`internal/checkout_sync.go:616-625`); the no-flag checkout run never fetches, and checkout's
   default policy is `no-fetch` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:107-110`). The fetch is a repository
   write with the same non-fatal failure handling as external: `RunSilentDir` discards Git's exit
   status, `failed` is printed to **stdout**, and planning continues over stale remote-tracking
   refs. The header itself (`Sync mode: fetch=… propagation=… scope=…`) is also stdout
   (`internal/checkout_sync.go:517-522`).
5. `BuildCheckoutPlan` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:464-517`): skip `entry.Archived`; skip empty
   `Base`; base is `entry.Base` **resolved literally** (`git rev-parse <base>`), except under
   `scoped && local-only && role==propagated`, where it becomes `parent.GitBranch()`; also resolves
   `PreSHA` for the child branch. `StackEntry.Repo` is never consulted.
6. `printLocalOnlyNoOp`; empty plan → release lock and return.
7. Transaction persisted **before** the first mutation (`internal/checkout_sync.go:656-690`).
8. Per entry (`processBranch`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:1022-1098`): **re-resolve** `NewBaseSHA`
   (the parent may have moved earlier in this same transaction — this is exactly the deferred
   destination of §5), `git checkout <branch>`, `doRebase`, ancestry verification
   (`merge-base --is-ancestor <NewBaseSHA> <branch>`), optional validation.
9. `doRebase` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:1100-1159`):

   | recorded cutoff state | argv |
   |---|---|
   | present and `!= NewBaseSHA` | `git rebase --no-fork-point --onto <NewBaseSHA> <LastBaseSHA>` |
   | absent or equal | `git rebase --no-fork-point <Base>` |

   `<NewBaseSHA>` is a **pinned SHA**, unlike external's ref name — but it is the SHA re-resolved in
   step 8, not the one `BuildCheckoutPlan` computed, so checkout already treats the plan's
   destination as provisional. `<Base>` in the plain arm is a **ref name**, resolved by Git at
   rebase time. The comparison `LastBaseSHA != NewBaseSHA` therefore uses the **post-parent** base
   SHA, exactly like external's `currentBaseSHA` — so the same conclusion holds: a recorded,
   resolvable cutoff pins the replay upstream commit in both arms. Output is captured with
   `CombinedOutput()` and **discarded on success** (`internal/checkout_sync.go:350-376`), which is
   why checkout mode showed the customer nothing about the dropped commit. A non-conflict failure
   is classified `FailSwitch` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:1132-1136`).
10. `finalizeTransaction` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:1161-1236`): **all** `LastBaseSHA` values are
    written at the end, attributed by logical `Name` with a legacy `GitBranch` fallback; final
    ancestry re-verification for every plan entry; `StageRestoring` + `restoreOriginal`; then push
    (`git push --force-with-lease origin <pe.Branch>`).

### 2.3 When `LastBaseSHA` is initialised and updated

This is decisive for how much the guard can promise.

- **Never at creation.** `tws new` / `tws add -n` build `StackEntry{Name, Base[, Branch][, Repo]}`
  and never set `LastBaseSHA` (`internal/cli/new.go:133-138`, `internal/cli/new.go:221-231`).
  A grep of production code confirms the only writers are sync finalization paths
  (`internal/stack.go:75-83`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:1170-1181`).
- **External**: written per entry, immediately after that entry's successful rebase + validation,
  with `SaveStack` each time; skipped entirely when the base SHA could not be read; **never**
  written on the archived (pass 2) path (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:158-162`, `:164-214`).
- **Checkout**: written for every plan entry at finalization, not per entry
  (`internal/checkout_sync.go:1161-1189`).
- Consequence: a stack that has never been synced has **no cutoff at all**, so the first sync is a
  plain rebase whose replay upstream is the **base ref as Git resolves it at rebase time**. That
  boundary is *not* a cutoff and the schema must never call it one (§4.3): it is a base-ref
  snapshot. It happens to coincide topologically with `merge-base(base, branch)..branch`, because
  `<upstream>..<branch>` is by definition "reachable from branch, not from upstream" — but the
  coincidence is a diagnostic, not a provenance. `StackEdge.MergeBase` may be printed as context; it
  must never be written into a `cutoff.*` field, and no `cutoff.provenance` value may claim a
  merge-base origin. The customer's cold-squash success (§6.2) is therefore **Git's duplicate-patch
  detection, not a tws cutoff guarantee**. The guard must label provenance explicitly
  (`recorded-by-sync` vs `none` for the cutoff; `recorded-cutoff` vs `base-ref-snapshot` vs
  `base-ref-deferred` for the effective replay upstream), and the roadmap item "safe
  reparent/restack" — not this feature — is where an authored cutoff would come from.

### 2.4 Divergence register the planner must mirror, not silently harmonise

| # | Concern | External | Checkout |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | in-stack parent base | `parent.GitBranch()` when same repo (`sync_helpers.go:335-340`) | literal `entry.Base` (a **logical name**) except under scoped local-only (`checkout_sync.go:487-493`) |
| D2 | default-branch base | mapped to `origin/<default>` (`sync_helpers.go:345-356`) | literal; a `master` root does not advance from the remote |
| D3 | `--onto` target | ref **name**, re-resolved by git | pinned **SHA** |
| D4 | `--update-refs` | yes when `scope=all` | never |
| D5 | `--no-fork-point` | not passed (equivalent by default) | passed explicitly |
| D6 | archived | worktree-directory absence; `Archived` flag ignored | `Archived` flag skips the entry |
| D7 | cross-repo | `Repo` honoured for context and edge filtering | `Repo` ignored in the plan; refused only in new mode (`sync_selection.go:223-229`) |
| D8 | cutoff write | per entry, mid-run | all at finalization |
| D9 | rebase output | git's **stderr** streamed through `RunDirClean`'s filter loop and re-emitted to `os.Stderr` (`internal/exec.go:142-185`); stdout is merely inherited and git writes essentially nothing there | `CombinedOutput()` captured and dropped on success (`gitRebaseOnto`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:350-362`) |
| D10 | non-conflict rebase failure | reported as `conflict` | `FailSwitch` |

Short names in the table above are `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go`, `internal/checkout_sync.go`, and
`internal/sync_selection.go`.

D1 hides a latent defect the guard will expose: when a **parent** entry has a decoupled
`branch:`, checkout's `gitResolveRef(repoDir, entry.Base)` resolves a *logical name* as a ref and
fails the whole plan. No test covers it — the decoupled fixtures in
`internal/cli/checkout_sync_modes_test.go:206,425-427` decouple children whose base is `feat-root`,
where `Name == GitBranch`. The plan must print the base ref **as the executor resolves it**, so
this surfaces as a visible, diagnosable plan error instead of a mid-run one. Fixing D1 is a
candidate for this feature only if the spec claims it explicitly; otherwise it belongs to a
separate fix.

### 2.5 Route register: what a trigger flag actually changes

Because the control flags are orthogonal to the trigger set (§0.2), a plan must describe **one of
two underlying runs** and say which. The differences are not cosmetic, and this is the complete
list the planner must honour:

| # | Concern | Legacy route (no trigger flag) | New-mode route (≥1 trigger flag) |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | external fetch set | **every** unique repo of the whole stack, unconditionally (`internal/cli/sync.go:541-544`) | only the repos of the **selected** entries, and only when `policy.Fetch == fetch` (`internal/cli/sync.go:559-566`) |
| R2 | checkout fetch | never (`RunCheckoutSync` fetches only under `opts.NewMode`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:616-625`) | when the resolved policy is `fetch` (never the checkout default) |
| R3 | header | none | `Sync mode: fetch=… propagation=… scope=…` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:502-504`) |
| R4 | external runtime state | `.sync-state.yaml` written **only on failure** (`saveIncompleteSync`) | `.sync-state.v2.yaml` + `.sync-run.lock` + legacy sentinel written **before** the fetch (`setupSyncRunState`) |
| R5 | selection model | none; `run == nil`, every entry participates (`syncRunContext.selects`, `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:31-36`) | `ResolveSyncSelection`, with I10-I13 refusals |
| R6 | duplicate `GitBranch` refusal | **not applied** (gated on `opts.NewMode`, `internal/sync_selection.go:231-239`) | applied, in both workspace modes |
| R7 | checkout cross-repo refusal | **not applied** (`ResolveSyncSelection` is called only under `opts.NewMode`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:592-609`) | applied (`internal/sync_selection.go:223-229`) |
| R8 | I14 local base verification | none | `verifySelectedBasesLocally` / `verifyCheckoutBasesLocally`, only under `--no-fetch` |
| R9 | `--update-refs` in external argv | passed (scope is always `all`) | passed only when `ScopeKind == all` (`syncRunContext.scoped`, `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:27-29`) |
| R10 | anchors under local-only | not expressible | skipped in external, excluded from the checkout plan |
| R11 | checkout transaction | still written, with **no** `state_version` and no frozen policy keys | `StateVersion = CheckoutTransactionVersion` plus the frozen policy/selection keys |
| R12 | unreadable `stack.yaml` | external: `fetchQuiet` + **mutating** `syncFallback`; checkout: `load stack:` error after the lock | clean refusal `sync modes require a stack; feature %q has no readable stack.yaml`, before any lock or state |

R12 is the one with teeth: it is why §8.5.5 requires a `plan-unavailable` interception on the legacy
route rather than a claim that routing makes `syncFallback` unreachable.

---

## 3. Inputs the plan must treat as first-class

1. **Logical `Name` vs `GitBranch()`** — identity in `stack.yaml`, selection, and state is the
   logical name; every Git operation uses `GitBranch()` (`docs/engineering-workflow.md`, coding
   conventions; `internal/stack.go:22-27`). The plan must print both and must key its rows by name.
2. **Literal base refs and default-base resolution** — explicit refs are literal (`master`,
   `origin/master`, tags, SHAs); only an omitted base uses the selected repo's `origin/HEAD`
   (`internal/exec.go:59-88`, `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:345-356`). The plan must print
   `base.name` (configured), `base.kind` (`stack-entry | literal-ref | none`), and `base.ref`
   (executor-resolved) as three distinct facts, exactly as `StackEdge` already separates them
   (`internal/stack_ancestry.go:154-156`).
3. **Cross-repo entries** — external plans them with the entry's `Repo` as Git context and never
   treats a cross-repo parent as a stack parent (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:335-340`): the
   parent's **logical name is passed to `resolveBase` and comes back literal**, so the executor
   hands `git rebase` a ref name that usually does not exist in the child's repository. The
   expected row is therefore `base.kind = literal-ref` with an unresolvable `base.ref`
   (`replay.reason = base-ref-missing`), not a special cross-repo replay verdict. Checkout ignores
   `Repo` entirely in `BuildCheckoutPlan` and refuses cross-repo entries **only on the new-mode
   route** (R7), so a legacy-route plan must show the literal single-repo resolution the legacy run
   would really perform. `cross-repo-unsupported` is a shipped **`StackEdge` ancestry status**
   (`AncestryStatusCrossRepo`, `internal/checkout_health.go:151`, reason `cross-repo`,
   `internal/stack_ancestry.go:93,374-377`) and appears in the plan **only** inside the consumed
   `ancestry` block — never as a `replay.reason` (§4.1) and never as a strategy.
4. **Fetch / no-fetch** — the plan's base SHAs are only meaningful *after* the run's input-ref
   decision. A plan computed before the fetch would show a different new base than the run uses, so
   the plan is computed after it. Four consequences the schema must carry, not hide: (a) under an
   effective `fetch` policy the plan invocation itself **writes remote-tracking refs** (§0.1);
   (b) the effective policy is mode-defaulted — `fetch` external, `no-fetch` checkout
   (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:107-116`); (c) a **failed** fetch is ignored by both executors, so
   the plan may be a projection over stale inputs and must say so (§4.4); (d) **the directory the
   fetch runs in is not always a repository of the workspace** — external's shipped ladder falls
   back to the **process cwd** with no `-C`, so the write can land in an unrelated clone, which the
   document discloses through `fetch.repos[]` rather than suppressing (§0.1, §8.6.9, §11). Under `--no-fetch` the
   plan is fully local. It does **not** inherit I14 as an early error: `verifySelectedBasesLocally`
   (`internal/cli/sync.go:241-259`) and `verifyCheckoutBasesLocally`
   (`internal/checkout_sync.go:693-716`) exist on the new-mode route and stay exactly as shipped for
   unguarded runs, but on the plan-only route the same probe result is published as a **blocker
   row** (`base.ref` unresolvable, `replay.reason = base-ref-missing`) so the operator sees *which*
   entries are affected rather than one entry's message (§8.6.5).
5. **Full / local-only** — under local-only, selected anchors are excluded from the checkout plan
   entirely (`internal/checkout_sync.go:479-482`) and are printed as no-ops in external
   (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:100-105`). The plan must show them as `skipped (anchor)`, not as
   zero-commit rebases.
6. **all / only / from** — scope changes the argv: `--update-refs` is dropped for `only`/`from`
   (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:128-134`). It does **not** follow that a scoped run moves no
   collateral: `rebase.updateRefs = true` re-enables the behaviour without the flag (verified,
   §4.3), so the collateral section of a scoped plan is `[]` **only when the effective config says
   so**, and is otherwise computed exactly as for `scope=all`.
7. **Missing and archived entries** — external pass 2 is a separate arm with its own argv, its own
   repo context, and no cutoff read or write (§2.1 step 7, §5.4); a *prunable* worktree **stops the
   run**. The executor decides that with `IsPrunableWorktree(entry.GitBranch())`, which runs
   `git worktree list --porcelain` in the **process cwd**, with no `-C`, and **before** the arm
   picks `entry.Repo` as its Git context (`internal/exec.go:199-221`,
   `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:181-196`). The plan must **mirror that exact cwd-scoped verdict**,
   because a `-C repoRoot` or workspace-inventory probe answers a different question and would let
   the plan report a runnable run that stops, or a blocked run that proceeds. The row publishes
   `prunability.probe_context = cwd` so the verdict's scope is visible, and the cwd scoping itself
   is recorded as a **separate follow-up defect**, not fixed here (§18.16). The repository-scoped
   `BuildWorktreeInventory` (`internal/agent_status.go:527-536`) is still used — but only for the
   `--update-refs` checked-out-ref exemption of §4.3, never to replace the executor's prunable
   verdict. The plan must model
   `materialized | archived-metadata | worktree-missing | prunable`.
8. **Dirty tree / in-progress Git operation** — checkout refuses both before anything else
   (`internal/checkout_sync.go:565-580`); external refuses only a wrong-branch worktree. On the
   **plan-only route** these are reported as blocker facts with `runnable: false` and the document
   is still produced (§8.6.2), reusing `probeDirty`
   (`internal/stack_status.go:326-337`) and — for the *blocking* Git-operation answer — the
   executor's own `gitOperationInProgress` four-marker predicate rather than the wider
   `probeActiveGitOp`, which supplies a descriptive label only (§4.4 `state.git_op`, §8.6.2
   exactness rule). On the **guarded execution route** the shipped refusals run
   first, unchanged, and the guard never sees the run at all.
9. **External layout** — every path must derive from `externalSyncLayout`
   (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:176-221`); the plan must not re-derive feature paths through
   `TwsRoot()`.
10. **Continuation state** — a plan shown at `--continue` describes only the *remaining* entries and
    is reconciled against whatever the route froze: the v2 payload on the new-mode route
    (`SyncRunState`, `internal/sync_run_state.go:38-63`; `CheckoutTransaction`,
    `internal/checkout_sync.go:63-100`), and on the legacy route the far thinner
    `.sync-state.yaml` (`completed`/`pending`/`failed_branch` only,
    `internal/syncstate.go:11-17`) or the transaction a legacy checkout run still writes. Which of
    those exists **is** the effective route (§0.2): a continuation's route and policy are read out
    of the frozen state, never off the command line, and every continuation gate that state can
    fail is projected as a blocker instead of inherited as an early return (§8.6.4). A legacy
    external continuation has **no persisted policy and nowhere to persist a guard limit** (§8.7.4).
11. **Push and validation intent** — both are decisions of the run the plan describes, and both are
    invisible in the rebase argv, so the plan publishes them as first-class facts (§4.4 `intent.*`,
    and, for push, the projected `push.targets[]`)
    and binds them into the approval identity (§5.3). The routes differ and the plan must mirror
    each exactly: `--push` is a shipped presence-map key that pushes **after** the run
    (`internal/cli/sync.go:118-124`, `runNewModePush`, `finalizeTransaction`'s
    `git push --force-with-lease`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:1161-1236`) — and the *set* it pushes
    differs per route: the legacy whole-feature set under `scope=all` (`pushFeature` →
    `pushEntries`), exactly the selected-and-rebased, not-already-pushed entries under
    `only`/`subtree` (`pushScoped`, `internal/cli/push.go:70-108`), and every `tx.Plan` entry in
    checkout — the exact derivations are fixed in §4.4 ("Deriving `push.targets[]`"), including the
    `scope=all` set's inclusion of local-only anchors and unselected entries. That set is what
    `push.targets[]` publishes, as a projection **conditional on the described rebase and
    validation succeeding**, and it is why a push-stage continuation
    with **no** remaining rebase entry still has approvable work (§4.4, §8.6.4a). Whether the run
    reaches the push is the separate published pair `push.executable`/`push.blocked_by[]`, and the
    lease each push would take is published per target (§4.4). A v2 external payload
    and a checkout transaction **persist** the boolean (`SyncRunState.Push`,
    `internal/sync_run_state.go:52`; `CheckoutTransaction.Push`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:74`)
    and a continuation uses the persisted value, while a **legacy external** continuation takes
    push straight off the invocation (`handleSyncContinue(feature, layout, push)`,
    `internal/cli/sync.go:311`) because `.sync-state.yaml` holds no push key. Validation diverges
    the same way: the `--test` flag is **checkout-only** — external never reads it
    (`internal/cli/sync.go:50-58` passes `TestCommand` only to `CheckoutSyncOpts`), a legacy
    external run resolves `internal.LoadConfig().TestCommand` **fresh on every entry**
    (`runValidation`, `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:401-403`), and a new-mode external run freezes
    the config command plus its `validation_source` in the payload
    (`internal/cli/sync.go:180-186`) so a resume can never validate with a different command.
    A guard that bound the replay but not "and then force-push" or "and then run this command"
    would authorise strictly more than it showed (§4.4, §5.3, §8.7.7). The legacy external
    per-entry re-read is the one cell where "the plan published a validation identity" is not yet
    true of the run; §8.8 states the freeze that makes it true on guarded routes and the
    `intent.validation.stability` value that must be published if `define` declines it.

---

## 4. Plan vocabulary

The spec must fix this vocabulary exactly; every term below is either derivable from existing code
or explicitly nullable.

### 4.1 Per-entry fields

| Field | Meaning | Source | Null / unknown when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | logical `StackEntry.Name` | `stack.yaml` | never |
| `git_branch` | `GitBranch()` | `internal/stack.go:22-27` | never |
| `repo` | `StackEntry.Repo` (empty = default) | `stack.yaml` | never (empty string is a value) |
| `base_context` | the **Git context this row's base, default-branch and ref-resolution probes run in**, a **closed three-member object `{context_id, repo_root, source}`** (round-34 item 1, which splits round-33's single `repo_context` into the two contexts the shipped executors really use: on an external pass-1 row whose `StackEntry.Repo` is non-empty they are **two different directories**, and one field could name only one of them). `source` is a closed **five**-member enum — the four directory rules below plus **`not-applicable`**, the skip-row member of round-36 item 4, which is the one member that carries a `null` `context_id`/`repo_root` without being a refusal: **`entry-repo`** for an external **pass-1** row whose `Repo` is non-empty — `resolveEntryBase(stack, entry, syncRepoContext(layout, entry))` and `GetBranchSHA(gitContext, base)` both take `entry.Repo` there (`internal/cli/sync.go:593-602`, `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:117-122`) —, and **`worktree`** — **unconditionally, one cell and not two** — for a pass-1 row whose `Repo` is **empty** (round-36 item 1, which withdraws round-35 item 1): round 35 added a second cell for a worktree whose `os.Stat` fails with an error that is **not** `os.IsNotExist`, on the ground that the pass-1 loop's own `if _, err := os.Stat(path); os.IsNotExist(err) { continue }` guard lets it through (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:105-108`) and `syncRepoContext` then answers `""`, i.e. the process cwd (`internal/cli/sync.go:593-602`). **That cell is unreachable *as a rebase row*, and round-37 item 2 states its reachability exactly rather than removing it wholesale.** The stat guard is not the next thing the loop does with `path`: `checkSyncWorktreeBranch(path, entry)` runs first, and it is `git -C <path> rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` (`internal/health.go:102-110`), whose `chdir` fails for exactly the errors `os.Stat` failed for — `ENOTDIR`, `EACCES`, `ELOOP`, `ENAMETOOLONG` — so the run stops at the shipped wrong-branch refusal (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:111-115`) **before the loop's own `syncRepoContext` call**. **But the loop is not the only caller, and the route decides whether one runs earlier** (round-37 item 2, correcting round-36 item 1's over-broad "no context ref … reaches later planning"): on the **new-mode `--no-fetch`** route `runScopedSync` calls `verifySelectedBasesLocally` **before** `syncFeatureScoped` (`internal/cli/sync.go:164`, §9 route order), and that preflight calls `syncRepoContext(layout, entry)` for every selected non-local-only-anchor entry, so a non-`IsNotExist` stat error there really does answer `""` and the preflight really does resolve and verify that entry's base **in the process cwd** (`resolveEntryBase(stack, entry, "")` → `internal.VerifyGitRef("", ref)`, `internal/cli/sync.go:239-260`). The **legacy** external route and every **fetch**-enabled new-mode route never reach it at all — `verifySelectedBasesLocally` returns immediately unless `sel.Policy.Fetch == internal.SyncFetchDisabled` — so on those routes the run stops at wrong-branch with **no** base resolution anywhere and the cell is empty in every sense. The consequences are stated in one shape and no other: the entry's row is the shipped **rank 4 `preflight-refused`** row (§4.9 rank 4, "wrong-branch worktree"), it carries **no strategy, no argv, no rebase and no `execution_context`** — the worktree it names cannot be established — and **no rebase row for that entry, or for any entry after it, reaches later planning**; where the route's own preflight ran, that row may carry a **`process-cwd` `base_context`** and the `base.ref` the preflight resolved, which is a *preflight* fact and never an execution destination, and where the preflight's `VerifyGitRef` failed the run is refused before the loop and the row is the shipped I14 `base-ref-missing` cell instead (§8.6.5). **No surviving pass-1 *strategy* row ever carries a process-cwd base context on any route.** So for **every surviving** external pass-1 row with an empty `Repo` the base context is that entry's worktree, `base_context` and `execution_context` **coincide**, and round 34's "the two contexts coincide there" is **restored**: the only external split is the non-empty-`Repo` row. **`entry-repo`** for an external **pass-2** row whose `Repo` is non-empty, **`process-cwd`** for a pass-2 row whose `Repo` is empty — `resolveEntryBase(stack, entry, "")`, exactly what `RunSilentDir("", …)` / `RunSilent` do on that arm (§5.4, §11) — and **`workspace-repo-root`** in checkout, where `BuildCheckoutPlan` resolves every base in `opts.RepoDir`. **What is measured here and nowhere else, and round 35 makes the set *smaller* than round 34's** (item 3): the default-branch read `resolveBase` performs (`DefaultBranch()` with no `-C`, or `DefaultBranchIn(ctx)`, `internal/exec.go:59-77`), the resolution of `base.ref` from `StackEntry.Base`, and the `rev-parse` behind **`base.decision_sha`** that the executor itself issues as `GetBranchSHA` — the value it compares to `LastBaseSHA` to choose the arm and later records (§2.3, §5.1). **Everything `git rebase` itself resolves belongs to `execution_context` and is moved there**: `destination.sha`/`destination.snapshot_sha`, the cutoff verification, the head `rev-parse --verify`, the candidate `rev-list` count/identity/digest probes, the `<git_branch>..<upstream>` probe and the `for-each-ref refs/heads/` inventory whose intersection with the candidate range is the collateral upper bound. Round 34 attributed all of them here, which is wrong in exactly the cell the split exists for: the rebase is `RunDirClean(<worktree>, "git", "rebase", …)`, so Git peels its operands, the branch tip and every ref it may update in **that** store, and a plan that read them from `entry.Repo` would publish commits the run never sees and refs it never touches (§4.3, §4.5, §5.1). **`context_id` is the context's stable identity** — the 64-lowercase-hex digest defined in §4.4, and the **only** key by which this ref cites its `repositories[]` row, never the `(repo, repo_root)` pair and never the `repo` token, since §11 renders the root lossily and two distinct contexts may share the rendering (round-32 item 1, round-33 items 1 and 7, round-34 item 2). `repo_root` is that context's canonical absolute path **as §11 renders it, display-only and lossy**: it is never an identity, a join key, a sort key or a fingerprint member (round-33 items 1 and 4, unchanged by the split). The **raw** canonical path is a different thing from that member and keeps every job it had — it is what each probe's `-C` names, what §8.6.9 resolves a common dir from, and what `context_id` hashes — so nothing that *decides* anything reads the rendering. **The two refs may name one context, and usually do**: on **every** pass-1 row with an empty `Repo` (round-36 item 1), on every pass-2 row and on every checkout row they carry the **identical** `context_id` and cite the **same** `repositories[]` row, which is published once; where they differ, one `repo` token legitimately produces **two** `repositories[]` rows (§4.4, §13). **Whether they are one context is *measured*, never inferred from the two `source` labels** — both roots and both absolute common dirs are resolved and compared byte-for-byte by the context-pair rule below, and where the common dirs differ the row carries the rank 5.15 `base-execution-store-divergent` blocker (round-35 item 2). When `context_id` is `null` this ref cites **no** `repositories[]` row at all — by that id or by any other key — because nothing was probed there, so fabricating one would publish a repository the plan never read (§4.4, §5.3) | §2.1 step 6/7, §2.2, §5.4 | `context_id` and `repo_root` are `null` **together and only together**, and they have **exactly two causes, told apart by `source` and never conflated** (round-36 item 4): (a) **the context could not be established** — no resolvable, canonicalizable top level, or no resolvable absolute common dir, which are both members of the identity of §4.4 — where `source` still names the *rule* that chose the directory (`worktree`/`entry-repo`/`process-cwd`/`workspace-repo-root`) and the row is a **blocking** `repo-unavailable` row (§4.9 rank 5.1) whichever of the two refs failed, since a row whose base cannot be resolved and a row whose rebase has nowhere to run are equally unplannable; the two refs are nulled **independently**, and the one that resolved keeps its values (round-34 item 1); and (b) **no context applies to this ref at all**, where `source` is the fifth enum member **`not-applicable`** and the row is **never** blocking and **never** `repo-unavailable` — the skip-row cell fixed by the skip-context rule below. `source` is never `null` in either cause: the rule that chose the context, or the fact that no rule applies, is known even when the directory is not (round-33 items 1 and 2, round-36 item 4) |
| `execution_context` | the **Git context this row's own `git rebase`/`git checkout` runs in, and in which every precondition of that call is measured** — the same closed three-member object `{context_id, repo_root, source}`, with the same identity, join, display and nullability rules as `base_context` above (round-34 item 1). `source` is drawn from the same closed enum but is decided by the **arm**, never by `entry.Repo` alone: **`worktree`** for **every** external **pass-1** row, whose rebase is `RunDirClean(path, "git", rebaseArgs…)` in that entry's own worktree and whose validation runs there too (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:116-152`) — *including* a row whose `Repo` is non-empty, whose base context is that repository while its rebase, its dirty tree and its holder question are the worktree's, which is exactly the cell round 33's single field flattened —; **`entry-repo`** / **`process-cwd`** for an external **pass-2** row, whose `RunSilentDir(entry.Repo, …)` / `RunSilent` execution directory is the same directory its base resolves in, so both refs carry one `context_id` there (§5.4); and **`workspace-repo-root`** in checkout (`gitCheckout(opts.RepoDir, entry.Branch)`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:1040-1047`). **What is a fact of this context and of no other**: `context.dirty`, `context.autostash`, `context.autostash_applies_to_this_arm` and `context.autostash_reapply_may_conflict`, `context.rebase_in_progress`, `context.untracked_present`/`context.overwrite_risk`, `branch_checked_out_at` with its self-vs-foreign comparison and the `worktree list --porcelain` inventory that answers it (including the checked-out exemption half of the collateral set, §4.3), every `mutation.*` fact, the row's validation command (§8.8), **every ref, range and inventory `git rebase` itself resolves** — `destination.sha` and `destination.snapshot_sha` (`base.ref` peeled *here*, because the rebase runs here and resolves its operand here), the cutoff verification behind `cutoff.state`/`cutoff.resolved_sha` (the `--onto` arm's source boundary is an operand of that same command), `head.state`/`head.sha`, the plain arm's upstream, the candidate `rev-list` count/identity/digest probes, the `<git_branch>..<upstream>` probe behind `replay.may_drop_patch_equivalent`, and the `for-each-ref refs/heads/` inventory behind `collateral_refs` (round-35 item 3) —, and **the `rebase.*` configuration this row's rebase actually obeys** — `rebase.rebaseMerges`, `rebase.updateRefs`, `rebase.backend` and `rebase.autoStash` are read by the `git rebase` process, which starts *here*, so `effective_backend`, `collateral_mechanism`, the merge-recreation determinacy of §4.2 and the autostash facts of §5.4.7 all cite **this** ref's `repositories[]` row and never the base context's (round-34 item 2). **Contexts that are neither of these two stay their own projections**: `fetch.repos[].context_root` follows the `UniqueRepos` + `fetchQuiet` ladder (§8.6.9), `push.targets[].repo_root` follows the push ladder (§4.4), and `prunability.probe_context` is the process cwd (§3.7); none of the three may be read as, or derived from, either context ref | §2.1 step 6/7, §2.2, §5.4 | exactly as `base_context` above and **independently of it**: `context_id` and `repo_root` are `null` together precisely when *this* context could not be established, which is the same **blocking** `repo-unavailable` row (§4.9 rank 5.1); `source` is never `null` |
| `role` | `anchor` / `propagated` | `SyncSelection.Role` (`internal/sync_selection.go:125-134`) | never for selected entries |
| `base.name` | **configured base identity**, verbatim | `StackEntry.Base` | empty base → `null` |
| `base.kind` | `stack-entry` / `literal-ref` / `none` | mirror of `stackBaseRef` semantics | never |
| `base.ref` | **resolved base ref the executor will pass to git** — and, in exactly one cell, a ref the executor resolves without passing it to any rebase: on a **`skipped-updated-ref`** row of the **new-mode `--no-fetch`** route the value is the one `verifySelectedBasesLocally` resolved and verified in the preflight, published because the route really computed it and labelled by the row's `strategy` as **not an execution destination** (round-37 item 1, §4.1 skip-context rule) | `resolveEntryBase`/`BuildCheckoutPlan` rule for the active mode; the I14 preflight on the one skip cell above (`internal/cli/sync.go:239-260`) | base unset, or resolution failed; **`null` on every skip row whose `base_context.source` is `not-applicable`** — which is every `skipped-anchor`/`skipped-archived`/`skipped-no-base` row and every `skipped-updated-ref` row outside the new-mode `--no-fetch` route (round-37 item 1) |
| `base.decision_sha` | **the strategy-decision SHA, and never the destination** (round-35 item 3): the value the shipped external executor reads for `base.ref` with `GetBranchSHA` and compares to `StackEntry.LastBaseSHA` to choose between the plain and `--onto` arms, and the value it writes back with `UpdateBaseSHA` on success (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:117-122`, `:158-162`, §2.3, §5.1).
