  reports `freshness: not-refreshed-no-fetch-targets` (the **seventh** cell above — the
  non-suppression one, below the six suppressions in precedence, renumbered by round-23 item 3 and
  again by round-25 item 2);
- nor is a **fetch that contacted nothing**: the process ran and exited 0, so nothing was declined
  and nothing failed; it reports `contacted: false` and
  `freshness: not-refreshed-no-resolved-remote` (the **eighth** cell above, round-22 item 3);
- nor is a **fetch whose effect or submodule reach could not be established**: it ran, it exited 0,
  and only the description is incomplete, so it reports `freshness: unknown-fetch-effect` with
  `fetch.mutated_remote_tracking_refs: null` (the **ninth** cell above, round-23 items 1 and 3 —
  round-27 item 5 corrects the number, which said "eighth" and collided with the no-resolved-remote
  cell one bullet up).
  Its fail-closed sibling **is** a suppression and is cause 5, not a cell: an effective recursion
  mode of `yes` over an `unknown` reach declines the fetch entirely
  (`freshness: not-refreshed-submodule-reach-indeterminate`, rank 5.05); **its round-25 twin is
  cause 6 and behaves identically** — a covering positive refspec over a held, or unestablishable,
  local-branch destination declines the fetch too
  (`freshness: not-refreshed-local-branch-checked-out`, rank 5.06, round-26 item 5);
- a `--continue` invocation, which never fetches for the separate reason of §8.6.4 and reports
  `not-refreshed-continuation` rather than `not-refreshed-live-run`; when both apply, the
  continuation reason wins, because it is the executor's own behaviour rather than this route's
  precaution.

**8.6.2 Fresh-run refusals become projected blockers.** These are the checks a fresh run performs
before the first mutation; on the plan-only route each becomes a `blockers[]` row with a stable
`refusal.kind`, instead of an early return. Every kind in this table is a §4.9 rank 1-5 fact, so
each of them **does** set `runnable: false` — unlike the guard verdicts of ranks 7-12, which do not
(§4.4):

| Shipped fresh-run refusal | Source | Plan-only rendering |
|---|---|---|
| checkout transaction exists | `internal/checkout_sync.go:564-566` | `state-refused`, with the transaction's stage and failed entry |
| another Git operation in progress | `:567-569` | `state-refused`, **projected from the shipped `gitOperationInProgress` predicate and from nothing wider** (see the exactness rule below) |
| dirty working tree | `:570-577` | `state-refused` (`probeDirty` detail) |
| detached HEAD | `:578-583` | `state-refused` |
| checkout lock held | `AcquireCheckoutLock`, `:185-220` | `state-refused`, observed only — **and projected in full, arm by arm** (see the native-acquisition rule below) |
| scoped guard claim on a fresh new-mode external run | `ClaimSyncRunGuard`, `internal/sync_run_state.go:171-201`, via `setupSyncRunState` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:385-386`) at `internal/cli/sync.go:186` | `state-refused`, **arm by arm, each with its own shipped sentence** (see the native-acquisition rule below) |
| external `previous sync incomplete` / cell refusals | `internal/cli/sync.go:107-111`, `syncCellRefusal` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:302-361`) | `state-refused`, with the cell's own sentence |
| scoped sync already running (live guard) | `internal/cli/sync_modes.go:302-311` | `state-refused` |
| selection refusals I10-I13 (new-mode route only) | `internal/sync_selection.go:173-237` | `selection-refused`; the document is a refusal document with no `entries[]` |
| wrong-branch worktree (external, per entry) | `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:111-116` | per-row `blocking: true`, `preflight-refused` |
| prunable worktree (external pass 2) | `:181-184` | per-row `blocking: true`, `prunable-worktree` (§5.4.3) |
| missing/unresolvable head ref | `internal/checkout_sync.go:500-503`; external pass 2 `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:196-201` | per-row `head.state`, `blocking: true`, `head-ref-missing` (§5.1 rule 6) |
| I14 base-not-local under `--no-fetch` | `internal/cli/sync.go:241-259`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:693-716` | per-row `base.ref` unresolvable, `replay.reason = base-ref-missing` (§8.6.5) |
| unreadable `stack.yaml` | §8.5.5 | `plan-unavailable`; this one produces **no** `entries[]` |
| unsortable stack (cycle) | `internal/stack.go:177-180` | `stack-unsortable`; also **no** `entries[]` (§5.5) |

Everything else — a conflict, a validation failure, a push failure — is *not* projected, because it
is not knowable before mutation (§4.2) and the plan must not pretend otherwise. When several of
these hold at once, all of them appear in `blockers[]` and §4.9 decides which one is `refusal.kind`.

**The two native acquisition ladders are projected in full, and they sit *above* the guard seam —
which is why nothing needs hoisting there** (round-17 item 3). Two shipped functions take ownership
before anything this feature adds can run, and each is a **refusal ladder**, not a single check:

- **`ClaimSyncRunGuard`** on a fresh new-mode external run (`internal/sync_run_state.go:171-201`),
  reached through `setupSyncRunState` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:385-386`) at
  `internal/cli/sync.go:186` — **before** `syncFeatureScoped`, and therefore before the guard seam,
  which sits after the fetch loop and before the first rebase (§8.7.5). Its observable arms, in
  shipped order, each byte-exact: `read existing sync guard: %w` (the guard exists and cannot be
  read); `invalid sync guard; inspect %s and use --abort to recover: %w` (it does not decode);
  `sync guard is being initialized or is invalid; retry or inspect %s` (`guard.PID <= 0`);
  `a scoped sync is already running for %q (pid %d, started %s); wait for it or use
  --continue/--abort after it exits` (`syncProcessAlive`); and `stale sync guard from PID %d with
  existing scoped state; use --continue or --abort to recover` (a dead PID with
  `HasSyncRunState`). **Two differences from `ReclaimSyncRunGuard`'s ladder must not be
  harmonised**: the claim path has **no `pid != os.Getpid()` conjunct** — on a fresh run the guard
  is never ours — and it carries the extra stale-with-state arm, which the reclaim path
  deliberately does not (`internal/sync_run_state.go:171-201` vs `:207-232`). The first cell of the
  ladder is not a read at all but the `O_EXCL` create, so "the guard exists" is itself observed as
  `os.IsExist`; the plan mirrors the *outcome*, never the create.
- **`AcquireCheckoutLock`** on a fresh checkout run (`internal/checkout_sync.go:185-220`), taken at
  `:612` **before** `BuildCheckoutPlan` and therefore before the checkout guard seam. Same shape,
  its own sentences: `read existing checkout-sync lock: %w`; `invalid checkout-sync lock; inspect
  %s and use --abort to recover: %w`; `checkout-sync lock is being initialized or is invalid; retry
  or inspect %s`; `checkout-sync lock held by live process %d (created %s); cannot steal live lock`;
  and `stale lock from PID %d detected with existing transaction; use --continue or --abort to
  recover`. Note that its live sentence differs from `forceAcquireCheckoutLock`'s
  (`lock held by live process %d; cannot reclaim`, `:281-283`): fresh runs and continuations are two
  ladders with two texts, and neither is ever substituted for the other.

Four consequences are binding. **Plan-only projects every arm**: each becomes a rank 3
`state-refused` blocker carrying the shipped sentence in `refusal.detail`, `runnable: false`, exit
0, derived from the pre-acquisition snapshot — the plan route calls neither function and takes
nothing (§8.6.1 step 2, §0.1). **Guarded execution needs no seam work here at all**: the acquisition
runs *before* the seam, so a guarded run in one of these cells never reaches the guard, prints the
shipped sentence **marker-free** and exits 1 exactly as on `main`. That is §8.7.1's ordinary case,
not a hoist — nothing was moved, so there is nothing to re-evaluate, and §8.7.5's three-step order
applies to the **scoped continuation** seam and to it alone. **The write-path arms are not
projectable and are never invented**: `create sync guard directory: %w`, `create lock directory:
%w`, `reclaim stale sync guard: %w`, `reclaim stale checkout-sync lock: %w`, `acquire checkout-sync
lock after stale recovery: %w` and the raw `writeSyncGuardExclusive`/`writeLockExclusive` errors are
outcomes of writes the plan never performs, so the document publishes no blocker for them; a guarded
run reaches them natively and prints them itself. **And this is what bounds
`owner-artefact-undecodable`** (§4.9 rank 3, §8.6.1 cause 3, §19.22): a corrupt or unreadable
*regular* guard or lock file is refused by the ladder above, natively, in its own words — so that
cell is a **shipped** rank 3 refusal, not a controlled-path divergence, and it emits no member. What
remains for the member is exactly what the native ladder reads straight through or never reads at
all: a **symlink whose target decodes** (`os.ReadFile` follows it while the `Lstat`-first inspector
records `presence: symlink`), and an **applicable** owner-signalling artefact on a path this route never
consults — `.sync-run.lock` under a **legacy**
external route, where no shipped acquisition touches the file and the guarded route's fail-closed
decision is the only thing that would. **Applicability is the outer bound** (round-19 item 5): an
artefact the mode cannot have is `applicable: false` with `presence: not-applicable`, which is a
route fact and not an undecodable one, so `.checkout-sync.lock` under an **external** route — never
probed, never decodable, never a divergence — emits nothing, and the cross-mode cell earlier drafts
listed here is deleted (§4.4 `state`).

**The checkout Git-operation blocker mirrors one shipped predicate exactly, and the broader probe is a label only.** The refusal `RunCheckoutSync` performs is `gitOperationInProgress(opts.RepoDir)` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:396-406`, called at `:567-569`), and its marker set is closed at **four**: a `rebase-merge` **or** `rebase-apply` directory (`gitRebaseInProgress`, `:392-394`), `MERGE_HEAD`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `REVERT_HEAD`. The plan's `state-refused` projection is that predicate and no other, evaluated the same way — each marker resolved with `git rev-parse --git-path <name>` and then `os.Stat`, through the same `gitPathExists` helper (`:408-418`). **It is also a *checkout-mode* blocker and nothing else** (§4.4 `state.git_op`): the top-level `state.git_op` publishes `applies: false` with `in_progress`/`kind`/`kind_source` all `null` on every external document, and no external route derives a Git-operation blocker from it — the external facts are the per-row `context.rebase_in_progress` (§4.1, §4.9 rank 5.45) and the shipped continuation gate over the failed branch (§8.6.4), each in its own directory. Four consequences are binding:

- **Bisect is a fact, never a refusal.** `probeActiveGitOp`'s marker inventory additionally holds `BISECT_LOG` (`internal/stack_status.go:341-351`), which the executor never consults, so a repository mid-`git bisect` **is not refused by the shipped checkout run** and must not be refused by the plan either. It is published as the non-blocking `state.git_op.kind: bisect` with `in_progress: false` and `kind_source: active-op-probe` (§4.4 `state`), and it may become a `warnings[]` row, never a `blockers[]` row. Projecting it as `state-refused` would publish `runnable: false` over a run that really succeeds — the plan→guard oracle broken in the direction that is hardest to notice, because the operator simply believes the tool.
- **A malformed or missing `.git` mirrors the executor, which means it does not refuse.** `gitPathExists` returns `false` on **any** error — a failed `rev-parse`, an absent `.git`, a `.git` file whose `gitdir:` pointer is malformed or dangling — so `gitOperationInProgress` answers `false` and the shipped run proceeds to fail (or succeed) further down on its own terms. `probeActiveGitOp` deliberately does the opposite and returns an **error** for exactly those inputs (`internal/stack_status.go:353-401`), because `tws status` must not fabricate `"none"` for a repository whose Git directory is gone. The plan keeps both answers apart: `state.git_op.in_progress` follows the executor and is `false`, while the probe's failure is recorded as the **closed `kind` value `probe-failed`** with `kind_source: active-op-probe` naming the inventory that failed (round-25 item 6, which replaces the previous draft's `kind: null` here — `null` is now reserved for `applies: false`, so an external document and a broken checkout repository are no longer spelled the same way). It does not become a Git-operation refusal, because the run it describes is not refused by one.
- **The mode boundary is asserted, not assumed.** A checkout fixture mid-`rebase-merge` refuses in the plan *and* in the real run; the **same** repository reached through the **external** route publishes `state.git_op.applies: false`, no top-level Git-operation blocker, and only the per-row `context.rebase_in_progress` for the rows whose own **execution directory** is affected — which is what the external executor really does, since it never calls `gitOperationInProgress` (§4.4, §8.6.2 above).
- **The broader predicate is never substituted for the narrow one.** `probeActiveGitOp` is a status-surface helper with a wider marker set and a stricter error contract; reusing it as the blocker would over-refuse on bisect and over-refuse on a repository shape the executor tolerates. It supplies the human-readable `kind` label and nothing else, and §15's checkout state tests assert both directions: a `REVERT_HEAD` fixture refuses in the plan *and* in the real run, a `BISECT_LOG`-only fixture refuses in **neither**, and a dangling-`gitdir` fixture produces no Git-operation blocker in either.

**Six blockers in that array are *not* projections of a shipped refusal, because no shipped check
exists for them**: `repo-unavailable` and `probe-failed` (§4.1 probe-failure rule), the **two**
pre-switch preconditions `branch-checked-out-elsewhere` and `context-dirty` (§5.4.7), the
**external** pre-mutation `external-rebase-in-progress` fact of §4.9 rank 5.45, and the
checkout **`restore-blocked`** fact of §4.4/§4.9 rank 4.5, whose three probes predict the failure
`restoreOriginal` hits *after* every entry has already been rebased. **The count is six, not round
17's seven**: `untracked-would-be-overwritten` is withdrawn with its rank 5.55, because the
prediction behind it was not decidable statically — the untracked-overwrite question leaves the
blocker array entirely and is published as the non-blocking `untracked-present` warning instead
(round-18 item 1, §4.1, §4.9, §5.4.7, §19.26). They are guard
**introductions**, exactly like the legacy-external `plan-unavailable` interception of §8.5.5: each
predicts a failure the shipped run really has — `git rebase` dying at a missing directory, at
`branch … is already used by worktree at …`, at `cannot rebase: You have unstaged changes`, or at
`It seems that there is already a rebase-merge directory`; or
`restoreOriginal` dying at a branch that is gone, held elsewhere, or moved while it was not in the
plan —
and each is therefore **guard-generated by origin**, so a guarded refusal carries the marker line
while the shipped run's own message keeps whatever Git prints (§8.7.6).

**The external Git-operation fact is per row, and it is deliberately *not* a top-level blocker**
(§4.4 `state.git_op`). No external arm runs `gitOperationInProgress`, and no external arm probes a
rebase-in-progress **before a fresh rebase on either arm** — `isRebaseInProgress` is reached only on
the `--abort` cleanup paths and on the two `--continue` failed-branch gates
(`internal/cli/sync.go:270`, `:302`, `:317`, `:373`). So the fresh-run cell has no shipped check to
project and must not pretend it does: the plan probes **each selected row's own execution
directory** — the worktree for a pass-1 row, `execution_context.repo_root` (`entry.Repo`, else the
process cwd) for a pass-2 one — for a `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` **operation directory**,
publishes `context.rebase_in_progress`, and raises the rank 5.45 row blocker where it is `true`
(§4.1). Four consequences are binding. **The predicate is the operation-directory one, not the
shipped `isRebaseInProgress`**: that helper is `false`-biased at a `break` stop and on any context
whose `rev-parse --git-dir` fails, which is right for the continuation gate it belongs to and wrong
for a fresh-run prediction, where a `false` authorises a rebase Git will refuse (§8.6.4). **Autostash
never overrides it**: `rebase.autoStash` decides the rank 5.5 dirty-tree cell, and Git refuses an
`already a rebase-merge directory` invocation before it would stash anything, so the settled
`autostash-across-switch` warning of §19.18 does not reach this rank and no configuration turns
this blocker into a warning. **It stays
per row and per directory**: an unrelated worktree elsewhere in the workspace, or a rebase in a
repository no selected row runs in, changes nothing — publishing a broad top-level external Git-op
blocker would refuse a run the executor performs. And **on pass 2 it prevents destruction, not just
failure**: the shipped pass-2 failure handler answers Git's refusal with `git rebase --abort` in the
same directory (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:200-206`), so an unguarded run that meets a foreign
rebase there **aborts it**; blocking before `git rebase` is the only place that can be stopped
(§5.4 consequence 7, §11, §12). **And plan-only says why, not that**: the document's job in this
cell is to tell the operator, before the fact, that the next rebase in that directory will fail,
which directory it is, and — on pass 2 — what the failure handler would then do to whatever is
already there, which is precisely what no shipped external surface does today.

**8.6.3 A refusal document is still a document — and a workless or limitless one still has no
token.**
`plan-unavailable`, `stack-unsortable` and `selection-refused` produce
a document with the head fields, `runnable: false`, `refusal.*` populated, `entries: []`,
`push.targets: []`, `restore.applies: false` and
**`approval.fingerprint: null` — always, not "where the inputs allowed it"**. The rule is the
usable-token predicate of §4.4, and it has **three** clauses: the *work* clause — `entries` empty,
`push.targets` empty **and** no restoring mutation —, the *limit* clause, at least one effective
`guard.limits` value, and the *encoding* clause, `encoding_issues == []` (round-28 items 4 and 6).
These three kinds fail the first. That covers
the other workless cells
too: a `state-refused`
`nothing to continue`, a continuation whose remaining rebase, push and restore work are all empty,
and a
stack with no entries all
behave identically here. **The two rows-less cells the work clause deliberately does not cover** are
a
push-stage continuation, whose `push.targets[]` is non-empty, and a checkout resume at
`stage: restoring`, whose `restore.applies` is `true`: each publishes a real token
over the work it really performs (§4.4, §8.6.4a) **when a limit is in force**, because there is work
left to authorise and something to guard it with. **A *fresh* checkout run over an empty plan is
not one of them**: it returns at `len(plan) == 0` after releasing the lock, writing no transaction
and performing no restoration (`internal/checkout_sync.go:651-654`), so its `restore.applies` is
`false` and it is an ordinary workless document with no token — the correction this round makes to
the previous draft's "every fresh checkout run restores" reading (§4.4 `restore`, §8.6.4a).

**Which aggregate profile such a document takes is not left to the implementation**: it is
`summary.plannability` and the two-column table of §4.4, and this section adds nothing to it. **One
field crosses both columns unchanged and is called out here because it is easy to zero by
accident**: `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` is derived from the step 2 snapshot, which is taken
*before* the stack load and *before* the sort, so a `plan-unavailable`, `stack-unsortable` or
`selection-refused` document publishes **whichever of `live-owner-concurrency` and
`owner-artefact-undecodable` those snapshot facts imply — either, both (sorted), or neither** — and
`[]` only when neither holds; never `[]` merely because no plan was
derived (§8.6.1 cause 3 and step 2a, §4.4 profile table). **On the `plannability: empty` column the
same array can carry two further members, and the rule there is membership rather than a snapshot
pair** (round-26 item 1): the fetch-decided `fetch-submodule-reach-indeterminate` (rank 5.05) and
`fetch-local-branch-checked-out` (rank 5.06) are established from a resolved fetch context, which
the checkout `--fetch` route has before its empty-plan return, so an empty document on that route
publishes them exactly as a rows-bearing one would. The three refusal kinds of *this* paragraph
never do — their refusal precedes the fetch step, so suppression cause 2 applies, no context is
resolved and nothing about a fetch was decided — and `fetch-context-indeterminate` is unreachable on
either rows-less column, which keeps the array's domain at **five** here as everywhere
(§4.4 profile table, §4.9 ranks 5.05/5.06, §8.6.1 causes 5 and 6,
§15.18b b2 (v3)/(v4)). **The two round-27 kinds are not members of this array on any profile**
(round-28 item 6): `invalid-git-config` (5.07) and `identity-not-utf8` (5.08) already set
`runnable: false` on both routes, so they have nothing for this axis to express and a rows-less
document that carries either still publishes `guard.execute_blocked_by: []` for that reason. **The round-20 phrasing
"publishes `["live-owner-concurrency"]` exactly when a pre-existing signalable foreign owner was
observed, and `[]` otherwise" is withdrawn as a biconditional that silently excluded the array's
second member** (round-21 item 3): an undecodable owner artefact blocks controlled execution on
exactly the same footing, on this profile as on any other, and a rows-less document that published
`[]` beside a symlinked `.sync-run.lock` would assert "the guarded twin will not refuse for
ownership" from evidence it never gathered. Its `refusal.kind` stays the rank 1-3 kind above; the
concurrency fact is a separate axis and does not compete with it. The
three kinds above are `plannability: unavailable` — the candidate and collateral aggregates are
`null`, the count-of-published-rows fields are `0`, `summary.collateral_bound` is `null`, and
`repositories[]` is **`[]`** unless something in the document **cites** an established context —
the four citers of §4.4's emission rule (an entry's `base_context`, an entry's `execution_context`,
a `push.targets[].context_id`, or a restore context if one is ever published), round-36 item 5.
Merely having *resolved* a directory is not enough: checkout's `ws.RepoRoot` is a §8.6.6 hard
precondition and is therefore always resolvable on that route, yet a rows-less refusal with no push
target cites it from nowhere and publishes `[]`; an external `plan-unavailable` document has no
stack, no worktree and no `entry.Repo`, so it carries `[]` for the stronger reason that no context
was ever established. A rows-less document that is *not* a refusal —
an empty stack, an empty remaining set (§8.6.4a) — is `plannability: empty` instead: its aggregates
are real zeros and empty sets, and `runnable` is **`true` only when no independent non-waivable
rank 3, rank 4, rank 4.5, rank 5.05, rank 5.06, rank 5.07, conditional rank 5.08 or (under the
blocking rendering) rank 6 fact applies**, because `tws sync <f>` over
an empty
stack succeeds today and a document that called it unrunnable would describe a different command.
**The qualification is not decoration.** The same empty document is `runnable: false` whenever such
a fact really is present — a rank 3 `state-refused` dirty tree, detached HEAD, in-progress Git
operation, live guard or continuation gate; a rank 4 `preflight-refused` I19 containment failure
or, on a push-stage cell, the projected completion gate of §8.6.4a; a rank 4.5 `restore-blocked`
fact on a checkout resume whose restore is the whole remaining work (§4.4, §4.9); **any of the four
rows-less rank-5 members — 5.05 and 5.06 from the checkout `--fetch` route's single resolved
context, 5.07 from any probed repository context whose invalid value this route will really hand to
Git, and 5.08 only where this rows-less document would otherwise mint a token** (round-28 item 6,
§4.9, §4.4 profile table); and, under
the blocking rendering, a rank 6 `selection-hazard` carried by a selection whose remaining rows are
empty — because that empty run really would refuse. **A rows-less document that publishes
`encoding_issues[]` without minting is *not* one of them**: it keeps `runnable: true` and carries no
rank 5.08 blocker (round-28 item 4). **`refusal.kind` is total over that set, and
over one more that `runnable` deliberately excludes** (round-19 item 6, extended by round-20
item 5): whichever of those facts made `runnable` false is the kind the document publishes, rank
4.5 `restore-blocked` included, **and where none of them applies while the document nevertheless
carries approvable work — a non-empty `push.targets[]` or `restore.applies: true` — the guard
verdicts of ranks 7, 7.5 and 8 are reachable here exactly as they are with rows, and whichever of them
ranks highest is the document's `refusal.kind` on a `runnable: true` document**. That is not an
exception to `runnable`; it is the standing separation of the two axes (§4.9): ranks 7-12 are
verdicts about *this invocation's* limits, token and evaluability, never about whether the plan can
execute. The reachable cells are the ones the work-and-limit predicate already admits — a
push-stage continuation and a checkout `restoring` resume both mint real tokens and are both
evaluated against effective limits (§4.4 usable-token rule, §8.6.4a) — so a
`guard-limit-mismatch` (rank 7) on such a resume, an `approval-without-limits` (7.5) and an
`approval-mismatch` (8) against its real token
are each the published refusal of a rows-less document whose `runnable` stays `true`; rank 9
`revalidation-mismatch` belongs to the same set but is reachable only at the **guarded** seam, which
emits a marker line and no document (§8.7.6), so it is the refusal *kind* of that rows-less
invocation rather than a field of a published one. **Ranks 10, 11 and 12 are not reachable on this
profile, and the round-20 `indeterminate-entry`/`limit-total` cells are withdrawn** (round-21
item 4): the profile's own evaluation set is a single `total` row with `value: 0` and
`verdict: within-limit` under `max_replay_total`, and **no** row under `max_replay_per_entry`
(§4.4 profile table, §8.3.2a), so nothing is `unknown` for rank 10 to refuse on, no entry exists for
rank 11 to exceed, and `0` exceeds no non-negative total for rank 12. The remaining push or restore
work these cells describe is not replay work and never enters a replay limit — publishing
`limit-total` over it would refuse a resume against a number that measures something else. **No
rows-less document ever pairs `runnable: false` with `refusal.kind: null`, and none publishes a
`runnable: false` for a rank 7-12 verdict**: the first direction is the round-19 totality fix, the
second is the invariant that keeps `runnable` a statement about the *plan* and not about the
invocation's flags. The
ordinary **workless** rows-less document reaches none of ranks 7-12: with no work it mints no token, so
rank 8 has no object (§4.9), and with no rows and no remaining replay there is nothing for a
per-entry limit to exceed — `limit-per-entry` (rank 11) is unreachable on **every** rows-less cell,
workless or workful, exactly as `indeterminate-entry` (10) and `limit-total` (12) are. **The wrong-branch worktree preflight is not in
that set**: it is an external per-entry fact raised over a row (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:111-116`),
so it cannot exist on a document with no rows, and the previous round's inclusion of it here and in
§4.4's profile table is withdrawn. **Rank 5 is *almost* not among them either, and the rows-less rank-5 set is exactly `{5.05, 5.06, 5.07, conditional 5.08}`** (round-23 item 3, round-25 item 2, round-26 item 1, round-27 items 3 and 7, round-28 item 6; the earlier "two exceptions, not one" count is **withdrawn**, and every restatement of the set — here, in §4.4's profile table, in §8.6.3 and in §15.18b — carries all four members with 5.08's condition attached): its row members
need a row and its document-level 5.0 member needs a multi-candidate fetch token, which needs
selected entries that would themselves be rows, so the previous round's `fetch-context-indeterminate`
cell on this profile is withdrawn as unreachable (§4.4, §15.18b b2) — **but rank 5.05
`fetch-submodule-reach-indeterminate`, rank 5.06 `fetch-local-branch-checked-out`, rank 5.07
`invalid-git-config` and, only where this rows-less document would otherwise mint a token, rank 5.08
`identity-not-utf8` *are* reachable here**. The first two reach it on exactly one
route: checkout's single `workspace-repo-root` context is resolved and its fetch decided **before**
the stack load and the `len(plan) == 0` return (`internal/checkout_sync.go:611-654`), so an empty
checkout `--fetch` document over a superproject with unconditional, unbounded submodule recursion
publishes a rows-less `plannability: empty` document with that blocker, `runnable: false`,
`fetch.outcome: skipped` and `freshness: not-refreshed-submodule-reach-indeterminate`, and the same
empty document over a context whose positive refspec covers `refs/heads/**` while a worktree of that
store holds a covered branch publishes the 5.06 blocker with `runnable: false`,
`fetch.outcome: skipped` and `freshness: not-refreshed-local-branch-checked-out`. Each is a
document-level fact about a fetch context rather than about a row, which is precisely why it can
exist where no row does; each also publishes its own `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` member on that
cell (§4.4 profile table); the external zero-context cell cannot reach either, having no context at all
(§4.4 profile table, §8.6.1 causes 5 and 6, §15.18b b2 (v3)/(v4)). **5.07 reaches this profile on
both modes and needs no fetch at all** (round-29 item 1): a rows-less push-stage continuation and a
rows-less `restoring` resume run `git push` and `git checkout` respectively, so an invalid
`submodule.recurse` in the probed context blocks them, `runnable` is `false`, and the same document
over an invalid *rebase-scope* key stays `runnable: true` because no `git rebase` will run.
**5.08 reaches it only on the conditional cell round 28 states** — where the rows-less document
would otherwise mint a token — and a rows-less document that merely publishes `encoding_issues[]`
without minting keeps `runnable: true` (round-28 item 4). The
earlier "`runnable` stays `true`" reading of this section is **withdrawn** too: it contradicted §4.4's
own profile table, whose `refusal.kind` row always admitted an independent fact, and it
would have told an operator with a dirty tree that a run which exits 1 was runnable. §4.4 states the
rule; §15.18b asserts both halves.

The document
is complete because everything it can say, it said; the token is null because there is **no
approvable plan** to bind, and a token over "no rows" would authorise nothing while looking like an
authorisation. `approval.scope` and `approval.covers` are still published (scope from the
invocation, `covers` with empty lists, `hard_blockers_waived: false`, `requires_limits` set from
this invocation's resolved limits, `has_work: false` — the clause this document fails — and
`encoding_safe` from its own `encoding_issues[]`), and so is `approval.usable: false`, so the object
shape stays total and the `null` cause is readable **from the quadruple rather than by elimination**
(round-30 item 4). Supplying `--approve-plan` against such a document yields
`approval.supplied: true`,
`approval.accepted: false` and a `refusal.kind` that stays the document's **own** top-ranked kind
(§4.9). The fetch block is total here too, and it **defers to §8.6.1's suppression precedence rather than
naming one cause** (round-20 item 4): the three kinds above are all established **before** the
fetch step on **every** route — the plan sorts before it fetches (§8.6.1) — so they publish
`fetch.attempted: false` and `fetch.outcome: skipped` without exception, while `freshness` is
whichever suppression cause **outranks** the others in that invocation. On a fresh invocation that
is `not-refreshed-no-plan-subject`; on a **`--continue`** whose stack cannot be read, sorted or
selected it is **`not-refreshed-continuation`**, because continuation outranks no-plan-subject in
the fixed order continuation → no-plan-subject → live-run → context-indeterminate →
**submodule-reach-indeterminate** → **local-branch-checked-out** → no-fetch-targets → policy — the
full ladder of §8.6.1, restated here in the same words rather than in the stale five-rung form this
paragraph carried through round 24 (round-25 item 7) — and because that cause is the executor's own
behaviour rather than this route's precaution (§8.6.1 step 6, §4.4 profile table). **Two of those
rungs are reachable on this very profile**, on the checkout `--fetch` route whose one context is
decided before the empty-plan return: rank 5.05's `not-refreshed-submodule-reach-indeterminate` and
rank 5.06's `not-refreshed-local-branch-checked-out` (§4.4 profile table, §15.18b b2 (v3)/(v4)). The previous draft's "with no route-dependent
exception" wording read as "always `not-refreshed-no-plan-subject`", which contradicted §8.6.1's
precedence and §4.4's profile table alike, and is **withdrawn**: the route-independent claim is
about `attempted`/`outcome`, never about `freshness` (§8.6.1, §5.5, §15.15g). In the human
rendering the final line is `Approval fingerprint: none` (§8.3.5) — the literal `none`, never a
blank line and never an omitted line, so `tail -1` has a defined answer on every document.

**The limit clause produces the same `none` on a document that is anything but empty**, and that is
deliberate. A plain `tws sync <f> --plan` with no limit flag describes the whole run — rows,
candidate counts, collateral, blockers, fetch, `state` — and is the ordinary way to look at a stack;
it publishes `approval.fingerprint: null`, `approval.usable: false`,
`approval.covers.requires_limits: true` and the `Approval fingerprint: none` line, because
`--approve-plan` requires an effective limit (§8.5.1) and a token no invocation could ever supply
would be a receipt for nothing. Nothing else about the document is weakened, no blocker is added, and
`runnable` is untouched. The operator who wants a token re-runs the same plan with the limits they
intend to guard with, and gets one over the identical work. Every
other blocker kind produces a full document with rows and — **under an effective limit** — a real
64-hex token.

**8.6.4 Continuation: every gate is projected, and the route comes from the state.**
`--plan --continue` inspects whichever continuation state exists (v2 payload, legacy
`.sync-state.yaml`, checkout transaction), publishes the **state-derived** effective route and
policy (§0.2, plus `requested_route` when the command line asked for another), and describes the
*remaining* entries.

The previous draft projected only "nothing to continue" and "rebase in progress". That was
incomplete: every gate a resume can fail is a fact the operator needs *before* resuming, and
inheriting any of them as an early return would make `--plan` refuse instead of describe. The
complete set, each rendered as a `blockers[]` row with `runnable: false`,
`refusal.kind = state-refused` and the **exact shipped sentence** in `detail`, in a document that
exits 0:

| Continuation gate | Shipped literal (verbatim in `detail`) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| axis mismatch (external v2) | `cannot change %s on --continue: the run was started with %s=%s and this invocation requests %s` | `syncContinueMismatches`/`syncContinueMismatch`, `internal/cli/sync.go:435-460` |
| axis mismatch (checkout v2) | same sentence | `checkoutContinueMismatches`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:767-793` |
| nothing to continue (legacy) | `nothing to continue — no sync in progress` | `handleSyncContinue`, `internal/cli/sync.go:313-315` |
| nothing to continue (scoped, no payload) | same sentence | `handleScopedSyncContinue`, `:365-367` |
| no transaction (checkout) | `no transaction to continue: %w` | `ContinueCheckoutSync`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:719-721` |
| rebase still active (external) | `rebase still in progress in %s; resolve conflicts, run git add . && git rebase --continue, then retry` | `:317-319`, `:372-375`, evaluated by `isRebaseInProgress(layout.WorktreePath(FailedBranch))` — **that predicate exactly**, see the exactness rule below |
| rebase still active (checkout) | `rebase still in progress; finish resolving conflicts then run --continue again` | `resumeTransaction`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:868-872` |
| failed branch missing from stack | `failed branch %q no longer exists in stack` | `:327-329`, `:388-390` |
| resolved branch does not contain parent | `resolved branch %s still does not contain its configured parent %s` | `:330-332`, `:391-393` |
| post-conflict ancestry (checkout) | `after conflict resolution, %s is not descended from base %s` | `internal/checkout_sync.go:879-881` |
| state/payload unreadable or unsupported version | the cell 3/6/9/12 and cell 10 sentences of `syncCellRefusal` | `internal/cli/sync_modes.go:302-361` |
| transaction version too new | `checkout sync transaction state version %d is newer than %d; upgrade tws or remove %s` | `internal/checkout_sync.go:723-726` |
| selection missing (checkout v2) | `selected stack entry %q no longer exists in stack; use --abort` | `checkoutSelectedStillPresent`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:796-812` |
| selection missing (external v2) | the same sentence, plus any `ResolveSyncSelection` refusal the rebuild raises | `scopedSelectionFromPayload`, `internal/cli/sync.go:481-493`, called at `:381` |
| foreign / unreclaimable guard | `sync guard %s does not belong to the recorded scoped run; inspect it and remove it manually`; `sync guard held by live process %d; cannot reclaim` | `internal/cli/sync.go:397-399`; `ReclaimSyncRunGuard`, `internal/sync_run_state.go:226-228` |
| stack unreadable on resume | `load stack: %w` | `:321-323`, `:377-379` — reported as `plan-unavailable` (§8.5.5), not `state-refused` |
| trigger flags against non-v2 state (I20) | `cannot use sync mode flags on --continue without v2 state; continue without them or abort and start a new run` | `errSyncModeFlagsNeedV2`, `internal/cli/sync_modes.go:24-26` (§8.5.3) |
| **`--push` added to a pre-v2 checkout transaction** | `cannot add --push to an existing transaction that was started without it; persisted push=%v wins` | `ContinueCheckoutSync`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:736` — the only continuation gate that is *about* push intent, and therefore the one a plan describing `intent.push` must project rather than discover at resume time (§3.11, §4.4) |
| **completion gate before the push (external)** | `Sync incomplete; stale stack edges remain:` plus one `  [!] %s does not contain parent %s` line per edge | `staleStackEdgesFiltered` → `syncFailure`, `internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:216-226`, reached on **every** external resume before `pushFeature`/`runNewModePush` runs. It is the one gate in this table that is **not** rank 3: it is a shipped **pre-mutation preflight**, so it ranks 4 (`preflight-refused`) and it is what makes a projected `push.targets[]` non-executable (§4.9, §8.6.4a) |

**The external continuation gate mirrors `isRebaseInProgress`, and that helper has exactly four call sites — both continuation gates and both abort paths.** It is called by legacy `handleSyncContinue` (`internal/cli/sync.go:317`) and scoped `handleScopedSyncContinue` (`:373`), and by the two `--abort` cleanups that answer a live rebase with `git rebase --abort` — the cell-2/5 scoped abort (`:270`) and legacy `handleSyncAbort` (`:302`). It is used **nowhere on a fresh-run path**, and the fresh per-row operation-directory predicate of §4.1 remains a separate question, in a separate directory, computed separately (§4.9 rank 5.45). Both external resumes compute the same thing over the same directory: `failedPath := layout.WorktreePath(state.FailedBranch)`, then `state.FailedBranch != "" && isRebaseInProgress(failedPath)` (`internal/cli/sync.go:316-319` legacy, `:372-375` scoped). This is a **continuation** fact about a **recorded** failed branch; the fresh-run cell is a different question in a different directory with a different predicate, and round-16 separates them completely (§4.1 `context.rebase_in_progress`, §4.9 rank 5.45). The projected fact must be that function, spelled out, because the obvious substitute is wrong in both directions:

```go
func isRebaseInProgress(worktreePath string) bool {
    gitDir := internal.RunSilent("git", "-C", worktreePath, "rev-parse", "--git-dir")
    if gitDir != nil {          // git-dir short-circuit: ANY error ⇒ false
        return false
    }
    err := internal.RunSilent("git", "-C", worktreePath, "rebase", "--show-current-patch")
    return err == nil           // exit status alone; any error ⇒ false
}
```

Three properties are binding on the plan, the guard and their tests:

- **The git-dir short-circuit answers `false`, never “unknown”.** A `FailedBranch` whose worktree has been deleted, pruned, replaced by a plain directory, or whose gitfile dangles, makes `rev-parse --git-dir` fail, so the shipped gate does **not** fire and the resume proceeds to whatever happens next (typically the `failed branch %q no longer exists in stack` or the parent-containment gate). The plan publishes `false` there too. A probe that reported “probe failed” and refused would invent a refusal the executor does not perform.
- **The second command is judged by exit status only, and it is `false`-biased — but not uniformly.** `git rebase --show-current-patch` shows the commit currently being applied, which is `REBASE_HEAD`. On Git 2.55.0 the three stop points do **not** agree, and the round-15 gloss that lumped them together was wrong: a **conflict** stop exits **0** (there is a patch), an interactive **`edit`** stop also exits **0** — the commit just applied is still the current patch, so the gate fires and the resume is refused — and a **`break`** stop exits **non-zero**, because a `break` is not a commit and there is no current patch to show. So the shipped gate fires at a conflict stop and at an `edit` stop, and lets a resume through at a `break` stop even though a `rebase-merge` directory plainly exists. **The plan publishes exactly that, cell for cell**, including the `false` at `break`. Because the mapping is Git's and not tws's, it is pinned by a table-driven case run against the **shipped helper itself** rather than by this prose, so a future Git that changes any cell fails the suite instead of silently desynchronising the plan from the run (§15.20c). This is the one place where mirroring the executor is more important than being right about Git: a stricter predicate would refuse a `--continue` the shipped code accepts, and the test matrix asserts the pair (§15.16d, §15.20c). It is also exactly why the **fresh-run** cell does not reuse this helper — there, the same `false` at a `break` stop would authorise a rebase Git refuses (§4.1).
- **Four predicates, four questions, four directories — and none is ever substituted for another.** Checkout’s continuation gate is `resumeTransaction`’s own `rebase still in progress; finish resolving conflicts then run --continue again` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:868-872`) over `opts.RepoDir`; checkout’s *fresh-run* gate is the four-marker `gitOperationInProgress` (§8.6.2); **this** gate is `isRebaseInProgress` over the recorded failed branch’s worktree; and the external **fresh-run** fact is the `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` operation-directory probe over each row’s own execution directory (§4.1, §4.9 rank 5.45). The document keeps them apart by name, by mode, by route and by citation, and `state.git_op` is **not** consulted on any external route (§4.4).

The fresh external cell is therefore **not** "the same predicate over a different directory": it is a different, stricter, guard-introduced predicate, chosen precisely because `isRebaseInProgress`’s `false` bias is safe for projecting a shipped refusal and unsafe for predicting one (§4.1 `context.rebase_in_progress`, §4.9 rank 5.45, §5.4 consequence 7).

**Guarded execution keeps every one of these as shipped**: same check, same order, same sentence,
exit 1 — the projection is a plan-route rendering of the same fact, never a second implementation of
the gate, and never a softening of it. Where several gates hold, the document lists them all and
§4.9 picks `refusal.kind` (rank 3 for all of them except the stack-load failure, which is rank 1,
and the completion gate, which is rank 4).
The **one gate this feature adds** is not in the table because it is not shipped: a supplied limit
that disagrees with the persisted one is `guard-limit-mismatch` at rank 7, owned by the guard, not
by the resume ladder (§8.7.4).

Three consequences of the state-derived route: `RebaseStrategy.scoped` and the projected argv follow
the **persisted** policy on a v2 continuation (§7.3), so a continuation with no trigger flag still
shows scoped argv when the interrupted run was scoped; `intent.push`, the validation identity and
the effective limits are likewise read out of the state on a v2 route and off the invocation on the
legacy external one (§3.11, §4.4, §8.7.4); and the fingerprint binds that effective
set, so a token minted against a legacy continuation cannot authorise a v2 one (§5.3).

**It does not fetch, on any route or in either mode**, because no shipped continuation executor
does: `handleSyncContinue` (`internal/cli/sync.go:311-360`), `handleScopedSyncContinue` (`:363-431`)
and `ContinueCheckoutSync` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:718-754`) all go from state load and
mismatch checks straight into the rebase loop. So a `--plan --continue` publishes
`fetch.attempted: false`, `fetch.repos: []`, `fetch.outcome: skipped`,
`fetch.mutated_remote_tracking_refs: false` — **whatever `policy.fetch` says**, including a
`policy.fetch = fetch` external continuation. The freshness value is
`not-refreshed-continuation`, never `local-only`: the refs were not refreshed because the executor
never refreshes them on this path, which is a different fact from a policy decision, and reporting
it as a policy decision would misdescribe both. The base SHAs in such a document are as old as the
last successful fetch of the interrupted run.

**8.6.4a `RemainingRebaseEntries`: the exact remaining-work derivation, per route and per stage.**
"the *remaining* entries" was an unstated primitive in every earlier draft, and three different
readings of it were all defensible: the persisted `Pending` list, the persisted selection, or a
recomputation. They disagree in real cells, so the derivation is fixed here as **one shared
function** (§7.3 step 4a) consumed by the plan document, the guard seam, the JIT seams and the
fingerprint tuple (§5.3.2). It is **state-derived, never flag-derived** (§0.2): the effective route
and policy come out of the frozen state on every continuation, and this function is defined over
that state.

**External — legacy `handleSyncContinue` and scoped `handleScopedSyncContinue`.** Both resumes
follow the same shape, and the shipped code is unambiguous:

```
universe := TopoSort(LoadStack(featurePath))          # re-derived NOW, from the current stack.yaml
                                                      #   sync.go:343 (legacy), :411 (scoped)
selected := run.selects(name)                         # scoped: the selection rebuilt from
                                                      #   payload.Selected; legacy: run == nil ⇒ all
done     := set(Completed) ∪ {FailedBranch}           # sync.go:336-342 (legacy), :404-410 (scoped)
remaining := [e ∈ universe | selected(e) ∧ e ∉ done]  # in TopoSort order
```

Four properties of that derivation are load-bearing and each corrects a plausible misreading (a
fifth and sixth, added this round, cover the push projection and the restoring mutation):

- **The universe is the *current* `TopoSort`, not a persisted list.** Both handlers call
  `internal.TopoSort(stack)` on the freshly loaded stack. So an entry added to `stack.yaml` after
  the interruption **is** in the legacy route's remaining set, and is excluded on the scoped route
  only because `payload.Selected` does not name it (`scopedSelectionFromPayload`,
  `internal/cli/sync.go:494-507`).
- **The resolved failed branch is treated as done.** Both handlers insert `FailedBranch` into the
  `done` map after verifying the rebase is no longer in progress and that the branch now contains
  its configured parent. It is therefore **not** in the remaining set, and a plan that listed it
  would show a rebase the resume will not perform.
- **`Pending` is informational and must never be the authority.** The persisted list is read for
  exactly one purpose — `fmt.Printf("Resuming sync with %d pending branch(es)\n", len(state.Pending))`
  (`:347`, `:417`) — and is otherwise unused. It can also be *stale*: `saveIncompleteSync` computes
  it from the `sorted` slice of the failing run (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:265-275`), so it
  predates any stack edit. The document may echo it as an observed state fact; it may not derive
  rows from it.
- **A push-stage interruption yields an empty rebase set and a non-empty push set.** When the rebase
  loop completes,
  `syncWithStackScoped` writes `Completed` = every processed entry and `Pending = nil`
  (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:238-246`) *before* the push runs, so a run interrupted at
  `stage: pushing` (or failing there) resumes with every entry in `done`. `RemainingRebaseEntries`
  is `[]` and the document is `plannability: empty` — **but it is not
  workless**. The remaining work is a push, and the document states it as work rather than as a
  boolean: `intent.push: true` with its `push_source`, and a **projected `push.targets[]`** derived
  by the three rules of §4.4 ("Deriving `push.targets[]`") — for external `scope=all` the legacy
  whole-feature set over every materialized entry of `stack.Branches`, **including local-only
  anchors** and entries this run never selected, because `pushEntries` iterates the stack and skips
  only what has no worktree; for `only`/`subtree` exactly the selected entries recorded in
  `Completed` and not in `payload.Pushed`, which excludes anchors (they never enter `Completed`)
  and non-materialized rows (`pushScoped`'s own archived skip); for checkout every `tx.Plan`
  entry (`internal/checkout_sync.go:1221-1247`). Because that set is non-empty, the document
  publishes a **real `approval.fingerprint`** over it (§4.4) and a supplied `--approve-plan` is
  compared, not ignored — so a guarded push-stage resume can be approved, and a token minted for one
  push set does not authorise another. The rebase limits still evaluate, and evaluate to nothing to
  worry about: one `total` row with `value: 0`, `verdict: within-limit` (§8.3.2a). `--plan` itself
  pushes nothing, here as everywhere (§0.1).
- **On a *fresh* run the same array is a conditional projection, not a report.** At plan time
  `completed` is empty by construction, so deriving targets from it would publish `[]` for every
  fresh `--push` run and hide the entire blast radius the flag creates. The plan therefore projects
  the set the run **would** have after its rebase and validation succeed: the whole materialized
  stack on `scope=all`/legacy, and the selected, materialized, non-anchor, non-blocking rows on a
  scoped run. Rows this document already marks `blocking` are excluded — they will not rebase, so
  `pushScoped` will not push them — while a `scope=all` row's archival status alone decides its
  membership, exactly as the shipped loop does. The conditionality is published, not implied: it is
  what `push.executable`/`push.blocked_by[]` qualify (§4.4).
- **But an external push-only resume is gated, and the plan projects the gate rather than the
  push alone.** Neither external resume reaches its push directly: both re-enter
  `syncWithStackFiltered`/`syncWithStackScoped`, and that function ends with the shipped
  **completion gate** — `staleStackEdgesFiltered(layout.WorktreesRoot, stack, selected)` over every
  selected child whose parent is in the same repo and whose worktree exists, plus, before it, the
  `branchContainsConfiguredParent` check on a recorded `FailedBranch`
  (`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:216-226`, `internal/cli/sync.go:325-334`, `:386-395`). A stale edge
  prints `Sync incomplete; stale stack edges remain:` and returns `syncFailure`, so
  `result.Complete` is false, the caller returns `sync incomplete` at exit 1, and
  `pushFeature`/`runNewModePush` **never runs**. The plan therefore evaluates the same
  `merge-base --is-ancestor` predicate over the same set at plan time and, when it would fail,
  publishes a rank 4 `preflight-refused` blocker carrying the shipped sentence and the offending
  edges, `runnable: false`, and — **as published fields, not as prose a consumer must infer** —
  `push.executable: false` with `push.blocked_by: ["preflight-refused"]` (§4.4). The array itself is
  still populated, because it is the projection of what *would* be
  pushed; what changes is the executability pair beside it. The previous draft said the document
  "states that these targets are not executable on this invocation" without giving that statement a
  field, which left every consumer to re-derive it from `blockers[]` — on the one operation where a
  wrong inference force-pushes branches. Two properties are binding:
  the gate is a **shipped** check, so a guarded refusal here is marker-free by the origin rule
  (§8.7.6); and the plan **never pushes behind the gate's back** — no guarded invocation may skip,
  reorder or pre-empt the completion gate to reach a push the unguarded resume would not perform
  (§15.16l2 vi).

Anchors skipped under `--local-only` stay **in** the remaining set as rows (`run.skipsAnchor`
consumes them inside the loop and marks them done there), published as `skipped-anchor` with
`determinacy: not-applicable`: they are entries the resume will process, and they replay nothing.
The pass-1/pass-2 split of §5.1 applies *within* the remaining set exactly as it does on a fresh
run.

**Checkout — `ContinueCheckoutSync` → `resumeTransaction`.** The universe is `tx.Plan` (already
filtered when it was built), the cursor is `tx.CurrentIndex`, and **`tx.Stage` decides whether the
current index is still owed a rebase**. `CompletedIndices` is informational — it is appended to
alongside every `CurrentIndex++` and is never read back for control flow — so the cursor is the
authority:

| `tx.Stage` | Current index | Later indices | Resume arm, and why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `planned` | **included** | included | `executeTransaction` → `processBranch` re-resolves the base, checks out and rebases this entry (`internal/checkout_sync.go:850-859`, `:1022-1064`) |
| `switched` | **included** | included | `resumeFromSwitched` calls `doRebase` for this entry immediately, bypassing `processBranch`'s re-resolution (`:895-897` → `:933-939`) — and **without any rebase-in-progress precondition**, which is why it needs its own guard seam (§8.7.5) |
| `rebasing` | **included** | included | same arm as `planned`: `executeTransaction` re-runs `processBranch` from the current index |
| `conflict` | **excluded** | included | the entry was already rebased and the conflict resolved by the operator; the resume verifies ancestry, records `PostSHA`, sets `rebased` and continues to validation (`:868-893`; the `switched` arm begins at `:895`). No `git rebase` is issued for it |
| `rebased` | **excluded** | included | `resumeFromRebased` verifies ancestry, validates, advances the cursor (`:941-986`) |
| `validating` | **excluded** | included | `resumeFromValidating` re-runs validation only (`:988-1008`) |
| `restoring` | **none** | **none** | `resumeFromRestoring` restores the original branch and cleans up (`:1010-1018`); every plan entry is done — **the persisted push is dropped, and the restore itself is the remaining, approvable work**, see below |
| `completed` | **none** | **none** | `finalizeCleanup` (`:1237-1253`); the only remaining work is a **push retry** (`:1239-1247`), which the document states through `intent.push` **and** the projected `push.targets[]` — so this stage is rows-less but *not* workless, and it publishes a real approval token (§4.4, §8.6.4a) |

**The `restoring` resume drops the push — and it is not workless, because restoring *is* work.**
`resumeFromRestoring` calls `restoreOriginal` and then `finalizeCleanup`
(`internal/checkout_sync.go:1010-1017`), and `finalizeCleanup` (`:1237-1253`) pushes **only** under
`tx.Stage == StageCompleted && opts.Push` (`:1239-1247`). A resume entered at `restoring` still
carries `Stage: restoring` at that call, so the condition is false: the transaction is deleted, the
lock released, and **the push the interrupted run was asked to perform never happens**. This is a
shipped defect, not a plan decision, so the document mirrors it exactly, and it mirrors it in all
four push fields rather than in two: the stage is rows-less,
`intent.push` stays **`true`** with its `persisted-transaction` source (the run really was asked to
push), `push.targets[]` is **`[]`** — there is no target this resume would push — and the
executability pair is **`push.executable: false`** with
**`push.blocked_by: ["push-dropped-restoring"]`**, accompanied by a `warnings[]` row of the same
kind (§4.4). Publishing `executable: true` beside an empty target list, as a naive reading of "every
gate passed" would, is the one wrong answer available here: it would say *the run reaches its push*
about a run whose push the arm silently discards. `push-dropped-restoring` is deliberately **not** a
blocker and never becomes `refusal.kind`: nothing is refused, the resume performs exactly what the
shipped code performs, and the document's job is to name the loss, not to invent a gate that
stopped it.
**What the previous draft then concluded — that the document is workless and mints no token — is
withdrawn.** The resume is not a no-op: `restoreOriginal` runs `git checkout <tx.OriginalBranch>` in
`opts.RepoDir`, which **switches HEAD in the operator's single physical checkout**, and
`finalizeCleanup` then deletes the transaction and releases the lock. That is mutation, it is the
entire content of the invocation, and calling it "no approvable work" made the one resume that
*only* mutates HEAD the one resume no `--approve-plan` could bind. The document therefore publishes
the plan-level **`restore`** object of §4.4 —
`{applies: true, will_switch_head, target_branch: <tx.OriginalBranch>, target_source: transaction,
target_sha: <its resolved tip>, executable, blocked_by[], deletes_transaction, releases_lock,
push_dropped: true}` — and, because
`restore.applies` is `true`, a **real 64-hex `approval.fingerprint`** — whenever a limit is in force,
the second clause of the usable-token predicate (§4.4) — over a tuple whose `entries[]`
and `push_targets[]` are both empty and whose `restore` identity is not (§4.4, §5.3.2, §8.6.3). A
token minted while the original branch pointed at one commit does not authorise a resume that would
switch to it after someone moved it.

**Restoring work is projected totally, not just named.** `restore.applies: true` says the arm runs;
it does not say the arm succeeds, and on this cell the arm is the *whole* invocation, so the
document publishes the same executability pair the push has (§4.4 `restore.executable`):

| Probe (all in `opts.RepoDir`, all pure reads) | Mirrors | Published when it fails |
|---|---|---|
| does `refs/heads/<target_branch>` resolve? | `gitCheckout(opts.RepoDir, tx.OriginalBranch)`, which dies on a missing branch | `restore-target-missing` |
| does a **foreign** worktree of that context hold the branch — checked out, or mid-rebase/bisect while detached? | the same holder inventory and the same "holds" definition as §5.4.7 / §4.9 rank 5.4, and Git's own refusal (`branch … is already used by worktree at …`) | `restore-target-held` |
| is `target_branch` **absent from `tx.Plan`** *and* is its current tip different from `tx.OriginalHEAD`? | `restoreOriginal`'s own post-checkout check, which runs **only** for a branch that was not in the plan and fails with `original branch %s HEAD changed during transaction (was %s, now %s); manual recovery needed` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:1258-1284`) | `restore-head-moved` |

Any of them makes `restore.executable: false`, populates `restore.blocked_by[]`, and raises the rank
4.5 **`restore-blocked`** blocker with `runnable: false` (§4.9) — because a resume whose *only*
mutation is already known to fail should refuse before it starts, and a fresh run whose restoration
is already known to fail should refuse before it rebases the whole stack and strands the operator
mid-transaction. It also flips `deletes_transaction` and `releases_lock` to **`false`**:
`resumeFromRestoring` returns the moment `restoreOriginal` fails and never reaches `finalizeCleanup`
(`:1010-1017`), so the transaction survives and the lock stays held. The previous draft called those
two members "`finalizeCleanup`'s two unconditional effects" and published them as constants; that is
withdrawn — they are effects **on success**, and reporting "your lock will be released" for an
invocation that leaves it held is exactly the kind of claim §4.2's knowability rules exist to
prevent. The pairing
`intent.push: true` + `push.targets: []` remains exactly the cell that forced the withdrawal of the
`intent.push ⇔ non-empty targets` biconditional (§4.4), and `push_dropped: true` is where the loss
is stated as a fact rather than left to be noticed. Recovering the lost push is **out of
scope** for this feature and is recorded as an explicit follow-up and non-goal (§18.20): correcting
`finalizeCleanup` would change what an existing resume *does*, which is an executor behaviour change
with its own compatibility surface. The plan makes the loss **visible** — a document that said
"this resume will push" would be false, and one that hid `intent.push` would erase the evidence.

**The `completed` stage is the contrasting cell**: there `tx.Stage == StageCompleted`, so
`finalizeCleanup`'s retry really does push every `tx.Plan` entry, the targets are real, and the
document publishes them with a real token.

**One precondition qualifies exactly two of the three "current index included" stages** —
`planned` and `rebasing`, and **not** `switched` — and it is a state gate, not a row fact: the
`StagePlanned, StageRebasing` arm of `resumeTransaction` first checks
`gitRebaseInProgress(opts.RepoDir)`; if a rebase *is* in progress it rewrites
the transaction to `stage: conflict` and refuses with
`rebase in progress; resolve conflicts then --continue` (`internal/checkout_sync.go:911-922`). So
those two stages yield "current index included" **only** when no rebase is live; when one is, the
document publishes the shipped sentence as a `state-refused` blocker (§8.6.4) and the remaining set
is never reached. A plan that reported a rebase row for that cell would describe work the resume
refuses to start. **`switched` is ungated**: its arm goes straight from the stage switch to
`resumeFromSwitched` and thence to `doRebase` (`:895-897`), with no `gitRebaseInProgress` check and
no rewrite to `stage: conflict` before that call — which is precisely why that arm carries its own
JIT guard seam, evaluated between entry load and `doRebase` rather than inherited from a
precondition it does not have (§8.7.5).

**A *fresh* checkout run with a non-empty plan publishes `restore` too, and its target comes from a
probe, not from a
transaction.** A fresh checkout run **whose built plan is non-empty** ends in `restoreOriginal` +
`finalizeCleanup`
(`internal/checkout_sync.go:1204-1234`), so `restore.applies` is `true` on the plan-only and guarded
seams alike — long before any transaction exists to read `OriginalBranch` out of. The planner
therefore **probes the same two facts `RunCheckoutSync` itself captures, at the same point and with
the same commands, before any mutation**: `gitCurrentBranch(opts.RepoDir)` and
`gitResolveRef(opts.RepoDir, "HEAD")` (`:578-586`), which the executor evaluates *after* its
transaction/Git-op/dirty/detached preflight and *before* the lock, the fetch, the plan build and the
first `git checkout`. The document publishes them as `restore.target_branch`/`restore.target_sha`
with `target_source: probed-head`, which is what makes the projection the executor's own input
rather than a guess: the run cannot record a different original branch than the one the plan just
read, unless HEAD moves between the two, and that is exactly what the token exists to catch.

**The non-empty qualification is the correction this round makes, and it is a fact about the shipped
code rather than a policy choice.** `RunCheckoutSync` builds the plan, prints the new-mode no-op
notice, and then returns at

```
if len(plan) == 0 {
    ReleaseCheckoutLock(opts.FeaturePath)
    return nil
}
```

(`internal/checkout_sync.go:651-654`) — **before** `SaveCheckoutTransaction`, before the first
`git checkout`, and therefore before anything that could later need restoring. The run releases the
lock it took, writes **no transaction**, performs **no restoration**, leaves HEAD exactly where it
found it and exits 0. So the empty-plan cell — an empty `stack.yaml`, a selection that legitimately
matches nothing, a `BuildCheckoutPlan` that yields no step for a non-empty stack — publishes
**`restore.applies: false`** with every other member `null`/`false`/`[]`, exactly like external
(§4.4 `restore`, §4.4 profile table). The previous draft's "every fresh checkout run" wording was
wrong in three linked ways and all three are withdrawn together: it claimed a HEAD switch
(`will_switch_head`) for a run that never switches HEAD; it claimed `deletes_transaction`/
`releases_lock` effects of a `finalizeCleanup` that is never called (the lock *is* released, but by
the early return, not by the restoring arm); and — the consequential one — it made
`restore.applies: true` satisfy the *work* clause of the usable-token predicate on a document with
`entries: []` and `push.targets: []`, so an empty fresh checkout plan under an effective limit
minted a **real 64-hex token over no work at all** (§4.4, §8.6.3). **The token follows the actual
work**: that document is the ordinary rows-less workless cell, `approval.fingerprint: null`,
`approval.usable: false`, `approval.covers.has_work: false` with
`approval.covers.requires_limits: false` and `approval.covers.encoding_safe: true` (a limit *is* in
force and the identities are showable — the missing thing is the work, and round-30 item 4 puts that
in a boolean), and `Approval fingerprint: none` on the human final line. The
discriminator is the **built plan**, not the stack file and not `plannability`: the same document is
`plannability: empty` either way, and `restore.applies` is what distinguishes "this run switches
HEAD and puts it back" from "this run does nothing".

**A fresh *non-empty* checkout plan probes exactly as before.** The two probes are unconditional in
the executor — `gitCurrentBranch`/`gitResolveRef` run at `:578-586`, above the lock, the fetch and
the plan build, so the executor itself does not yet know whether the plan will be empty — and the
planner mirrors that: it performs the same two reads in the same context, and simply publishes
`applies: false` (with `target_branch`/`target_sha` still `null`, since an inapplicable restore
publishes no target) when the plan it then builds is empty. Nothing about the non-empty projection,
its `target_source: probed-head` label, its `will_switch_head` derivation or its fingerprint
membership changes.

Three consequences are binding for the non-empty cell, and each is one an "only continuations
restore" reading got wrong:

- **`will_switch_head` is a real question on a fresh run.** It is `true` when the probed branch is
  not where the plan's last entry leaves HEAD — the ordinary case, since checkout walks the plan and
  ends on its last entry — and `false` when the run would end on the original branch anyway. It is
  what distinguishes "this run will put you back" from "this run has nothing to put back". It is
  only ever asked where `applies` is `true`: an empty plan has no last entry, which is the same
  boundary stated from the other side.
- **The restore preconditions are probed identically** (the table above), with one asymmetry:
  `restore-head-moved` is *observable* only on a continuation, where `tx.OriginalHEAD` was recorded
  earlier and can be compared against the branch's current tip. On a fresh run the comparison is
  vacuous — the probe *is* the baseline — but the hazard is not: if the original branch is **not**
  in the plan and **is** inside the projected collateral upper bound (§4.3), an `--update-refs`
  replay may move it and `restoreOriginal` would then fail with the same "HEAD changed during
  transaction" error. The document publishes that as the `restore-head-collateral-risk` **warning**
  (§4.4), never as a blocker: the collateral set is an upper bound, so refusing on it would refuse
  runs that succeed.
- **The token binds it.** `restore` is a fingerprint member (§5.3.2), so a fresh-run token minted
  while HEAD was on `main@<sha1>` does not authorise a run started after the operator switched
  branches or moved that tip — the same protection the `restoring` resume gets, on the run that
  creates the transaction rather than the one that finishes it.

**Fingerprint consequence.** The tuple binds `entries[]` — which on a continuation *is*
`RemainingRebaseEntries`, name-sorted — **`push_targets[]` with their lease baselines, and the
`restore` identity**, and binds no stage, cursor or
`Pending` list (§5.3.2). That
is sufficient because the stage's entire effect is the set(s) it produces and the per-entry facts
derived from them; and it is necessary, because binding the cursor would make two documents over the
same remaining work mint different tokens. Binding the push set is what gives the push-stage cell a
token at all: with `entries[]: []` it is the *whole* remaining work, and two resumes that would push
different branch sets must not share an approval. Binding the `restore` identity is what gives the
`restoring` cell one, where both lists are empty and the HEAD switch is the whole work.

**8.6.5 `--plan --no-fetch` and I14.** I14 exists only on the new-mode route (R8), and `--no-fetch`
is a trigger, so this combination is always a new-mode preview (§5.3). The shipped I14 preflight
returns on the **first** entry
whose base does not resolve locally (`base %q for stack entry %q does not resolve locally; drop
--no-fetch or fetch manually first`). That is right for an executing run and wrong for a plan: the
operator wants *all* affected entries. So on the plan-only route the same probe result is published
per row (`base.ref` unresolvable, `replay.reason = base-ref-missing`, `blocking: true`,
`refusal.kind = base-ref-missing` at document level unless §4.9 ranks another blocker higher), and
the run is reported unrunnable. The
guarded execution route may use the same richer pre-mutation blocker in place of the early return —
it refuses either way, only with a better message. **Ordinary unguarded new-mode behaviour keeps
I14 exactly as shipped**, first-failure message and all; nothing in this feature re-baselines it.

**8.6.6 Hard errors before any document (both modes).** A document has a *subject*: a resolved
workspace, a resolved feature, a usable repository context and a legal flag set. Until all four
exist there is nothing to describe, so these are the **only** non-zero exits of the plan-only route,
and they emit no partial document on stdout (§8.3.5):

| Hard error | Source | Why no document |
|---|---|---|
| `RequireTool("git")` / `RequireWorkspace()` failure | `internal/cli/sync.go:36-41` | there is no workspace to plan in |
| unsafe or malformed feature name, sibling-space ownership guard, absent feature directory | `GuardFeatureName` (external), `RequireFeaturePath` (checkout), `internal/resolve.go:294-303`, `internal/spaces.go:692-704` | the subject of the document does not exist, or naming it would leave the workspace |
| layout / repo-dir resolution failure | `resolveExternalSyncLayout` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:176-221`); `ws.RepoRoot` unusable | every probe in the document is scoped to a path that could not be derived |
| malformed control flags | `resolvePlanGuardOptions`, deciding **exactly** the hard-error cells of the compatibility matrix in §8.5.1 and no others: `--json` without `--plan`; `--abort` with any of `--plan`, either limit or `--approve-plan`; a negative or non-integer limit; an empty `--approve-plan` token; and `--approve-plan` on a **fresh** invocation with no limit flag | the invocation does not name a well-formed question. This row is a *reference* to that table, not a second list: a cell may not be hard here and soft there |
| malformed trigger flags (I1-I8) | `resolveSyncPolicy` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:41-152`) | same, and it runs before the mode dispatch, so both modes reject identically |
| runtime-state path is a symlink | `syncSymlinkError` (`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:295-297`) and the payload-symlink classification (`internal/sync_run_state.go:379-384`) | the security refusal is the answer; reading through the symlink to build a "safe" document would defeat it. **The hard-error condition is the *shipped* one, computed from the shipped classification called with the shipped `AlwaysReadGuard: newMode`** — it is not widened by the plan route's own guard inspector (§8.6.1 step 2a). Where the shipped classifier never looks at the guard (a legacy route with no sentinel and no payload), a guard **symlink** is not a hard error; the inspector records `state.files.external_run_guard.presence: symlink` without following it, and the document is published exactly as the shipped run's own behaviour in that cell allows (§4.4 `state`, §11) |

Everything a plan could still describe after those four exist is **projected**, never inherited:
state cells, transaction, lock and guard facts, I19, dirty/detached/Git-op refusals, per-row
preflights, and every continuation gate of §8.6.4. The rule is one sentence: *once the subject
exists, the plan route reports; it never returns the executor's refusal.*

**8.6.7 Where the plan-only dispatch sits in external mode.** The external arm's ladder lives in
`syncCmd`'s `RunE` (`internal/cli/sync.go:35-125`). The dispatch goes **after the hard checks and
above every state-derived refusal**:

```
RequireTool + RequireWorkspace + resolveSyncPolicy + resolvePlanGuardOptions   (hard, before mode dispatch)
GuardFeatureName(twsRoot, feature)                              (hard: unsafe/foreign feature name)
resolveExternalSyncLayout(ws, twsRoot, feature)                 (hard: layout/paths)
classifySyncState(layout.FeaturePath, newMode)                  (probe runs; I18 symlink refusal stays hard, cells become observation)
>>> plan-only dispatch: project, print the document, exit 0 <<<
deferred I7 (--continue --abort against new-mode state, :90-93) (executing paths only)
--abort → syncCellRefusal → handleSyncAbortCell (:95-101)       (executing paths only)
--continue → syncCellRefusal → I20 → cell 5 / legacy (:102-113) (executing paths only)
syncCellRefusal(plain) + HasSyncState `previous sync incomplete` (:114-120)
runScopedSync / syncFeature → §9 guard seam                     (executing paths only)
```

Reading the ladder position by position:

| Shipped step | Under `--plan` |
|---|---|
| `GuardFeatureName`, `resolveExternalSyncLayout` | **hard**, unchanged: they define the subject (§8.6.6) |
| `classifySyncState` | **run, and consumed as observation**: its cell populates `state.external_cell`, and the plan's own inspectors populate `state.files.external_legacy_state`/`external_payload`/`external_run_guard` beside it (§4.4); its symlink refusals stay hard, because they are security answers, not descriptions. It is called with the **shipped** `AlwaysReadGuard: newMode` and its result is what reaches `syncSymlinkRefusal`/`handlingV2`, unchanged; the `state.files` half of `state` comes from the five separate safe inspectors of §8.6.1 step 2a, which run on **every** route so guard-only residue is never published as `absent`, and which feed no shipped predicate |
| I18 symlinked runtime-state path (`refusing to use %s: runtime state path is a symlink`) | **hard**: it is a security answer, and the classifier deliberately refuses to read through the link, so there is no safe state to describe (§8.6.6) |
| deferred I7 (`--continue --abort` against new-mode state) | projected: `state-refused` with the shipped sentence — `--plan --abort` is refused earlier by the plan-guard resolver anyway (§8.5.1) |
| `syncCellRefusal` for the plain/continue/abort verb | projected: `state-refused` carrying the cell's own sentence verbatim (§8.6.2, §8.6.4) |
| I20 | projected: `state-refused` with `errSyncModeFlagsNeedV2` verbatim (§8.5.3) |
| `HasSyncState` → `previous sync incomplete (failed on: %s); use --continue or --abort` | projected: `state-refused` with that sentence |
| `runScopedSync` / `syncFeature` | never entered; the plan route builds its own projection instead, which is also what keeps `syncFallback` unreachable (§8.5.5) |

The dispatch sits **above** `classifySyncState`'s consumers but **below** the probe itself, because
the document's top-level `state` object *is* that classification. Nothing above the dispatch may be
skipped, and nothing below it may run.

**8.6.8 Where the plan-only dispatch sits in checkout mode.** Checkout's CLI arm has its own ladder
before `internal.RunCheckoutSync` is ever called (`runCheckoutSync`,
`internal/cli/checkout_sync.go:15-68`). The plan-only dispatch goes **after the hard validation and
above the CLI-layer refusals**, in this exact position:

```
RequireWorkspace + resolveSyncPolicy + resolvePlanGuardOptions   (hard; already before mode dispatch)
internal.RequireFeaturePath(feature)                             (hard: unsafe name, sibling space, missing feature)
>>> plan-only dispatch: build and print the document, exit 0 <<<
I19 containment (cwd vs ws.RepoRoot, :22-31)                     (executing paths only)
--abort / --continue dispatch, incl. I20 (:36-57)                (executing paths only)
previous-transaction refusal (HasCheckoutTransaction, :59-62)    (executing paths only)
internal.RunCheckoutSync → its own ladder (§2.2)
```

**Hard — no document, non-zero exit:** the §8.6.6 set, i.e. workspace resolution failure; every
`RequireFeaturePath` error (`validateFeatureName` rejection, the sibling-space ownership guard, an
unresolvable/absent feature directory — `internal/resolve.go:294-303`,
`internal/spaces.go:692-704`); and flag-validation failures from either resolver. There is no
feature to describe in any of those cases, so inventing a document would be inventing a subject.

**Projected as blockers — document produced, `runnable: false`, exit 0:**

| CLI-layer / preflight fact | Source | Plan-only rendering |
|---|---|---|
