**the fingerprint whitelist** — an exhaustive inclusion table with "anything not listed is
excluded, including future fields", `route_triggers[]` dropped in favour of the effective policy,
and an explicit non-member list covering `invocation`, `requested_route`, the push/validation
labels, every guard verdict, blockers/warnings/refusal, `state`/PIDs/timestamps, `fetch.*` and
`summary.*` — which is exactly what lets a `--plan` token equal the guard-seam token (§4.6, §5.3.2,
§15.16f); **the fetch context** — per-fetch rows carrying
`{repo_token, context_root, context_common_dir, context_source, fetch_effect,
context_candidates[], attempted, ok}` — one shape, stated identically in §4.4, §8.6.9 and §15.21
(round-18 item 2) — the first-entry-per-token rule of
`UniqueRepos` mirrored exactly through `fetchQuiet`'s worktree → entry-repo → process-cwd ladder,
`freshness` scoped to those contexts with a `fetch-context-divergent` warning, and unspecified fetch
order never published (§4.4, §8.6.9, §15.15h); and **external pass-2 mutations and preconditions** —
the implicit `git checkout <branch>`, HEAD left on that branch on success *and* after `--abort`, no
`restoreOriginal` in external, published as `mutation.*`; the dirty probe in the row's real context
blocking as `context-dirty` when `rebase.autoStash` is false/unset; `branch-checked-out-elsewhere`
for every `will_switch_head` row; and `rebase.autoStash` joining the per-context config and the
fingerprint (§4.1, §4.3, §5.4.7, §11, §12, §13, §15.8c).

**Settled by round 8, and no longer open:** the **self-vs-foreign checked-out branch
rule** — `branch_checked_out_at` is published for every holder, and blocks only when the holding
worktree differs from the row's own worktree, so HEAD
already on the branch in a pass-2 context or in checkout's `opts.RepoDir` is allowed and the guard
is never stricter than Git; round 9 fixed **how** the two sides are compared (§4.1, §4.9 rank 5.4,
§5.4.7, §15.8c f/f2/f3); the **candidate identity
digest** — `replay.candidate_digest` over the **complete, uncapped, oldest-first** sequence from the
plan object, bound together with `candidate_count`, with `replay.commits` excluded from the tuple so
a cap, a rendering or an omitted list never moves a token while a changed tail always does
(§4.1, §4.5, §4.6, §5.3.2, §13, §15.5a); the **checkout fetch row** — exactly one row,
`repo_token` default, `context_root = ws.RepoRoot/opts.RepoDir`, `context_source:
workspace-repo-root`, mirroring the single `RunSilentDir` call, with `entry.Repo` ignored, no
per-repo rows, `fetch-context-divergent` inapplicable by construction, and legacy checkout fetching
not at all (§4.4, §8.6.9, §15.15h7); **repo-unavailable nullability** — stack- and route-derived
identity and blocker facts preserved, only Git-probe-dependent facts `null`, `head.state: null` with
`reason: repo-unavailable` instead of a fabricated `head-ref-missing`, `cutoff.state` `absent` vs
`null`, canonical sort and fingerprint still possible, and no `repositories[]` row for a `null` root
(§4.1, §4.9 rank 5.1, §5.3.2, §15.9b a2/b/b2, §15.16b e); the **early structural validation** —
`TopoSort`/selection run **before** the route fetch on every route, including legacy external where
the shipped executor sorts later, as a deliberate non-mutating reordering scoped to the plan/guard
seams, making every no-plan-subject document `fetch.attempted: false` +
`not-refreshed-no-plan-subject` and removing the previously-carved-out legacy-external fetch cell,
with no unreachable `freshness` value left (§5.5, §8.6.1, §8.6.3, §15.15g/g3, §15.18a);
**rows-less push-work approvability** — a
push-stage continuation projects canonical `push.targets[]` and publishes a real token, the tuple
binds that set, and a supplied approval is compared rather than ignored (the token rule itself
gained its third clause, `restore.applies == false`, in round 10) (§4.4, §4.9, §5.3.2,
§8.3.5, §8.6.3, §8.6.4a, §11, §15.16h/l/l2, §15.16f d, §15.18b); the **single limits encoding** —
`guard.limits` is a per-key `{value, origin}` object with `{value: null, origin: "none"}` for
absent, and the parallel `guard.limits_source` field is **withdrawn** (§4.4, §8.7.4, §15.16c,
§15.21); **evaluation on rows-less profiles** — one `total`/`value: 0`/`within-limit` row for a
supplied total limit on a `plannability: empty` document, no per-entry rows there, `[]` on every
`unavailable` document, and a push-only document evaluated as the empty rebase it is with its push
intent described separately (§4.4, §8.3.2a, §15.16e g, §15.18b); **zero fetch targets** —
`fetch.outcome: skipped` with `freshness: not-refreshed-no-fetch-targets`, distinct from
local-only/no-plan-subject/live-run/continuation and never reported as `fetched` (§4.4, §8.6.1,
§15.15g2); the **process-cwd fetch disclosure** — a bare external plan can fetch and rewrite
`refs/remotes/**` in the process cwd under the shipped `fetchQuiet` fallback, possibly outside the
workspace, disclosed through `fetch.repos[]`, with every "selected repositories only" claim removed
from the analysis and required to be absent from the docs and skills (§0.1, §8.6.9, §11, §14); the
**`fetch-context-divergent` predicate** — emitted only when entry rows cite the token and the
context matches none of their resolved roots, never on a rows-less document and never for checkout's
single row (§4.4, §8.6.9, §15.15h3′); the **tracked-only external dirty predicate** — Git's real
rebase precondition, untracked-only allowed **as far as `context-dirty` is concerned** (round 17
added a separate rank 5.55 collision fact beside it; **round 18 withdraws that blocker** and leaves
the non-blocking presence pair in its place, without touching this predicate either way), autostash
covering tracked changes only, and checkout
keeping its shipped full-porcelain whole-repo gate as a separate `state.worktree.dirty` fact, with
round 9 fixing the exact argv
(§0.1, §4.1, §4.9 rank 5.5, §5.4.7, §11, §13, §15.8c d/d2/d3/d5/e, §19.18); and the **threshold scope
disclosure** — limits are per invocation and, on a resume, per remaining work, never cumulative
across prior resumes, stated in the flag help, the docs and the skills (§8.3.2, §8.7.4, §14).

**Settled by round 9, and no longer open:** the **conditional emptiness rule** —
`plannability: empty` publishes `runnable: true` **only** when no independent non-waivable
fact applies, and `false` with that fact's own kind when one does (dirty tree, live guard, I19, a
failing push-stage gate), the unconditional wording of §8.6.3 being withdrawn — round 10 narrowed
the reachable set to ranks 3, 4 and 6 and removed the rank 5.0 cell, and round 19 added the rank 4.5
`restore-blocked` cell to both the `runnable` and the `refusal.kind` column
(§4.4, §8.6.3, §15.18b b2); the **limit-origin domain and its fingerprint status** — one published
enum only (`none`/`flags`/`persisted-payload`/`persisted-transaction`/`flags-persisted-continuation`/
`flags-legacy-continuation`), the `persisted`/`supplied`/`null` alternate domain withdrawn, and the
tuple binding each key's effective **`value`** with `origin` an explicit non-member, so two resumes
that guard identically mint one token (§4.4, §5.3.2, §8.7.4, §15.16c c3/c6, §15.16f); the
**push-target implication** — `intent.push: false ⇒ targets == []` only, never the converse, since
all-archived, already-pushed, empty-`tx.Plan` and checkout `restoring` resumes are real
`true`-with-`[]` cells, and the token follows the work (§4.4, §8.6.4a, §15.16l, §15.21); the
**fetch-outcome predicate** — `ok`/`failed`/`partial`/`skipped` defined over the attempted rows,
with `partial` reachable only on a multi-context fetch and never in checkout (§4.4, §15.15c2, §15.21);
the **new-mode fetch-context nondeterminism** — a deterministic sorted `context_candidates[]` per
token, safe collapse when the candidates are equivalent, and otherwise a `null` chosen
context, the rank 5.0 `fetch-context-indeterminate` blocker, an invocation-wide fetch skip with
`freshness: not-refreshed-context-indeterminate`, and the unguarded/legacy/checkout behaviour left
exactly as shipped (round 10 fixed *which* candidates exist and *when* two are equivalent)
(§4.4, §4.7, §4.9, §8.6.1, §8.6.9, §15.15h4′/h4″/h4‴, §18.21); the **exact
tracked-dirty argv** — `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 status --porcelain --untracked-files=no`
(round 10 added `--ignore-submodules=all`), whose
in-memory refresh mirrors rebase on a stat-dirty content-identical file, with the `diff-files`/
`diff-index` "equivalence" withdrawn and forbidden (§4.1, §5.4.7, §11, §13, §15.8c d/d3); the
**self-hold comparison** — the command context stays the cwd/entry repo, while both the holding
worktree and the row's own directory are resolved through `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` and then
canonicalized, making a subdirectory of the row's own worktree *self* (§4.1, §5.4.7, §13,
§15.8c f2/f3); the **checkout `restoring` push loss** — the resume drops the persisted push, so the
document publishes `push.targets: []` and the requested-but-not-effective intent,
with the repair recorded as a follow-up non-goal (round 10 replaced the `null` token there with a
real one over the `restore` object) (§8.6.4a, §18.20, §15.16f e, §15.16l2 vii); the
**external push-only completion gate** — a push-stage resume must pass `staleStackEdgesFiltered`
plus the failed-branch ancestry check before its push, so a failing gate is a rank 4
`preflight-refused` blocker with non-executable targets and no push behind the gate's back
(§4.9 rank 4, §8.6.4a, §15.16l2 vi); and the **candidate stream contract** — the full ordered stream
is consumed to EOF and every SHA hashed, the cap bounding retention only, with the early-close
wording withdrawn (§4.5, §13, §15.5a f, §19.12).

**Settled by this round (round 10), and no longer open:** the **push-target derivation** — three
arm-specific rules read off the shipped loops (`pushEntries` over every materialized entry of
`stack.Branches`, anchors included, archived skipped; `pushScoped` over the selected entries the run
expects to rebase and validate, minus anchors, non-materialized rows and `payload.Pushed`;
`finalizeCleanup` over `tx.Plan` subject to stage, archived and selection), published as a
**projection conditional on the described rebase/validation succeeding** rather than a reading of a
plan-time-empty `completed` list, with the target identities bound into the tuple
(§4.4, §5.3.2, §8.6.4a, §15.16l2 i2/i3); **push executability as fields** — `push.executable` and
`push.blocked_by[]` beside the targets, derived, non-fingerprint, `false` whenever a completion or
state blocker stops the run before its push, with the previous draft's "the document states that
these targets are not executable" prose-only claim withdrawn — and, from round 18, with the array
defined **by kind** rather than by a rank set, so a blocking-configured rank 6
`selection-hazard` is a member too; **round 20 replaced "every kind in `blockers[]`" with the
unreachability predicate** — a kind is a member iff it is effective, unwaived and makes *that*
action unreachable in the controlled invocation — which is what excludes waived limits and
push-after-restore ordering artefacts, **and round 21 removed the stale copy assertion §15.21 still
carried** (§4.4, §8.5.6, §8.6.4a, §15.16l2 vi, §15.18b, §15.21);
**implicit lease facts** — every target carries
`lease: {mode: implicit-remote-tracking, expectation, expected_ref, expected_sha,
expected_sha_freshness}`, the
plan never passes or claims an explicit `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<sha>`, and the tuple binds the
lease **baseline identity plus its `expectation`** while the freshness label stays outside it
(§4.4, §5.3.2, §15.16l2 i4/i4′);
the **checkout restoring mutation** — a plan-level `restore` object
(`applies`/`will_switch_head`/`target_branch`/`target_source`/`target_sha`/`executable`/
`blocked_by`/`deletes_transaction`/`releases_lock`/
`push_dropped`), the token rule restated as **`entries == [] && push.targets == [] &&
restore.applies == false`** — **the *work* clause of the predicate, not the predicate: the limit and
encoding clauses were added by round 12 and round-27 item 7, and the three-clause form of §4.4 is the
one that binds** —, the restore target identity bound into the tuple, and the push loss
recorded as `push_dropped: true` — with `push.executable: false` and
`push.blocked_by: ["push-dropped-restoring"]` beside it — plus the unchanged §18.20 follow-up
(§4.4, §4.9, §5.3.2, §8.6.3, §8.6.4a, §18.20, §15.16f e2, §15.16l/l2 vii, §15.18b); the
**`guard-limit-mismatch` document** — the persisted value and origin stay effective and published,
the attempted value is published in `guard.limit_conflicts[]`, `runnable` stays `true`,
`refusal.kind` is the mismatch, and the minted token binds the **persisted** plan and can never
waive the mismatch (§4.4, §4.9 rank 7, §8.7.4, §15.16c c7); **fetch-context equivalence** — the
material effect of a fetch is the pair `(canonical absolute --git-common-dir, effective bare-fetch
target)`, so candidates collapse
only when both match (the ordinary multi-worktree stack never refuses) and
`fetch-context-indeterminate` ranks for a differing store, a differing remote/refspec effect or an
unresolvable one **among two or more candidates** (round-21 item 7), with
`fetch-context-divergent` moved onto the same key (§4.4, §8.6.9, §15.15h3′ iv/h4′/h4b/h4c/h4″); the
**candidate first-set rule** — minimum graph depth per token, because `TopoSort` is Kahn's algorithm
over a FIFO queue on a forest and therefore emits strict BFS level order, so same-level ties are
real and deeper entries can never be first; the previous "non-ancestor" rule is withdrawn
**[Round 22 narrows this one further and withdraws its "same-level ties are real" half: only the
zero-in-degree root seed is randomized, so the set is one deterministically first entry **per root
component** and same-root ties are not ties at all — item 5]**
(§8.6.9, §15.15h4a); the **enumeration hoist** — candidates are enumerated at §8.6.1 step 5a,
before the fetch, on the plan and guard paths alike, so an indeterminate token refuses before any
network call, with teardown limited to artefacts the refusing invocation created and the divergence
stated as controlled-path-only (§8.6.1, §9, §15.15h4⁗); the **submodule-ignoring dirty argv** —
`GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 status --porcelain --untracked-files=no --ignore-submodules=all` for the
per-row rebase precondition, matching `git rebase`'s own `require_clean_work_tree`, with checkout's
whole-repo gate unchanged (§4.1, §5.4.7, §13, §15.8c d/d4); **holder totality** — a worktree holds a
branch when it has it checked out *or* is mid-rebase/mid-bisect on it
(`rebase-merge/head-name`, `rebase-apply/head-name`, `BISECT_START`), foreign holders block, self
holds never do, and a failed `rev-parse --show-toplevel` on a switching row is a replay-critical
`probe-failed` (§4.1, §4.9 rank 5.4/5.9, §5.4.7, §15.8c f4/f5); **skip-row candidate facts** —
`candidate_count: 0`, `commits: []`, `commits_listed: 0`, `commits_truncated: false` and the
empty-sequence digest are *known* facts published without a probe, while `range`/`upstream_*`/
`first_candidate` stay `null`, so every aggregate derives from the rows and `collateral_exposed`
stays independently computed (§4.1, §4.8, §8.3.2a, §15.10a); the **rows-less freshness precedence** —
§8.6.1's order governs, so a rows-less `--continue` reports `not-refreshed-continuation` and
everything else reports `not-refreshed-no-plan-subject`, replacing §4.4's withdrawn "always"
(§4.4, §8.6.1, §8.6.3, §15.15g) — **restated in full by round-25 item 7, which repaired the
copies of this ladder that still omitted a rung**; the **rank-5 reachability rule** — no rank 5 fact can appear on a
rows-less document, so `plannability: empty` carries ranks 3, 4, 4.5 and (under the blocking rendering) 6
only, and the round-9 `fetch-context-indeterminate` empty cell and its test are withdrawn as
impossible (§4.4, §4.9, §8.6.3, §15.15g2, §15.18b b2) — **narrowed by round-23 item 3, which adds
the first exception: rank 5.05 `fetch-submodule-reach-indeterminate` is document-level, is decided
from the fetch context rather than from a row, and is reachable on a rows-less *checkout* `--fetch`
document whose fetch is decided before the empty-plan return; narrowed again by round-25 item 2,
which adds the second on the same route and at the same point, rank 5.06
`fetch-local-branch-checked-out`; **superseded again by round-27 items 3 and 7 and round-28 item 6,
which bring the rows-less rank-5 set to `{5.05, 5.06, 5.07, conditional 5.08}` — the authoritative
statement — and by round-29 item 1, which makes 5.07 reachable on the fetchless push-stage and
`restoring` cells through `submodule.recurse`**; 5.0 and the row members stay
unreachable, and round-25 item 7 removed the surviving "no rank 5 cell" restatements in §15.18b**; and the **`approval.scope` whitelist
correction** — it is the one `approval.*` field inside the tuple, so the non-member row names
`fingerprint`/`supplied`/`accepted`/`covers` only, and the "`approval.*` in its entirety" wording is
withdrawn (§5.3.2, §19.3).

**Settled by round 11, and no longer open:** the **single work predicate** — a token exists iff
`entries` is non-empty **or** `push.targets` is non-empty **or** `restore.applies` is `true`, stated
in those words in §4.4, §4.9, §5.3.1, §8.3.3, §8.3.5, §8.6.3 and every test, with the two-clause
form withdrawn everywhere (round 12 adds the limit clause beside it, below); the **closed control-flag compatibility matrix** of §8.5.1 as the single
authority for `--plan`/`--json`/limits/`--approve-plan` × `--abort`/`--continue`/`--push`, cited by
§8.6.6, §8.7 and §15.17a rather than restated; **one guard encoding** — `guard_enabled` is removed
from the payload, the transaction, the document and the tests, the presence of a pointer-backed
per-key limit is the only durable "guarded" signal, and `--approve-plan` requires at least one
effective limit (a flag error on a fresh run, rank 7.5 `approval-without-limits` on a resume);
**skip rows are counted, not unknown** — `candidate_count: 0`, `commits: []` and the empty-sequence
digest on every `not-applicable` row, with no `null` assertion anywhere; the **restoring mutation as
first-class work** — `restore` is a top-level object with `target_source`, `executable` and
`blocked_by[]`, its `deletes_transaction`/`releases_lock` are on-success effects, its three blocked
cells are probed (`restore-target-missing`, `restore-target-held`, `restore-head-moved`) and ranked
4.5 `restore-blocked`, and a **fresh** checkout run projects the same object from a pre-mutation
probe of the branch/HEAD `RunCheckoutSync` itself records; the **restoring push cell stated in
fields** — `push.executable: false` with `push.blocked_by: ["push-dropped-restoring"]` and a warning
of that kind, never a `true` that would claim the gates passed; **implicit-lease semantics** — a
missing remote-tracking ref is `expectation: absent` (the remote ref must not exist), not an
unprotected force, and `expectation` joins the fingerprint beside `expected_sha` (round 19 added
*which* ref that is: the one the remote's own fetch refspecs map the pushed branch to, §4.4); **fetch-context
equivalence over the pair** `(absolute --git-common-dir, effective bare-fetch target)`, with the
absolute path format mandatory so unrelated `.git` strings never collapse; the **hoisted structural
sort on the guarded legacy external route**, now stated identically in §8.6.1, §9 and §15.15g; and
the removal of the **wrong-branch worktree** from the rows-less reachable set, since it needs an
entry row.

**Settled by round 12, and no longer open:** the **live-owner predicate as one
definition with two consequences** — defined once in §8.6.1 cause 3 (an owning PID that answers the
liveness probe, ownership/token/cell irrelevant; rounds 13-14 add the pre-acquisition,
owner-signalling and `presence: readable` conjuncts and restate the probe as *signalable*), suppressing the fetch on the plan-only route while the
document may still project whatever `state-refused` blocker the shipped ladder implies, and becoming
a **non-waivable rank 3 `state-refused` concurrency refusal on the guarded execution route**, so no
guarded run executes on refs it declined to refresh; the unguarded path is unchanged, which makes
this a stated controlled-path safety divergence and means **two** suppressions are now not shared
with the unguarded run (§8.6.1 causes 3/4, §9, §11, §18.5, §15.15f3); **refusal guidance by
mutation state** — pre-mutation plan and guard refusals never suggest `--continue`, while a
JIT/revalidation refusal taken after this invocation rebased an entry or reclaimed an interrupted
run's guard states that the recovery state is preserved and prints the `--plan --continue` →
guarded `--continue` workflow, with the fixed `state-preserved: ` marker-detail token naming the
cell (§12, §8.7.5, §8.7.6, §15.19 c2); the **usable-token predicate** — a token is minted iff
approvable work exists **and** at least one effective limit is in force **and** `encoding_issues` is
empty (the third clause added by round-27 item 7 and given its own field by round-28 item 4), because
`--approve-plan` requires a limit and an unshowable identity cannot be approved, so a limitless plan
is a complete, useful document that deliberately mints none;
the **three** `null` causes are legible from published fields rather than prose — **`approval.usable`**
(`true` iff the fingerprint is non-`null`), **`approval.covers.requires_limits`** (`true` iff neither
`guard.limits` key has an effective value) and the top-level **`encoding_issues[]`** (non-empty iff
clause (c) failed) — with the work cause read off `summary.plannability`/`entries`/`push.targets`/
`restore.applies` — **superseded in shape by round-30 item 4**, which gives clauses (a) and (c) their
own booleans `approval.covers.has_work` and `approval.covers.encoding_safe`, so all three causes are
read from one object and none is inferred from a different field or from an array's length —, and the rank 7.5 `approval-without-limits` cell no longer claims to mint a token
(§4.4, §4.9, §5.3.1, §8.3.3, §8.3.5, §8.5.1, §8.6.3, §8.7.4, §8.7.7, §14, §15.16l/l3, §15.18b e,
§15.21); **`guard.limit_conflicts[]` as the fixed schema** for a rejected limit change — the array of
`{key, effective_value, effective_origin, supplied_value}` sorted by `key`, never per-key fields on
`guard.limits`, and no longer a shape `define` may pick (§4.4, §8.7.4, §19.3); the
**`fetch-context-indeterminate` exits** — non-waivable in v1, with a required detail naming the three
honest options (narrow to a determinate `--only`/`--from` selection; make every candidate resolve the
same `(absolute common dir, effective fetch target)` pair by fixing the workspace, `entry.Repo` or
branch-remote configuration; or deliberately take the **different** `--no-fetch` new-mode route) and
never suggesting a rerun of the same command (§4.9 rank 5.0, §8.6.9, §14, §15.15h4″-g); the **schema
authority relation** — §4.4 is the authoritative, complete field and nullability contract, §8.3.6 is
authoritative for the top-level key set and must equal it, and §4.8 is a deliberate **subset**
covering the unknown-vs-known-empty hazard only, so the previous round's unsatisfiable
"three tables name the same fields" invariant is withdrawn in favour of equality plus containment
(§4.4, §4.8, §8.3.6, §15.21); and the corrected **`saveScopedSyncFailure` citation**
(`internal/cli/sync_modes.go:453-472`, with `syncFailure`/`saveIncompleteSync` at
`internal/cli/sync_helpers.go:256-262`/`:264-281`, §8.7.5).

**Settled by round 13, and no longer open:** the **pre-acquisition state snapshot and
its self-exclusion** — every state fact the plan and the guard evaluate comes from one snapshot taken
**before this invocation creates, acquires or reclaims** any guard, lock, transaction or sentinel,
carried unchanged through plan derivation, blocker projection and the guard seam; the live-owner
fact therefore requires that the artefact be pre-existing in the snapshot, that its PID answer the
liveness probe, and that it not be this
process (round 14 completes the predicate with two further conjuncts — an owner-*signalling*
artefact, and `presence: readable` — and restates "alive" as "signalable"), with `self` published per
owner-signalling artefact
and `state.snapshot: {taken_before_acquisition, self_pid}` published on every
document (the round-13 `self_artefacts[]` member is withdrawn as unobservable, round 14 item 4); "foreign" means a different **process**, never a mismatched token; and the exclusion is
the shipped conjunct (`pid != os.Getpid() && isProcessAlive(pid)`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:281`,
`internal/sync_run_state.go:226`), without which a fresh guarded new-mode external run, a fresh
guarded checkout run, a checkout `--continue` above its forced reclaim and a scoped `--continue`
above `ReclaimSyncRunGuard` would each refuse against themselves (§4.4, §8.6.1 cause 3, §8.7.1,
§8.7.5, §9, §11, §15.15f/f2/f3/f4, §15.19a, §15.20/§15.20b); **the plan predicts *controlled*
execution** — the new `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` array, closed at `live-owner-concurrency`
and `fetch-context-indeterminate` when round 13 introduced it and extended to three members by
round 15's `owner-artefact-undecodable`, never `null`, non-waivable, a fingerprint non-member, published
whether or not the same observation also produced a `blockers[]` row — and with it the single
plan→execute predicate stated identically everywhere,
`runnable && !guard.would_refuse && guard.execute_blocked_by == [] && refusal.kind == null` (plus no
later JIT drift), which eliminates the round-12 counterexample of a `runnable: true`,
`refusal.kind: null` document over a cell the guarded twin refuses; `runnable` keeps its prior
meaning (ranks 1-5 of the shipped ladder, plus rank 6 only under the explicitly selected blocking
rendering of `selection-hazard`; approvals and guard verdicts never move it) and a plan under
a live foreign owner still mints its ordinary token, which authorises nothing there (§4.4, §4.8,
§5.3.1, §5.3.2, §8.3.3, §8.3.5, §8.3.6, §8.6.1 cause 3, §8.7.7, §14, §15.15f2/f3, §15.16j, §15.21);
**fresh checkout restore applicability** — `restore.applies` is `true` on a fresh checkout run only
when the **built plan is non-empty**, because `RunCheckoutSync` returns at `len(plan) == 0` after

"every fresh checkout run" wording is withdrawn (§4.4 `restore`, §4.4 profile table, §8.6.3,
§8.6.4a, §15.16l2 ix, §15.18b); **the nonblocking-order correction** — `TopoSort`'s and

"stable-but-unspecified", and the `fetch-context-indeterminate` refusal is reproducible because it

**Settled by this round (round 22), and no longer open:** the **capability gates behind the fetch
resolution, stated per capability and with no minimum Git assumed** — `fetch.all` is honoured only
from **Git 2.44**; the **sole-configured-remote** step of the single-remote ladder exists only from
**Git 2.37**, added by commit `8a649be7` to `remotes_remote_for_branch`, so round 21's "far longer
than any Git this project supports" is withdrawn as false and below 2.37 an unset branch remote
falls straight to `origin`; `remote.<name>.skipFetchAll`/`skipDefaultUpdate` is ungated 2009-era
configuration. §19.27 now covers **both** gates, `define` answers them **per capability** rather
than once, and **no sentence in this document assumes or implies a minimum supported Git** (§4.4
`fetch.repos[]`, §8.6.9, §13, §15.15h4b2/h4b3 vii, §17, §19.27); the **fetch effect extended with
pruning and tag semantics** — `fetch_effect` is
`{all, contacted, may_delete_refs, may_delete_tags, remotes[]}` and each remote row is
`{name, url_configured, url_effective, refspecs[], prune, prune_tags, tag_opt}`, with `prune`
resolved as `remote.<name>.prune` else `fetch.prune` else `false`, `prune_tags` as
`remote.<name>.pruneTags` else `fetch.pruneTags` else `false` (Git's own per-remote-overrides-global
order), `tag_opt` from `remote.<name>.tagOpt`, and the two deletion facts derived from them — a
fetch **removes** remote-tracking refs and removes local tags, so the effect says so
(round 22's "and clobbers" is corrected by round-23 item 2: an unforced tag update is *rejected*,
and clobbering is the separate `may_clobber_tags`);
every member comes from the **same** ordered `config --list -z` per context, the collapse rule
compares the effect **whole**, and the implicit-lease baseline states plainly that the plan's own
fetch may flip `expectation` from `sha` to `absent` (§4.4 `fetch.repos[]`/`push.targets[].lease`,
§4.7, §8.6.9, §13, §15.15h4b3 vi-b/vi-c/vi-d, §15.21); the **URL-less, `insteadOf` and default-remote
behaviour, stated exactly** — `url.<base>.insteadOf` is part of the resolution and each row
publishes `url_configured` **and** `url_effective`; a `fetch.all` run fetches each remote by
**explicit name**, so a URL-less member may be rewritten into something reachable and succeed, or
fail while the other remotes still move; an explicit `branch.<name>.remote` (name or URL) follows
that same explicit resolution; and a **default** resolution — sole remote or `origin` — that is
invalid contacts **nothing** and exits **0**, which the document models as a *resolved* effect with
`contacted: false`, `ok: true` and the new `freshness: not-refreshed-no-resolved-remote`, never as
`fetched` and never as `fetch_effect: null` (§4.4 `fetch.repos[]`/`freshness`, §8.6.9,
§15.15g3/h4b2/h4b3 vi/vi-a, §15.21, §17); the **`FETCH_HEAD` correction** — it is a **per-worktree**
pseudo-ref in each context's own `$GIT_DIR`, not a common-dir file, so candidate collapse rests only
on the shared `refs/**`, `refs/tags/**` and `objects/` plus equivalent remote effects, and **the
planner never reads `FETCH_HEAD` anywhere**; it stays in §0.1's mutation inventory as a write the
run performs (§0.1, §2.1 step 4, §8.6.9, §13, §15.15h4b3 vi-e, §17); and the **exact reachable
candidate enumeration** — `TopoSort` randomizes **only** its zero-in-degree root seed, children are
appended in `stack.yaml` order and the FIFO queue preserves within-component relative order, so the
candidate set is **one deterministically first token entry per root component** whose subtree holds
selected entries of that token (minimum depth across components, over the run's real
selection/filter/order, deduplicated on the resolved context tuple with the bytewise-least
`first_entry` kept). Same-root siblings and same-root entries under different parents therefore
produce **one** candidate, round 21's minimum-depth rule is withdrawn as over-enumerating, and
rank 5.0 `fetch-context-indeterminate` is reachable **only** where a token spans two or more root
components with materially different effects (§4.4 `fetch.repos[]`, §4.9 rank 5.0, §8.6.1 cause 4,
§8.6.9 consequence 1, §15.15h4a, §17).

entry's worktree), pass 1 with an empty `Repo`, pass 2 and checkout collapse them onto one context —

**Settled by this round (round 31), and no longer open:** **`plan-only` is a projection wrapper, not
a route, and route scope is decided by the described underlying run** (item 1) — the phrase "a
plan-only route that executes nothing" is withdrawn wherever it stood for a scope decision. A key is
in scope exactly when the run this document describes would hand it to Git, i.e. would really
execute the `git fetch`, `git checkout`, `git push` or `git rebase` that reads it; the *only*
out-of-scope cell is a described route that would execute **none** of the four, and `--plan` never
narrows the scope below its guarded twin's, so a plan and the run it authorises parse the same keys
and publish the same `config_issues[]` rows (§4.2 Part 2, §4.9 rank 5.07, §8.7.2);
**`config_issues[]` is unambiguous structured evidence keyed on a stable digest** (item 2) — each row
is closed at **ten** members `{issue_id, repo_root, key, source, route_command, error_kind,
raw_value_present, raw_value_base64, raw_value_sha256, sanitized_value}` **[round 32 makes it eleven
by adding `context_id`, item 1]**. **`issue_id`** is 64
lowercase hex, the SHA-256 of a **length-framed raw tuple** — schema tag, raw context identity, key,
source, route command, a value-presence byte, the raw value bytes and the error kind — so it is
total, byte-stable, disclosure-free, and is the sort key, the de-duplication key and the join key the
blocker's `detail` and the human rendering both quote; round 30's "raw `(repo_root, key, source)`
triple" is withdrawn as a key a reader could not carry, since §11 bars the raw root from any
rendering. `repo_root` becomes the **display** rendering rather than the identity **[round-32
item 1 completes this: the identity and the only join/sort key is `context_id`, and the `issue_id`
pre-image takes it in place of the raw root]**. **`source` is
closed at eight** — Git's own seven `config_scope_name` outputs `system`/`global`/`local`/`worktree`/
**`command`**/`submodule`/`unknown`, verified against Git 2.55.0, plus the non-config `gitmodules` —
so an inherited command-scope occurrence is representable instead of being forced into `unknown`
(its cause corrected by round-32 item 2: it is `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`/
`--config-env` inheritance, not a `-c` tws adds). **The value
members are total**: `raw_value_present` is a never-null boolean and the other three are `null`
exactly when it is `false`, so a **valueless** occurrence (`raw_value_present: false`, all three
`null`) and an **explicitly empty** one (`true`, `""`, the SHA-256 of the empty string, `""`) are two
different published states rather than one. `blockers[].detail` stays a **sanitized string** naming
the `issue_id`, the key and the route command, never overloaded into an object and never requiring a
raw value; the human form points at the id and shows `sanitized_value` only where it is non-`null`
(§4.2 Part 3, §4.4, §4.7, §4.9 rank 5.07, §8.3.5, §11, §14, §15.16e, §15.21, §17);
**parser and row survival are exact, and each issue is one row and one blocker** (item 3) — for the
any-occurrence-fatal callback keys the scan walks Git's **real** parse order, `command` scope
included, and only the **first** occurrence that would make the described command die becomes an
issue, because every later occurrence is never parsed by a command that is already dead; for the
last-effective-value keys — `rebase.backend`'s unknown name, `rebase.abbreviateCommands` and
`rebase.maxLabelLength`, each as §4.2 Part 2 grounds it — an earlier invalid value **overridden by a
later valid one produces no issue at all**, and only the final effective invalid value produces one.
Rows and rank 5.07 blockers are therefore **one-to-one by `issue_id`**, with no orphan in either
direction, and round 30's "two rows where two scopes of one context carry two invalid values of one
key" is withdrawn as a claim about a parse Git never performs (§4.2 Parts 1 and 3, §4.4, §4.9 rank
5.07, §15.16e (v2)/(v3)/(v4)/(v5)/(vi)/(vii)/(vii2), §15.21);
**route-scoped config disclosure is total rather than merely negative** (item 4) — "out-of-scope
values are published" is withdrawn everywhere it survived; a route-irrelevant key is not parsed into
`config_issues[]` and no raw value of it need be revealed anywhere. The four `repositories[].config`
members become closed per-field objects **`{status, value, source}`** over the closed status enum
**`valid`/`absent`/`not-evaluated`/`probe-failed`/`invalid`**, so the four runs behind a `null`

**Settled by this round (round 29), and no longer open:** **`submodule.recurse` has a
multi-command scope, and rank 5.07 follows the commands rather than one label** (item 1) — the key
is read through `git_config_bool` by `git fetch` (`git_fetch_config`), by `git checkout`
(`git_checkout_config` → `git_default_submodule_config`, `builtin/checkout.c:1277-1296`,
`submodule.c:203-212`) and by `git push` (`git_push_config`, `builtin/push.c:519-524`), and dies on
a non-boolean in all three before doing any work, while `git rebase` never reads it at all (all four
facts verified against Git 2.55.0 by running the commands over a `submodule.recurse = bogus`
repository). So the blocker applies wherever the described route will run a fetch, a checkout or a
push — which makes a **checkout `--no-fetch` run**, a **checkout continuation**, a **push-stage
continuation** and a **`restoring` resume** blockable cells they were not under round 28's
fetch-only filing, with the kind appearing in `push.blocked_by[]`/`restore.blocked_by[]` by their
existing membership predicates; `fetch.recurseSubmodules` and the `.gitmodules` context-level
`fetch.recurseSubmodules` stay **fetch-only**, and the §13 budget is unchanged because all three
scopes read occurrences the one ordered `config --list -z` already delivers (§0.1, §4.2 Parts 1-3,
§4.4 `push.blocked_by[]`/`restore.blocked_by[]`, §4.9 rank 5.07, §13, §14,
§15.16e (viii2)/(viii3)(i)/(i2)/(iii), §15.18b b2, item 1);

keys are scoped by it** (item 2) — the merge backend is Git's default since **2.26**
("'git rebase' has learned to use the merge backend … by default", Git 2.26 release notes; the
`git config` manual names the choices but not the default, so the fact is proved against the running
command), so `effective_backend` is `merge`
when the argv carries a merge-forcing option **or** when `rebase.backend` is absent or `merge`, and
`apply` **only** on an exact, case-sensitive configured `apply` with no merge-forcing option;

**Settled by this round (round 28), and no longer open:** **the submodule recursion mode is resolved
the way `cmd_fetch` really resolves it, and the mechanism decides the consequences** — Git reads the
**ordinary config chain first** (`repo_config(the_repository, git_fetch_config, &config)`), then
`--recurse-submodules`, and reaches `.gitmodules` only behind two guards
(`if (config.recurse_submodules != RECURSE_SUBMODULES_OFF)` for the call, and
`rs = … == RECURSE_SUBMODULES_DEFAULT ? &config.recurse_submodules : NULL` for the member), so round
26's "seeded before the config chain overwrites it" is **withdrawn** while the five-rung precedence
it produced is unchanged; the consequence it hid is now stated: an **invalid** `.gitmodules`
`[fetch] recurseSubmodules` value is **ignored** wherever any valid context mode already resolves —
not called at all under `no`, read but never parsed under `yes`/`on-demand`, because
`gitmodules_fetch_config` guards `parse_fetch_recurse_submodules_arg` behind
`if (config->recurse_submodules)` — and is a **hard fetch-config failure**
(`bad fetch.recursesubmodules argument:`) only where the chain and the command line leave the mode
DEFAULT; the file's two rungs are consumed by **two reads at two moments** (rung 2 in `cmd_fetch`
before the walk, rung 4 later through `repo_read_gitmodules` → the submodule-config cache), so round
26's "one read supplies both" is withdrawn as a claim about Git while the plan's own single ordered
probe and the rule that both rungs come from one source are unchanged; and an **index-unmerged**
`.gitmodules` is **not** an unknown mode — `is_gitmodules_unmerged` guards `repo_read_gitmodules`
and not `config_from_gitmodules`, and a failed `:.gitmodules` read falls through to
`HEAD:.gitmodules`, so the ladder is worktree file → index-read failure → `HEAD` blob → nothing and
it **resolves** (§0.1, §4.4, §4.9 rank 5.05, §8.6.1 cause 5, §13, §15.15h4b3 (ε)/(ε2)/(ε3), item 1);
**the invalid-config blocker is route-scoped and its key domain is the one the previewed argv really
parses** — round 27 refused whenever any probed context carried an invalid value of four keys, which
stopped runs that never read the key, so the rule now blocks **fetch-scope** keys
(`fetch.recurseSubmodules`, `submodule.recurse`, `.gitmodules`'s context-level
`fetch.recurseSubmodules`) only where the route will attempt a fetch — never on `--no-fetch`, a
`--continue`, checkout's `no-fetch` default or behind an existing §8.6.1 suppression — and
**rebase-scope** keys only where at least one `git rebase` will run, with `rebase.backend`'s
unknown-name death and the sequencer-only `rebase.abbreviateCommands`/`rebase.maxLabelLength`
narrowed further by the arm's own argv — **two of those assignments are superseded by round 29
(items 1 and 2): `submodule.recurse` is not fetch-only (it blocks wherever the route runs
`git fetch`, `git checkout` or `git push`), and the sequencer keys are scoped by the row's derived
`effective_backend`, whose merge value includes the unset-`rebase.backend` default, not by the argv
alone**; the domain grows from four keys to twelve config keys plus
the one `.gitmodules` key (`rebase.stat`, `autoSquash`, `autoStash`, `updateRefs`,
`rescheduleFailedExec`, `forkPoint`, `rebaseMerges`, `backend`, `abbreviateCommands`,
`maxLabelLength` beside the two fetch keys), each with its exact parser, message and **occurrence
rule** — "any occurrence" for every `repo_config`-callback key and **last occurrence** for the three
Git resolves through the config set, where an earlier invalid value a later valid one overrides is
**not** a blocker; the closure rule is stated (a key the document publishes an effective value for
**and** Git parses fatally on these argv), the general `git_default_config` surface is explicitly
outside v1, and `rebase.instructionFormat`/`rebase.missingCommitsCheck` are named non-members with

`fetch.mutated_remote_tracking_refs`'s `null` clauses are scoped to `attempted: true` rows so a
suppressed fetch is `false` (cause 5 included), `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` is total over the
rows-less profile with `fetch-context-indeterminate` the **only** rows-less-unreachable member —
**a settlement round-26 item 1 carries into §4.4's profile table and §4.9's rank-5 paragraph, both of
which had been left stating the superseded two-member reading** —,
§15.18b's "no rank 5 cell on this profile" claim is withdrawn against the 5.05/5.06 exceptions it
already asserted, and `may_delete_tags` is written as the single predicate
`prune && (prune_tags || a positive destination covering refs/tags/**)` in prose and tests alike
(§4.4, §8.6.1, §8.6.3, §15.15g, §15.18b b2, §17, item 7).

**Settled by round 24, and no longer open:** the **submodule recursion mode is a
last-occurrence resolution, not a key precedence** — `fetch.recurseSubmodules` and
`submodule.recurse` are two names for one field (`builtin/fetch.c` `git_fetch_config` assigns both
into `fetch_config->recurse_submodules` as the ordered config is parsed), so the effective `mode` is
the **last occurrence across both keys** — later line of one file over earlier line of the other,
local over global, worktree over local — with Git's `on-demand` default where neither occurs, and
`mode_source` is the closed enum `fetch.recurseSubmodules`/`submodule.recurse`/`default-on-demand`
naming the **last writing key** — **superseded in round 26 (item 6), which adds
`gitmodules-fetch.recurseSubmodules` and `null`, so the authoritative enum is four values plus
`null`; the three-value form is round 24's history, not a live claim** (§4.4, §15.21, round-29
item 6) —; it is provenance, so it is the one member of the effect **excluded**
from candidate equivalence, and the ordered `config --list -z` the row already issues resolves it at
no extra process cost (§0.1, §4.4, §8.6.9, §13, §15.15h4b3 vi-f (3a), §15.21, §17, item 1);
**submodule reach is a gitlink-and-presence fact, not an activity fact** — `git fetch` recurses into
a populated gitlink on the strength of the index entry, the submodule store and the effective
mode/per-submodule `fetchRecurseSubmodules` alone, with no `is_submodule_active` call on that path
(`submodule.c` `get_fetch_task_from_index` → `fetch_task_create` → `get_fetch_recurse_config`), so
an **inactive but populated** submodule is fetched under `yes` and counts toward `may_recurse`,
`reach`, `submodules[]` and the rank 5.05 refusal exactly as an active one does; `active` remains a
**published informational** member, describing only the unpopulated-but-changed arm that does
consult it (`get_fetch_task_from_changed` → `is_tree_submodule_active`), no predicate reads it, and
no exit anywhere offers deactivation as a way to stop the recursion (§0.1, §4.4, §4.9 rank 5.05,
§8.6.1 cause 5, §8.6.9, §13, §15.15h4b3 vi-f (4a), §15.21, §17, item 2); **both tag members are
refspec-coverage predicates** — an effective prune plus **any positive configured refspec whose
destination pattern covers `refs/tags/**`** deletes local tags with or without `pruneTags` (which is
itself just `TAG_REFSPEC` appended, `builtin/fetch.c` `fetch_one`), a leading `+` on **any**
destination pattern covering `refs/tags/**` — the mirror `+refs/*:refs/*` included — is what
clobbers, `tagOpt` is excluded from both ("we don't care whether `--tags` was specified",
`builtin/fetch.c` `do_fetch`), and the coverage test is stated once (prefix-of/under `refs/tags/`,
non-pattern destinations exact, `^`-negatives contributing nothing) and asserted with a pattern
table (§0.1, §4.4, §14, §15.15h4b3 vi-b, §15.21, §17, item 3); **the suppression arithmetic is five
everywhere it is stated** — §8.6.1's own list, §9 and §18.5 said five while §8.6.1's header,
§10's doc-contract statement, §19's round-8 settled item and §20 still said four, and the empty
checkout `--fetch` cell still carried a two-value freshness list from before
round 23: that cell attempts a real fetch and takes **any of the four attempted-row verdicts**, or,
where a pre-fetch suppression applies to it — cause 5 on that route, causes 1 and 3 as anywhere —
publishes that suppression's value with `attempted: false` (§4.4 profile table, §8.6.1, §9, §10,
§14, §15.15h4b3 vi-f (5), §19, §20, item 4); and **a failed fetch row is not automatically unknown** —
`fetch.mutated_remote_tracking_refs` is `false` for an `ok: false` row whose effect **resolved** with
`contacted: false` and whose reach is `none`/`bounded` with nothing ref-writing, and `null` only for
a **contacted** (possibly mid-transfer) failure or an unknown effect/reach, which aligns §8.6.1's
rule-1 restatement with §4.4's field (§4.4, §8.6.1 table rule 1, §15.15g3a, §17, item 5). **One
non-contractual note is added and marked as such**: reading `$GIT_DIR/remotes/<name>` or
`$GIT_DIR/branches/<name>` makes Git warn that the mechanism is "nominated for removal"
(`remote.c` `warn_about_deprecated_remote_type`) — output the shipped `fetchQuiet` discards — and
`Documentation/BreakingChanges.adoc` lists both for removal in **Git 3.0**, at which point such a
remote stops resolving and that repository lands in the contact-free cell; no field, blocker or test
expectation is conditioned on it (§0.1, item 6).

**Settled by round 23, and no longer open** (three clauses below — the tag preconditions, the
submodule mode/activity rule and the mutation value of a failed row — are corrected or narrowed by
round 24 and are marked inline)**:** the **freshness verdict is total and
ranked, not existential** — over the `attempted: true` rows the value is decided by the first
matching rule and by nothing else: any `ok: false` ⇒ `possibly-stale`; else any `fetch_effect: null`
or `submodule_recursion.reach: unknown` ⇒ the **new** `unknown-fetch-effect`; else any
`contacted: false` ⇒ `not-refreshed-no-resolved-remote`; else `fetched` — so a **mixed** run whose
attempts all succeed while some contact a remote and some contact none publishes
`not-refreshed-no-resolved-remote`, **not** `fetched` and not both, and the suppression ladder
decides only the zero-attempt cells (§4.4 `freshness`, §8.6.1 cells 7-8, §9, §15.15g3, §15.21);
**`fetch.mutated_remote_tracking_refs` is tri-state and effect-derived** — `true` only where an
attempted, successful, **contacted** effect has a ref-writing remote (positive refspec, effective
prune, or tag auto-following/`tags`), `null` where an attempted effect is unknown, where a contacted
fetch then failed, or where a submodule recursion may have written unobservably, and `false` where
nothing was attempted or every attempted effect contacted nothing **— corrected by round-24 item 5:
a row that *failed* while its resolved effect contacted nothing, with no possible recursion, is
`false` too, `null` being for the contacted or unknown case** — with the per-worktree
`FETCH_HEAD` truncation staying in §0.1's inventory rather than being smuggled into this field
(§0.1, §4.4, §15.15g3a, §17); **`remotes[]` under `all: false` holds zero or one row** and
`contacted` means *resolved and non-empty*, never a spelling of unknown, which removes round 22's
self-contradiction between "exactly one row" and cell (iii)'s `remotes: []` (§4.4, §8.6.9, §15.21);
**`url_effective` is nullable and the name fallback is a separate member** — `url_source` is
`config`/`legacy-file`/`insteadOf-rewritten`/`name-verbatim`, and a bare remote *name* never appears
in a URL field, which also aligns §4.4 with §15.21's long-standing assertion (§4.4, §8.6.9, §15.21,
§17); **tag semantics are two facts, not one** — `pruneTags` **deletes** tags the remote no longer
has, an **unforced** tag update is **rejected** ("Since Git version 2.20 … any updates will be
rejected without `+` in the refspec (or `--force`)", `git fetch` manual, verified against 2.55.0),
and only a **forced** tag refspec clobbers, which the effect publishes as `may_clobber_tags` beside
`may_delete_tags` **— both preconditions widened by round-24 item 3 into refspec-*coverage*
predicates: prune plus any positive tag-covering destination deletes (with or without `pruneTags`),
and a `+` on any tag-covering destination clobbers (the mirror `+refs/*:refs/*` included)** (§0.1,
§4.4, §14, §15.15h4b3 vi-b, §17); **submodule recursion is modelled, and
the reach is bounded or refused** — `fetch_effect.submodule_recursion` publishes the effective
`mode` (`fetch.recurseSubmodules` else `submodule.recurse` else Git's default **`on-demand`**, with
per-submodule `fetchRecurseSubmodules` overrides, **the two context keys corrected by round-24
item 1 into one last-occurrence resolution across both, and the round-23 activity gate on the
candidate set removed by round-24 item 2 in favour of gitlink-and-presence**), `may_recurse`, `reach` and a bounded, `path`-sorted
`submodules[]` whose rows carry the submodule's own repo/store/remote facts; an **unconditional
`yes`** over an `unknown` reach **fails closed** — no fetch, rank 5.05
`fetch-submodule-reach-indeterminate`, `runnable: false`,
`freshness: not-refreshed-submodule-reach-indeterminate`, non-waivable — while `on-demand` over an
unknown reach fetches and publishes `unknown-fetch-effect`; it joins the equivalence key, the
freshness table, the mutation field, the probe budget and the tests, and **no text may call the
listed top-level contexts the fetch's full reach** (§0.1, §4.4, §4.7, §4.9 rank 5.05, §8.6.1 cause 5,
§8.6.9, §9, §11, §13, §14, §15.15g3/h4b3 vi-f, §15.21, §17); **the legacy remote files are part of
the resolution** — `$GIT_DIR/remotes/<name>` and `$GIT_DIR/branches/<name>` are consulted by
`remotes_remote_get_1` whenever the config remote has no URL, both feed `insteadOf`, `remotes/`
appends its `Pull:` refspecs to the configured ones and `branches/` synthesises
`refs/heads/<branch>:refs/heads/<name>` — a **local-branch** destination — so each row publishes
`source` (`config`/`legacy-remotes`/`legacy-branches`, naming which source supplied the URL), an unreadable legacy
file makes the effect **unknown** rather than empty, and round 22's contact-free cell is conditioned
on those reads. **The files live in the *common* directory**, being `is_common` members of Git's
`common_list` (`path.c`, verified against 2.55.0), so they cost no process and are shared between
worktrees; what stays per-worktree is which **name** each candidate resolves into them, which is why
the legacy effect is still part of candidate equivalence (§0.1, §4.4, §8.6.9, §13, §14,
§15.15h4b3 vi-g, §17); and **the capability gates are three, not two** — `fetch.pruneTags` (Git
**2.17**), the sole-configured-remote step (2.37) and `fetch.all` (2.44), each answered per
capability by §19.27, with the 2.20 tag-update boundary noted there as a *semantics* boundary rather
than a fourth gate (§4.4, §13, §15.15h4b3 vii, §19.27).

fetch applies **every** matching positive refspec, in configured order, writing each mapped
destination, so no text may call fetch "first-match"; the configured order is preserved because it
*is* the published sequence and because the separate implicit-lease query reads the **first matching
non-negative** refspec off the same list, which is the only first-match rule in this feature (§4.4

**[Round 22 narrows them once more: "two or more possible first contexts" means two or more **root
components**, since only the root seed is randomized — item 5]** — rank 5.0
`fetch-context-indeterminate` fires only where **two or more** possible first contexts of one token
resolve to materially different `(absolute common dir, fetch effect)` pairs, or where one of them
cannot be resolved and therefore cannot be *shown* to agree, so the execution context is genuinely
nondeterministic. A **single** context is determinate however broken it is: a missing, misconfigured
or URL-less remote, or a root that is not a work tree, publishes `context_root`/`context_source`
with `null` for whatever probe failed, **attempts** the fetch and reports `ok: false` /
`fetch.outcome: failed` / `freshness: possibly-stale` — the shipped call ignores that error and
continues, so refusing there would refuse a run the executor performs, and the guidance differs
accordingly (repair the remote, versus narrow the selection). Checkout's single
`workspace-repo-root` candidate therefore can **never** be indeterminate, its row is published in
the full canonical eight-key shape including `fetch_effect`, and an **empty** checkout `--fetch`
plan still fetches — the shipped fetch precedes the stack load and the `len(plan) == 0` return — so
the rows-less profile models a real attempt there rather than `not-refreshed-no-fetch-targets`,
which stays external's zero-context cell (§4.4 `fetch.repos[]`/`freshness`/profile table, §4.9
rank 5.0, §8.6.1 cause 4 and the fifth cell, §8.6.9, §15.15g2/h4b2/h4″-d/h7, §15.21, §17).

`fetch_effect` is `{all, remotes[]}`
**[Round 22 extends the value to `{all, contacted, may_delete_refs, may_delete_tags, remotes[]}` and
each row to `{name, url_configured, url_effective, refspecs[], prune, prune_tags, tag_opt}` — items
2 and 3; its *role* is unchanged]**, with `all` the effective **`fetch.all`** of the context and
`remotes[]` one `{name, url, refspecs[]}` row per remote a bare `git fetch` there would contact:
every configured remote minus those carrying `remote.<name>.skipFetchAll` (or its deprecated
synonym `skipDefaultUpdate`, resolved by Git's last-occurrence rule) when `fetch.all` is true —
**URL-less remotes included, published with `url: null`, since Git attempts them and fails**
(round-21 item 5) — and
otherwise the single-remote ladder round 19 settled, **as round 21 completes it**
(`branch.<name>.remote`, else the sole configured remote, else `origin`, never
`remote.pushDefault`). The rows are canonically **sorted by `name`** while each refspec list keeps
its **configured order**; the whole value — flag, row set, URLs and ordered refspecs, **and, from
round 22, `contacted`, both deletion facts and each row's prune/pruneTags/`tagOpt`** — is what
candidate collapse and `fetch-context-indeterminate` compare, so a context that fetches five
remotes can never collapse onto one that fetches one; and a multi-remote effect adds **no**
per-remote outcome axis, since one context still runs one `git fetch` whose exit status is a single
bit (`ok: false` plus `possibly-stale` on a partial failure, and `fetch.outcome: partial` still
reachable only across rows). The config behind it is read with **one ordered `config --list -z` per
context**, which is the only read that can preserve refspec order and the synonym rule, and is
cheaper than the per-key ladder it replaces (§0.1, §4.4 `fetch.repos[]`, §4.7, §4.9 rank 5.0,
§8.6.1 cause 4, §8.6.9, §13, §15.15h4b/h4b2/h4b3, §15.21); the **independence of the
untracked-presence probe** — it runs on **fresh checkout** rows too, warning-only, because round
18's justification for exempting them was false: the shipped whole-repo gate is
`git status --porcelain`, which honours **`status.showUntrackedFiles`**, so an untracked-only tree
passes it whenever that key is `no` and the run proceeds unannounced. A presence fact may not
depend on a display preference, so `ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` — anchored with
**`git -C <canonical toplevel>`, the one shipped spelling now that the `:(top)` alternative is
withdrawn** — answers the question on every route and from every subdirectory, while checkout's
shipped dirty **blocker** stays exactly where it was as a separate rank 3 `state-refused`
projection, configuration dependence and all (§4.1, §4.4 `warnings[]`, §5.4.7, §13, §14,
§15.8c d5 v2/v3/vi); **fetch refspec order and negative refspecs** — refspec lists are published in
**configured order and never sorted** — **because the configured sequence is itself the fact the
row publishes and because the lease query reads it in order, not because a fetch stops at its first
match: a fetch applies every matching positive refspec (round-21 item 6)** —; the implicit
`--force-with-lease` baseline is the destination of the **first matching non-negative** refspec,
with `^`-prefixed entries excluded from the mapping (they carry no `<dst>`) though still published
as part of the fetch effect; and a branch a negative refspec excludes from fetching is labelled
`expected_sha_freshness: possibly-stale` **even after a successful fetch**, since no fetch of that
remote updates its baseline. Canonicalization is stated as the general rule it follows from: sets
are sorted, sequences are preserved, and `fetch_effect` is both at once (§4.4

**Settled by round 18, and no longer open:** the **withdrawal of the exact
untracked-overwrite blocker** — round 17's `context.untracked_overwrite_paths[]` and its rank 5.55
`untracked-would-be-overwritten` are **removed, not narrowed**, because the claim underneath them
was false: a static union of the trees an arm would write is not Git's refusal set. Git selects its
writing path at runtime — **up-to-date** (nothing is replayed), **fast-forward** (the ref moves and
*that* tree is checked out) and **sequential replay** (whose first write is onto the `--onto` commit,
so a path created and deleted inside the range never lands) — and decides the refusal in
`unpack_trees` over the entries the checkout actually writes, under `core.ignorecase`,
sparse-checkout patterns and that path's ignore rules, none of which a `diff-tree --diff-filter=A`
name list models; and a **checkout continuation** has no fresh dirty gate at all
(`gitWorkingTreeDirty` is reached only from `RunCheckoutSync`, `internal/checkout_sync.go:570-577`,
never from `ContinueCheckoutSync`, `:718-754`). What ships instead is a **residual fact, published
and not decided**: `context.untracked_present` (boolean) and
`context.overwrite_risk` (`unknown` | `none-known`) on **external** rows and on **checkout
continuation** rows, one `warnings[]` row of kind `untracked-present` when the risk is `unknown`,
**no** blocker, **no** `runnable` consequence, **no** `refusal.kind`, **no** fingerprint membership,
and the explicit statement that **Git may still refuse**. `none-known` is the only direction a
presence probe settles (nothing is there to be overwritten) and is never "safe"; `unknown` is never
"will fail". A **fresh** checkout run is outside the fact's domain because the shipped whole-repo
dirty gate already refuses it for any untracked file at rank 3. The probe shrinks to one
`ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` per execution directory, the two-to-three `diff-tree`
calls per row disappear with the intersection, §13's blanket "no `git log`, no `git diff`, no
`diff-tree`" rule stands unqualified again, and a failed enumeration is an **enrichment** failure
(`null`/`null`, not `probe-failed`). The false pass/fail tests are **deleted** and replaced by
worked cells that demonstrate the undecidability — up-to-date, fast-forward, add-then-delete,
ignored file — plus a real-refusal cell asserting the document **warned and did not promise**. Exact
`read-tree -m -u -n` dry-run simulation is **out of scope for v1** and recorded as a follow-up, not
a residual (§0.1, §4.1, §4.4, §4.8, §4.9, §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.4 consequence 4, §5.4.7, §8.6.2, §11,
§12, §13, §14, §15.8c d5, §15.18b, §17, §18, §19.18, §19.26); the **scope of the plan→execute
predicate** — `runnable && !guard.would_refuse && guard.execute_blocked_by == [] &&
refusal.kind == null` is a biconditional over **admission**, not over Git success: it excludes every
ordinary runtime failure the planner cannot know (replay conflicts, a checkout Git refuses, hooks,
the validation command, a rejected push, the environment), and what the guard guarantees is **plan
identity plus its own declared blockers**. §15.16j's matrix now asserts admission and carries a
positive cell that is admitted and then fails during the rebase, so the exclusion is a test rather
than a sentence (§0.2, §8.6, §14, §15.16j); the **single fetch row shape** — `fetch.repos[]` rows
are `{repo_token, context_root, context_common_dir, context_source, fetch_effect,
context_candidates[], attempted, ok}` and `context_candidates[]` members are
`{context_root, context_common_dir, fetch_effect, context_source, first_entry}` in **§4.4, §8.6.9
and §15.21 alike**, with `fetch_effect` a member of **both** tuples — it must be, since the collapse
rule is defined over each candidate's `(context_common_dir, fetch_effect)` pair — and every
abbreviated citation elsewhere updated to the same keys, so no second schema exists to drift
(§4.4, §8.6.9, §15.21, §17, §19); the **totality of `push.blocked_by[]`** — the array is defined
**by blocker kind, never by a rank set**: every kind present in `blockers[]` that makes the push
unreachable is a member, which now explicitly includes rank 6 `selection-hazard` **when `define`
configures it as blocking** and excludes it under the warning rendering, and which admits future
kinds with no edit. §15.18b asserts the pair in both renderings. **[Round 20 narrows the second
half of this clause: the "every `blockers[]` kind appears in the array whenever `push.executable` is
`false`" structural assertion is withdrawn and replaced by the unreachability predicate and its
per-kind assertions, since a waived limit and a post-push-ordered fact are both in-document facts
that do *not* make the push unreachable — see round 20, item 6; **round 21 deletes that
assertion's last restatement, which had survived in §15.21 — item 1**]** (§4.4, §8.5.6, §15.18b,
§15.21, §19.13); the **fingerprint's remaining ambiguities** — **`replay.reason` is an explicit
whitelist member** (two rows agreeing on `determinacy` and count while disagreeing on the reason are
different work), the `repositories[]` member binds each config fact's **`.value`** and nothing else,
and each **`.source`** is named individually on the explicit non-member list as the descriptive
label it is; `context.untracked_present`/`context.overwrite_risk` are named non-members too, since
binding an ambient scratch file would self-invalidate tokens (§4.4, §5.3.2, §15.16f); and the
**`unreadable_reason` nullability rule** — it is **`null` on every `presence` other than

of the artefact-level triple is ever `null`" is **withdrawn as unimplementable** against the
per-file inspector this document specifies, and §15.20/§15.21 assert the two-part rule in both

**Settled by round 17, and no longer open** (one clause below is withdrawn by round 18 and is marked inline)**:** the **reclaim precheck's return
contract** — `checkSyncRunGuardReclaimable(featurePath, ownerToken string) (syncGuardReclaimCheck,
error)`, where the check carries `{absent, originalBytes, guard}`, performs **exactly one**
`os.ReadFile`, writes nothing, and keeps all five shipped arms (`os.IsNotExist` success,
`read sync guard: %w`, `invalid sync guard %s: %w`, `sync guard is being initialized or is invalid;
retry or inspect %s`, `sync guard held by live process %d; cannot reclaim`) byte-exact.
`ReclaimSyncRunGuard` becomes `MkdirAll` → check → (`absent` ⇒ `writeSyncGuardExclusive`) /
(`removeLockIfUnchanged(path, check.originalBytes)` → `writeSyncGuardExclusive`), with the
`reclaim sync guard: %w` wrapper and the token left in the caller. Round 16's `error`-only shape is
**withdrawn as unsound, not merely as awkward**: it could express neither *which* arm succeeded nor
*over which bytes*, so the caller could only recover both by a **second `os.ReadFile`** — which
loses the absent-vs-stale branch `main` has, and which anchors `removeLockIfUnchanged` to freshly
read bytes, comparing the file against itself, always succeeding, and silently clobbering a guard
another process wrote inside the window. The CAS is now **anchored to the judged bytes** by
construction and the reclaim's read count is unchanged from `main`; `ownerToken` is accepted for
call-shape parity and consulted by **no** arm, which §15 asserts directly. The **same shape is
required of the optional checkout hoist** if `define` takes it —
`checkForceAcquireCheckoutLockReclaimable(featurePath) (checkoutLockReclaimCheck, error)`, one read,
`{absent, originalBytes, info}`, no token — leaving only the *whether* open (§8.7.5 step 1 and step
3, §16, §15.16c e3a, §19.24); the **external untracked-overwrite fact** — **[withdrawn in full by
round 18, item 1: the rank 5.55 blocker, the `context.untracked_overwrite_paths[]` field and the
exactness claim described below are superseded by the non-blocking
`context.untracked_present`/`context.overwrite_risk` pair and the `untracked-present` warning; the
clause is kept as the record of what was claimed and corrected]** — the tracked-dirty
predicate is **unchanged** (`status --porcelain --untracked-files=no --ignore-submodules=all`,
rank 5.5), and the untracked question is asked **separately**, because `require_clean_work_tree`
ignores untracked files while the checkout the arm performs next refuses to clobber them: the plan
enumerates `ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` once per execution directory and intersects it
with the paths the operation **adds** (`diff-tree -r --name-only --diff-filter=A -z`; only an
addition can collide, since a path in the index is tracked) — pass 1 over the **new base** tree plus
the candidate range, pass 2 over the **explicit branch operand's** tree as well — publishing
`context.untracked_overwrite_paths[]` and blocking at the new rank **5.55**
`untracked-would-be-overwritten`, external-only, guard-introduced, non-waivable, never rescued by
`rebase.autoStash` (which is `git stash` without `-u`) and never merged into `context.dirty`.
Untracked files that collide with nothing remain **allowed**, exactly as §5.4.7 already promised;
the predicate fails closed only on a **proven** intersection, a failed probe is rank 5.9
`probe-failed` with the set published as `null` rather than `[]`, and the under-prediction residuals
(add-then-delete inside the range, type changes, case-insensitive filesystems, sparse checkouts) are
**named** rather than rounded up, because over-refusing a run that works is the one direction this

§15.8c d5); the **complete projection of the two native acquisition ladders** —
`ClaimSyncRunGuard` on a fresh new-mode external run and `AcquireCheckoutLock` on a fresh checkout
run are refusal *ladders*, and **every** observable arm (read, decode, `pid <= 0`, live owner, and
each ladder's stale-with-state/stale-with-transaction arm) is a rank 3 `state-refused` projection
carrying the shipped sentence; the claim ladder's two shape differences from the reclaim ladder (no

permitted there, which is what keeps §8.7.5's three-step order scoped to the *scoped continuation*

domain** — the member ranges only over the **controlled-path divergence** cells, i.e. those the

(`.sync-run.lock` under a legacy external route; round 19 removed the impossible

**Settled by this round (round 16), and no longer open:** the **complete `guard.evaluation[]` member
contract** — eight members on every row, all always present, with **`limit` the numeric effective
threshold** (`guard.limits.<key>.value` of the key the row's `id` names, `0` legal, never `null` on
an emitted row, never the `{value, origin}` object) and **`entry` the logical entry name on
`per-entry` rows and `null` on every `total`/`lower-bound` row**, plus the per-member nullability
table (`value` `null` only on an unknown `per-entry` row, `unknown_kind` `null` off `unknown`,
`unknown_entries` non-`null` exactly on `lower-bound`) and a **canonical bytewise `id` sort** whose
ids embed the entry deterministically and are unique by construction, so the array is byte-stable
across processes and `approval.covers.waived_evaluation_ids[]` is a sorted subset of the same key
space (§4.4, §4.7, §8.3.2a, §15.16e h, §15.21); the **separation of the fresh external
rebase-in-progress probe from the continuation gate** — the fresh cell is the
**operation-directory** predicate (`rebase-merge` **or** `rebase-apply` via
`rev-parse --git-path` + `os.Stat`, the shipped `gitRebaseInProgress` shape, `false` on any error),
evaluated over **each row's own execution directory**: the pass-1 worktree **and** the pass-2
`execution_context.repo_root` (round-16's `repo_context.repo_root`, re-spelled by round-35 item 13
after round 34 split the field; the fact is unchanged), so `context.rebase_in_progress` is **no
longer `null` on a pass-2 row**;
it is guard-introduced, `rebase.autoStash` never overrides it, and on pass 2 it is the one blocker
that prevents *destruction* — the shipped failure handler answers Git's refusal with
`git rebase --abort` in that same directory and would abort a **foreign** rebase; the continuation
gate alone mirrors `isRebaseInProgress` verbatim (git-dir short-circuit ⇒ `false`, then
`git rebase --show-current-patch` by exit status alone), and its stop points are **not** uniform on
Git 2.55 — a conflict stop and an **`edit`** stop exit **0** (the gate fires), a **`break`** stop
exits non-zero (the gate does not), which is exactly why the fresh cell cannot reuse it; the round-15
"`edit`/`break` both answer `false`" gloss and the "same predicate over a different directory"
framing are **withdrawn** (§4.1, §4.9 rank 5.45, §5.4 consequences 4 and 7, §8.6.2, §8.6.4, §11,
§12, §13, §15.20c); the **shared native reclaim precheck** — `checkSyncRunGuardReclaimable` is
**extracted verbatim** from `ReclaimSyncRunGuard` (same `os.ReadFile`, `os.IsNotExist`,
`yaml.Unmarshal`, `PID <= 0`, self-conjunct and liveness arms, same four format strings), called by
both the shipped reclaim and the hoisted precheck, with `os.MkdirAll` and the token left in the
caller, so the two cannot drift — **corrected in round 17**: the predicate returns
`(syncGuardReclaimCheck, error)` rather than a bare `error`, and it takes the `ownerToken` (inert,
consulted by no arm) so the two callers share one call shape; the caller keeps `os.MkdirAll` and the

**Settled by this round (round 15), and no longer open:** the **two-layer `state` schema** — the
object is `{snapshot, files, external_cell, worktree, git_op, head}`, with `state.files` closed at
the five **runtime files** (`checkout_transaction`, `checkout_lock`, `external_legacy_state`,
`external_payload`, `external_run_guard`), each carrying
`{applicable, presence, unreadable_reason, …decoded fields}`, and with the `{applicable, presence}`
pair confined to those five, because there is no `Lstat` behind “the tree is dirty” and the round-14
all-members claim could not be implemented; the **composite `state.external_state` path is
withdrawn** — two independent files can be absent, readable, corrupt or symlinked independently, so
one `presence` could never answer for both — and the shipped joint classification moves to
`state.external_cell`, `marker_present` to the legacy row and `payload_version` to the payload row;
`state.snapshot` is **probe metadata only**; `state.worktree`/`state.git_op`/`state.head` are probe
facts carrying `applies` and their own exact members and **no** `presence`; **`unreadable` and
`malformed` are distinguishable** through the closed `unreadable_reason`
(`not-regular-file`/`io-error`/`decode-error`/`empty-document`), which never changes a verdict; and
**every runtime file is read through its own dedicated `Lstat`-first safe inspector**, symlinks
recorded and never followed, regular files decoded once through the shipped loader — **refined in
round 16**: "decoded" means *that artefact's own* loader's rule, not one blanket
version/emptiness rule — with
**`HasCheckoutTransaction` and `ReadCheckoutLock` explicitly barred as plan inspectors**, because
`os.Stat`/`os.ReadFile` follow symlinks and collapse *absent* and *unreadable* into one answer, the
exact conflation the totality triple exists to remove (§0, §4.4, §4.8, §8.3.6, §8.6.1 step 2/2a,
§8.6.7, §14, §15.20, §15.21); the **undecodable-owner oracle** —
`guard.execute_blocked_by[]` is closed at **three** members, gaining
**`owner-artefact-undecodable`** for an owner-signalling artefact whose `presence` is `unreadable`
or `symlink`, non-waivable at rank 3, snapshot-derived, total over `plannability`, published whether
or not the shipped ladder also refuses, and independent of `live-owner-concurrency` (both may appear
together, sorted), so the four-conjunct plan→execute predicate stays **exact** in the one cell where
the plan-only document would otherwise promise a run its guarded twin refuses; the plan-only
rendering may still say the underlying unguarded route ignores the file, and the controlled-execution
block is stated explicitly beside it — **narrowed in round 17**: the member ranges only over the
cells the native acquisition ladders would not already refuse (the symlink-that-decodes cell, and
**applicable** artefacts on paths the running route never consults), because a corrupt or unreadable **regular** guard/lock file
is rejected by `ClaimSyncRunGuard`/`AcquireCheckoutLock` in its own words and is a shipped rank 3
refusal with `execute_blocked_by: []` — (§4.4, §4.9 rank 3, §8.6.1 cause 3/step 2a, §8.6.2, §15.20,
§15.20d, §15.21,
§19.22); the **fresh native read at the scoped-continuation seam** — the pre-acquisition snapshot
supplies every published field, every plan fact and the fingerprint, while
`ReclaimSyncRunGuard`’s **native** conditions are re-evaluated immediately before the seam from a
fresh safe read, still before any acquisition, reclaim or self-written artefact, so an owner that
exited between the snapshot and the seam produces **no fabricated live refusal** and a genuinely
live one still gets the exact shipped marker-free sentence; the plan and limits are then computed or
revalidated and only a passing verdict reaches the reclaim, which stays the first write of the

read is taken through the `checkSyncRunGuardReclaimable` predicate extracted verbatim from

Still genuinely open — each of these is a real choice between shipped-behaviour-compatible options,
not a fact this analysis could have determined. **The numbering is a stable cross-reference anchor,
so a question that later closes keeps its number and is struck through rather than deleted and
renumbered** (round-35 item 12, making explicit what round 34 did to item 3): an entry rendered
**~~struck~~** is a *settled analysis contract* listed here only so `§19.<n>` citations elsewhere
still resolve, and `define` may not treat it as a choice. Among the entries in that state are — **item 3**
(the fingerprint whitelist, the non-member table and the field-id tables, settled at tuple schema
version `0x0004`), the **field-framing half of item 4** (`collateral_exposed` as a plan field, a
fingerprint member and a revalidation input) and **item 2** (the guarded-refusal exit code, closed at
**1** by round-36 item 9) — and the *only* thing still open under item 4 is the
configuration/loudness pair named there:

1. **Where external state is created** relative to the guard on the **new-mode route**: tear down
   after a refusal (smaller change) or move `setupSyncRunState` after the guard (cleaner, larger
   blast radius on the sync-modes contract). Either way the teardown-scope rule of §9 holds — and
   it now has two more cells to cover, both landing *after* this invocation wrote its three
   artefacts and *before* any network call: the hoisted fetch-context enumeration (§8.6.1 step 5a),
   whose `fetch-context-indeterminate` refusal is decided there, and the **live-owner concurrency
   refusal** of §8.6.1 cause 3, decided from the step 2 snapshot. Under either option the
   refusal removes only those artefacts (§9, §12). **Round 13 narrowed what this choice can still
   decide, and it is worth stating so `define` does not re-litigate it.** The *correctness* of the
   live-owner refusal no longer depends on the answer: the snapshot is taken before
   `setupSyncRunState` under both options, so the invocation's own state and guard are excluded
   whether they are written before the seam or after it (§4.4 `state.snapshot`, §8.7.5). What
   remains open is the ordinary trade-off — teardown surface versus a change to the sync-modes
   contract — plus one property the *deferred* option gains for free: with `setupSyncRunState` moved
   below the guard, a fresh new-mode refusal creates nothing to tear down at all. The same reading
   applies to checkout, where `AcquireCheckoutLock` sits above `BuildCheckoutPlan` and therefore
   above the seam: moving it is **not** proposed, because the snapshot already excludes it and the
   lock is what makes the plan build meaningful. The
   legacy route has no such question.
2. **~~Exit code for a guarded execution refusal~~ — closed, not open** (round-36 item 9): the code
   is **1**, and that is binding for this analysis. The "introduce 2 for 'refused by plan guard'"
   option is **withdrawn**: it is a cross-cutting convention change to `Execute()` that no fact in
   this document depends on, every consumer is already told to branch on `runnable`,
   `guard.would_refuse`, `guard.execute_blocked_by[]` and `refusal.kind` and never on the exit
   status (§8.3.5), and a second code would give a guarded refusal a status the shipped executors
   do not use. The plan-only route's 0-on-refusal contract (§8.3.5) is unchanged and was settled
   either way. A `define` that wants a distinct CI code is proposing a **separate** `Execute()`
   convention change, not exercising an option this analysis left open.
3. **~~Fingerprint tuple ratification~~ — closed, not open** (round-34 item 9, §5.3.2, §5.3.2a):
   the whitelist and the tuple encoding are **settled for this analysis**, at tuple schema version
   **`0x0004`** (round-35 items 3 and 5 moved it from `0x0003`; the closure is unchanged — a settled
   contract is amended by the procedure below, not re-opened as a decision). The membership is exhaustive as the tables state it — `approval.fingerprint` vs
   `revalidation.digest` as two different questions,
   `approval.scope` (**the one `approval.*` member**, which is why the non-member row names
   `fingerprint`/`supplied`/`accepted`/`usable`/`covers` and not the object), `head.state`, the

4. **Collateral configuration and loudness** (§4.3) — **and nothing else; the field framing that
   used to share this number is ~~closed~~** (round-34 item 9, restated as a closure rather than a
